abstract.text: To investigate the association between regular black tea consumption and asthma outcomes in children receiving standard asthma therapy.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This prospective cohort study enrolled 200 children aged 5-12 years with physician-diagnosed asthma, of whom 140 completed 24 months of follow-up (70 in the tea group and 70 in the non-tea group). Participants were classified according to habitual black tea consumption into a tea group (≥1cup/day,n=70) and a non-tea group (n = 70). Outcomes included acute asthma exacerbations, emergency department visits, systemic corticosteroid use, Childhood Asthma Control Test (C-ACT) scores, and spirometric parameters. Multivariable Negative Binomial regression was used to model exacerbation rates. Baseline-adjusted linear regression (ANCOVA) was used for continuous end-of-study outcomes (C-ACT, FEV1, FEV1/FVC), and binary logistic regression for binary utilization outcomes, adjusting for age, sex, baseline GINA asthma severity step, baseline medication adherence, environmental tobacco smoke exposure, and baseline outcome values.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Annualized exacerbation rates were significantly lower in tea consumers than non-consumers (0.23±0.48 vs. 0.91±0.82 episodes/year; p < 0.001). In multivariable Negative Binomial regression, tea consumption was associated with a lower incidence rate of exacerbations (Incidence Rate Ratio [IRR] = 0.35; 95% CI, 0.22 to 0.56; p < 0.001). Tea consumption was also associated with lower odds of emergency department visits (aOR = 0.22; 95% CI, 0.09-0.51; p = 0.001) and systemic corticosteroid use (aOR = 0.24; 95% CI, 0.10-0.57; p = 0.001). In baseline-adjusted ANCOVA models, post-study C-ACT score (β=+3.12; 95% CI, +2.35 to +3.89; p < 0.001), post-study FEV1 (β=+4.51%; 95% CI, +2.20 to +6.82%; p<0.001), and FEV1/FVC (β=+3.20%; 95% CI, +1.35 to +5.05%; p=0.001) were significantly higher in the tea group.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Regular black tea consumption was associated with fewer exacerbations, lower asthma-related healthcare utilization, and better asthma control and lung function. The observational design does not establish causality. These findings represent observed cultural habits and do not constitute a clinical recommendation for pediatric caffeine consumption.

articles.title: Military nurses' moral distress during triage in mass casualty incidents: A concept analysis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Moral distress among military nurses during mass casualty incidents (MCIs) triage presents unique ethical challenges due to resource scarcity, dual loyalty, military mission requirements, and high-risk operational environments. Moral distress arises when military nurses cannot act according to their moral judgment, negatively affecting their psychological well-being and mission effectiveness.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: This study analyzed and defined moral distress among military nurses performing triage during MCIs to support recognition of moral distress and better understand the challenges.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This study used Walker and Avant's concept analysis approach. A comprehensive literature search identified nine studies for inclusion.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Five defining attributes were identified: (a) Military nurses perceive a constraint on carrying out the morally appropriate action; (b) Military nurses are conflicted between their duty to the military mission and their obligations to the nursing code of ethics; (c) Military nurses experience ethical tensions related to critical resource levels and the care of enemy combatants; (d) Military nurses experience psychological distress and internal moral tension; and (e) Military nurses experience limited authority and chain-of-command barriers concerning ethical judgment. Consequences spanned psychological effects, professional outcomes, and organizational impacts.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This concept analysis provides a theoretical foundation for future studies related to moral distress of military nurses completing triage during MCIs. This multifaceted phenomenon is distinct from other related concepts and defining attributes. Future studies should focus on instruments to improve training and awareness.

articles.title: Opinion & Special Articles: Mobile Stroke Treatment Unit: A Distinctive Learning Experience in Neurology Residency.

abstract.text: The mobile stroke treatment unit (MSTU) elective offers a novel immersive experience that exposes neurology trainees to acute stroke care in the prehospital setting. Unlike traditional inpatient or emergency department rotations, residents on the MSTU are dispatched to suspected stroke patients and are able to participate in the initial evaluation and treatment of stroke in the field, gaining critical skills that can translate into providing more effective stroke care in the hospital. By working alongside emergency medical services (EMS) personnel, trainees can develop a better understanding and appreciation for prehospital systems of care and socioeconomic factors that influence patient outcomes. Currently, only a few neurology residency programs operate a MSTU at their institution, and even fewer offer a dedicated MSTU rotation. Given the critical role that EMS prehospital response plays in stroke systems of care, providing residents with exposure to an MSTU in residency through a dedicated elective rotation can aid in bridging the gap between theory and practice while enriching their educational experience and improving overall patient care.

articles.title: Prehospital Advanced Airway Management in Traumatic Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Nationwide Cohort Study Using Time-Dependent Propensity Score Sequential Matching.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Traumatic out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (TCA) has extremely poor outcomes, and the benefit of prehospital advanced airway management (AAM) remains uncertain, partly because previous observational studies may have been affected by resuscitation time bias. We examined the association between prehospital AAM and clinical outcomes in adults with TCA using a time-dependent analytic approach.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a nationwide retrospective observational cohort study using the All-Japan Utstein Registry linked with emergency medical services transport records from 2021 to 2023. Adults (≥18 years) with TCA were included. The exposure was successful prehospital AAM, including supraglottic airway placement or endotracheal intubation. The primary outcome was 30-day survival, and the secondary outcome was favorable neurological outcome (Cerebral Performance Category 1-2) at 30 days. We applied time-dependent propensity score sequential matching and estimated corrected risk differences (RDs) using generalized estimating equations with inverse-frequency weighting.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 7,217 patients, 2,653 (36.8%) received prehospital AAM, of whom 2,637 were successfully matched within the analytic cohort. Thirty-day survival was 1.8% in the AAM group and 1.4% among matched controls (corrected RD, 0.6%; 95% confidence interval (CI), -0.1 to 1.2). Favorable neurological outcome occurred in 0.2% and 0.4%, respectively (corrected RD, -0.2%; 95% CI, -0.6 to 0.1). No significant timing-dependent association or prespecified subgroup heterogeneity was observed.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this nationwide cohort study using time-dependent propensity score sequential matching, prehospital AAM was not significantly associated with improved outcomes in adults with TCA.

articles.title: Technology-enhanced training for prehospital mass-casualty incident preparedness: A scoping review.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The use of technology-enhanced training for prehospital mass-casualty incident (MCI) preparedness has expanded rapidly, yet how these technologies function throughout the educational process and how competencies are evaluated remain systematically under-examined. This scoping review, conducted as part of the MCIPHER (Mass-Casualty Incident Prehospital Emergency Response) project, mapped the technological modalities, educational functions, and assessment frameworks used in prehospital disaster training.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Following Arksey and O'Malley's framework with Levac refinements and PRISMA-ScR reporting, we searched seven databases and supplementary sources for English-language studies and protocols (2015-2025) on technology-enhanced prehospital MCI training for healthcare learners and professionals. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data. Descriptive and narrative synthesis included modified Kirkpatrick outcome mapping for completed studies, incorporating L2+ (Applied Learning).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Twenty-eight studies met the inclusion criteria. Virtual reality was the most common modality (43%, n = 12), followed by hybrid approaches (29%, n = 8) and screen-based simulations (21%, n = 6). Synthesis of the interventions revealed three consistent operational patterns: half of the studies (50%, n = 14) utilized dual-purpose platforms for both training delivery and automated assessment; embedded data collection was directly linked to achieving applied learning outcomes; and 75% (n = 21) lacked an explicit training design framework. Two additional patterns-a disconnect between immersion level and evaluation depth, and a tension between technological sophistication and scalability-emerged as areas needing future research. Furthermore, no studies originated from low- or lower-middle-income countries. Using the modified Kirkpatrick framework, 56% (n = 14 of 25 completed studies) demonstrated applied learning through embedded performance metrics. Only one study (4%) evaluated workplace behavior change (L3), and none (0%) assessed organizational impact (L4).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The educational value of technology in prehospital MCI training depends more on integrated performance measurement than on visual fidelity or surface immersion. Future investments should prioritize dual-use platforms with embedded assessment, improve pedagogical reporting transparency, and address geographic disparities in training access.

articles.title: Resuscitation using fresh-frozen plasma is associated with improved contextual fear memory in a non-TBI mouse model of trauma and hemorrhagic shock.
articles.journal_full: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Cognitive dysfunction is a consequence of traumatic injury with lasting impacts. Even without direct brain injury, trauma and hemorrhagic shock (T/HS) can cause malperfusion, inflammation, and neuronal injury. Disruption of the endothelial glycocalyx (eGC), a key regulator of vascular homeostasis, contributes to trauma-induced endotheliopathy and may influence secondary neurologic injury. Prior work demonstrated that fresh-frozen plasma (FFP) resuscitation preserves eGC expression and reduces maladaptive vascular repair in a murine T/HS model. This study evaluates post-injury cognition and FFP protection against cognitive impairment compared with lactated Ringer's (LR).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Male C57BL/6 mice were randomized to sham procedure or T/HS followed by a volume-driven LR or pressure-directed FFP resuscitation approach. T/HS mice underwent laparotomy, femoral artery cannulation, hemorrhagic shock, pseudofractures via bone homogenate injection, and hindlimb muscle crush injuries. Sham mice received laparotomy and femoral artery cutdown. Four days postsurgery, open field testing assessed locomotion, followed by fear conditioning on days 7 to 8 to assess cognition. Brains were collected to analyze hippocampal glycosaminoglycans hyaluronan, heparan sulfate (HS), and chondroitin sulfate (CS).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Open field testing showed intact locomotion at post-injury day 4 in all groups. On day 8, mice resuscitated with FFP had significantly greater contextual freezing compared with mice resuscitated with LR, consistent with improved hippocampal-dependent contextual memory. Cued fear conditioning did not differ between groups. LR and FFP resuscitation strategies resulted in distinct hippocampal hyaluronan and HS staining patterns, without synthesis gene expression differences. T/HS+LR brains showed increased 4-O-sulfated CS (CS-4S), a neurologically detrimental sulfation pattern, whereas FFP decreased CS-4S and increased CS-6S.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Goal-directed plasma resuscitation is associated with improved spatial memory and distinct eGC structural remodeling compared with volume-driven crystalloid resuscitation following T/HS. These findings highlight the potential for resuscitation strategy after hemorrhagic shock to influence neurological recovery, even in the absence of direct brain injury.

articles.title: Treatment of Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Review.

abstract.label: IMPORTANCE
abstract.text: Acute ischemic stroke, caused by thrombotic or embolic occlusion of a cervical or cerebral artery, leads to neurologic injury due to sudden disruption of blood flow to the brain. Ischemic stroke is a leading cause of disability and death and accounts for about 85% of strokes in the US.

abstract.label: OBSERVATIONS
abstract.text: Symptoms of acute ischemic stroke vary based on the area of the affected brain. Common presentations include sudden arm or leg weakness, aphasia or slurred speech, sudden loss of balance or coordination, sudden visual difficulties, and/or facial drooping. Patients with suspected stroke should be transported to the nearest emergency department for urgent brain imaging, typically noncontrast computed tomography (CT). Based on 2026 American Heart Association/American Stroke Association (AHA/ASA) guidelines, first-line therapy for patients with acute ischemic stroke presenting within 4.5 hours from symptom onset with disabling symptoms (eg, affecting the ability to perform activities of daily living) is intravenous thrombolysis (tenecteplase or alteplase) in those without intracranial hemorrhage or other contraindications to thrombolysis. The treatment window can be extended to 9 hours-and up to 24 hours in patients with large vessel occlusion (eg, involving the internal carotid artery or proximal middle cerebral artery [M1 segment]) who are unable to receive thrombectomy-based on identification of salvageable tissue using perfusion imaging with CT perfusion or magnetic resonance imaging. In appropriately selected patients with acute ischemic stroke, pooled randomized trial data show an approximately 10% absolute increase in the probability of a better functional outcome with intravenous thrombolysis. Based on 2026 AHA/ASA guidelines, endovascular thrombectomy, which involves clot removal with an intra-arterial mechanical device, is recommended for patients with large vessel occlusion within 6 hours of stroke onset (class 1 recommendation) and is recommended in selected patients with large vessel occlusion within 24 hours of last known well (class 1 recommendation). Endovascular therapy should be performed after intravenous thrombolysis unless patients have contraindications to thrombolytic therapy. Compared with medical management, which includes intravenous thrombolysis when indicated, endovascular thrombectomy produces an approximately 20% absolute increase in functional independence.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE
abstract.text: Acute ischemic stroke causes substantial disability and mortality. First-line therapy for patients with disabling acute stroke symptoms is intravenous thrombolysis (if no contraindications) within 4.5 hours of stroke onset and up to 24 hours in carefully selected patients not receiving mechanical thrombectomy; for large vessel occlusions, mechanical thrombectomy may be performed up to 24 hours after stroke onset in eligible patients.

articles.title: Clinical behaviors of efficient emergency physicians: insights into what they actually do -a scoping review.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Efficiency in the emergency department is critical for patient care and flow, yet it is a challenging competency to develop and is inconsistently taught in emergency medicine residency programs. This review focused on identifying strategies and behaviors of efficient emergency physicians that can be observed and taught.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A scoping review was conducted from January 1, 2015, to July 1, 2025 following the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology, to identify key behaviors of efficient emergency physicians. Medline/PubMed, Embase, Google Scholar, and gray literature were searched using controlled vocabulary, and included all types of methodologies except editorials and commentaries. Data were extracted using a standardized, structured process within the Covidence platform by two independent reviewers.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: After screening 6343 articles, 20 articles met full inclusion criteria. A clear and universally accepted definition of emergency department efficiency was not identified. Consequently, the included studies used a heterogeneous range of proxy measures to evaluate efficiency-related outcomes. Although no study directly demonstrated a specific set of strategies that improve efficiency, six major themes emerged. Efficient physicians showed greater effectiveness in communication, targeted investigations, documentation strategies, and clinical teaching skills. In addition, they employed specific cognitive and physical strategies like flow management and movement efficacy. Each theme yielded behaviors that either promoted or impeded efficiency.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Although our review identified a limited number of articles linking specific physician behaviors to efficiency metrics, it provides insights into behaviors and strategies that can be taught and observed in emergency physicians. Collectively, the identified strategies suggest that efficiency may largely depend on optimizing the initial patient encounter through communication, clinical reasoning, and shared decision-making. These findings represent the first step in a broader initiative aimed at developing a standardized observational tool to support the development of efficiency in emergency physicians.

articles.title: Sex-based analysis of characteristics, management, and outcomes of patients presenting to the emergency department with syncope.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Syncope is a common emergency department (ED) presentation and can be caused by serious conditions not evident on initial ED evaluation. Research into sex-based differences among ED patients presenting with syncope is lacking. We sought to compare clinical characteristics, management, risk stratification and serious outcomes between male and female ED syncope patients, assess the impact of sex on outcomes after adjusting for comorbidities and Canadian Syncope Risk Score predictors, and evaluate the change in performance of the Canadian Syncope Risk Score with the addition of sex.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a secondary analysis of the Canadian Syncope Risk Score derivation and validation study cohorts, comparing patient characteristics, ED management and outcomes between male and female patients presenting with syncope, using descriptive statistics and logistic regression models.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 9539 total patients, 5190 (54.4%) were female. Male patients were older, had more comorbidities, received more testing in the ED, had longer lengths of stay, were more frequently hospitalized and were more likely to have serious outcomes than females. The association between male sex and serious outcomes persisted after controlling for age, arrival by ambulance, hypertension, diabetes, coronary artery disease, atrial fibrillation or flutter, valvular heart disease, and congestive heart failure (OR=1.73, p<0.001) and Canadian Syncope Risk Score predictors (OR =1.45, p=0.005). However, adding sex to the Canadian Syncope Risk Score model did not significantly increase the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (difference = 0.0002, p=0.90).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Male ED syncope patients tended to have more risk factors than females, underwent more investigations, and were more likely to have serious outcomes even when controlling for comorbidities. While clinicians should recognize these sex-based differences, they can continue to rely on the Canadian Syncope Risk Score in its current form for risk stratification as incorporating sex did not improve model performance.

articles.title: Real-world handheld smartphone videos for nystagmus detection in acute vertigo: a feasibility study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Accurate identification of nystagmus is fundamental to the assessment of acute vertigo but remains challenging in emergency department (ED) settings. Although smartphone-based approaches have been proposed as scalable solutions, their feasibility under real-world acquisition conditions remains uncertain.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility of detecting nystagmus from handheld smartphone videos acquired in a real-world ED.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A subset of 67 videos from a published handheld smartphone-based acute vertigo dataset was analysed. A salient feature-based eye-tracking algorithm tracked stable ocular and periocular (facial) landmarks across frames. Horizontal displacement signals were extracted, and nystagmus episodes were identified through signal analysis and video verification.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Consistent eye-movement signals were successfully extracted from handheld smartphone recordings acquired during the acute phase of vertigo despite real-world challenges, including variable illumination, camera motion, image instability, and patient-related factors. Nystagmus patterns observed on video were accurately reflected in the corresponding signal traces, including very low-amplitude nystagmus that was barely discernible to the naked eye.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Our findings demonstrate that handheld image acquisition using standard, low-cost smartphones can capture clinically meaningful ocular motor information in real-world emergency care settings. This proof of principle lays the groundwork for the development of more ecologically valid scalable, telehealth-compatible tools for acute vertigo assessment. Further studies are needed to automate detection and validate performance in larger prospective cohorts.

articles.title: RSV bronchiolitis admissions in infants immunized with nirsevimab: a multicenter observational study.
authors: Impact of universal Respiratory Syncytial Virus prophylaxis in Spain Working Group

abstract.label: UNLABELLED
abstract.text: Real-world studies have confirmed the high effectiveness of nirsevimab, preventing approximately 80% of RSV bronchiolitis hospitalizations. This study aimed to evaluate the epidemiological and clinical characteristics of RSV bronchiolitis admissions following successful nationwide implementation of nirsevimab. We conducted a retrospective multicenter study across 15 Spanish pediatric emergency departments during the 2024-2025 RSV season. Infants eligible for the RSV prophylaxis, defined as those younger than six months at the start of or during the RSV season, with laboratory-confirmed RSV bronchiolitis requiring hospitalization were included. Patients immunized fewer than seven days before admission or with unknown immunization status were excluded. Epidemiological and clinical data were analyzed according to nirsevimab status, with age-stratified and multivariable analyses performed. Among 366 hospitalized infants with RSV bronchiolitis, 345 were previously healthy. Of these, 165/345 (47.8%) had received nirsevimab. Breakthrough cases were younger than non-breakthrough cases (2.0 months [IQR, 1.1-3.6] vs 5.2 months [IQR, 3.3-6.6]; p < 0.001). Overall, immunized and non-immunized infants showed similar rates of pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) admission (26.7% vs 21.1%; p = 0.2) and length of hospital stay (5 days [IQR, 3-7] vs 5 days [IQR, 4-7]; p = 0.6). After age stratification, clinical characteristics and outcomes remained comparable between groups. In multivariable analyses, no statistically significant association was observed between nirsevimab immunization and PICU admission, advanced respiratory support, or length of hospital stay.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In-hospital outcomes of RSV bronchiolitis admissions did not differ significantly by immunization status. These findings suggest that, once hospitalization is required, nirsevimab may offer limited additional protection against severe disease.

abstract.label: WHAT IS KNOWN
abstract.text: • Real-world studies have confirmed the high effectiveness of nirsevimab, preventing approximately 80% of RSV bronchiolitis hospitalizations.

abstract.label: WHAT IS NEW
abstract.text: • In-hospital outcomes of RSV bronchiolitis admissions did not differ significantly by immunization status. These findings suggest that, once hospitalization is required, nirsevimab may offer limited additional protection against severe disease.

articles.title: Traumatic renal injuries: the prevalence, management and outcome of renal vascular injury.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: To assess the prevalence, management and outcome of renal vascular injuries (RVIs; active bleeding and contained vascular injuries) seen on admission CT. Also, we wanted to find out the prevalence and survival of patients with concomitant injury to liver, spleen, and kidney seen on admission CT.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective, single-center, longitudinal cohort study with nine-year data (2013-2021) of all ≥ 15-year-old patients with renal injury identified in a trauma registry. Admission CT and angiographic examinations were reviewed to assess RVIs, including active bleeding, arterial dissection, segmental infarct, pseudoaneurysm or AV-fistulae. Medical records were reviewed for treatment, hospital length of stay and 30-day survival rate.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Out of 2805 patients with abdominal trauma, 243 (8.7%) had a renal injury, of whom 182 (74.9%) underwent CT on admission. RVI was found in 56 patients (30.8%). Among these 56 patients, 42 (75%) had active bleeding, eight (14.3%) segmental infarct, six (10.7%) pseudoaneurysm, and three (5.4%) arterial dissection. Of these, ten patients (17.9%) underwent angioembolization, and three (5.4%) underwent laparotomy. Patients with RVI were slightly older than those without RVI (43.6 vs. 37.8 years, p = 0.0409) and had more often a penetrating trauma (OR 2.836; 95% CI 1.127-7.136, p = 0.0416). Hospital length of stay (14.7 vs. 14.9 days, p = 0.9520) and 30-day survival (95.2% vs. 92.6%, p = 0.3165) did not differ significantly between patients without and with RVI. Among patients with available CT, fourteen (14/182; 7.7%) had concomitant injuries to the liver, spleen and kidney, with no statistically significant difference in 30-day survival compared with patients without such concomitant injuries (92.9% vs. 94.6%; p = 0.5237).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: RVI was not uncommon in our study cohort, occurring in 30.8% of patients with renal injury who underwent CT on admission. Of these, 17.9% were treated with angioembolization. Patients with RVI were slightly older and were more likely to have a penetrating injury than patients without RVI. No statistically significant difference in hospital length of stay or 30-day survival was found between patients without and with RVI.

articles.title: National Early Warning Score 2-Guided Sepsis Hour-1 Bundle Care for Adults With Suspected Sepsis in the Emergency Department: A Hybrid Type 1 Effectiveness-Implementation Stepped-Wedge Randomized Controlled Trial Pilot Study (NEWS-1 TRIPS).

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To increase the uptake of the Surviving Sepsis Campaign Hour-1 Bundle, we implemented a novel sepsis care model (National Early Warning Score [NEWS]-1 care), in which the Hour-1 Bundle is objectively triggered by a high NEWS-2 (≥ 5). We aimed to determine the feasibility of a full-scale type 1 hybrid effectiveness-implementation trial of this model.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: A pilot type 1 hybrid trial, comprising a stepped-wedge cluster randomized controlled trial and mixed-methods implementation evaluation with staff focus group interviews and an anonymous survey guided by the Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, and Maintenance framework.

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: Four emergency departments in Hong Kong.

abstract.label: PATIENTS
abstract.text: Adult patients of 18 years or older with a clinical diagnosis of infection requiring hospitalization and a NEWS-2 greater than or equal to 5.

abstract.label: INTERVENTIONS
abstract.text: Implementation of the Hour-1 Bundle when NEWS-2 was greater than or equal to 5.

abstract.label: MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS
abstract.text: The primary outcome was the feasibility of a full-scale hybrid trial, evaluated based on 14 progression criteria. Preliminary clinical effectiveness and safety were assessed, alongside implementation barriers and facilitators. During the implementation phase, compliance with lactate, blood culture, and antibiotics increased significantly. All progression criteria were met, except for suboptimal overall bundle compliance (56.1%). Exploratory intention-to-treat analysis (standard care group, n = 102; NEWS-1 group, n = 98) showed no significant between-group difference in 30-day all-cause mortality (standard care group, 3.9%; NEWS-1 group, 9.2%; absolute risk difference, 5.3%; 95% CI -1.6% to 12.1%); in-hospital, 90-day all-cause, or sepsis-related mortality; need for mechanical ventilation, renal replacement therapy, intensive care, or surgery; or ventilator-free days and adverse events. Implementation evaluation identified 15 barriers and 13 facilitators.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The effectiveness of NEWS-1 care remained uncertain, though adverse events were rare. A full-scale hybrid stepped-wedge trial is feasible but requires a much larger sample size. Real-world implementation barriers and facilitators should be considered in sepsis management guidelines.

articles.title: Neurological Outcomes of Rhythm Transitions in Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest With Initial Nonshockable Rhythms: A Nationwide Population-Based Study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To evaluate the prognostic implications of rhythm transitions between asystole and pulseless electrical activity (PEA) in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) patients with initial nonshockable rhythms.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Nationwide population-based observational study.

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: Nationwide OHCA Registry of South Korea, managed by the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency.

abstract.label: PATIENTS
abstract.text: Consecutive adult (≥ 18 yr old) OHCA patients with nonshockable rhythms from January 1, 2016 to December 31, 2021.

abstract.label: INTERVENTIONS
abstract.text: None.

abstract.label: MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS
abstract.text: Patients were categorized into four groups based on rhythm changes during cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR): asystole-to-asystole (A-A), asystole-to-PEA (A-P), PEA-to-asystole (P-A), and PEA-to-PEA (P-P). The primary outcome was good neurologic outcome at hospital discharge, defined as a Cerebral Performance Category score of 1-2. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was used to adjust for measured confounding. In the primary IPTW model, weighted risks of good neurologic outcome were 0.101% in A-A, 0.231% in A-P, 0.384% in P-A, and 0.874% in P-P. Compared with A-A, the odds of good neurologic outcome were higher in A-P (odds ratio [OR], 2.28; 95% CI, 1.78-2.93; risk difference [RD], 0.130 percentage points), P-A (OR, 3.80; 95% CI, 3.01-4.80; RD, 0.283 percentage points), and P-P (OR, 8.70; 95% CI, 6.98-10.83; RD, 0.773 percentage points). Compared with A-P, P-A had higher odds of good neurologic outcome (OR, 1.66; 95% CI, 1.39-1.99; RD, 0.153 percentage points).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Asystole conversion to PEA during CPR was associated with a better neurologic outcome than persistent asystole. Although transitioning from PEA to asystole was associated with lower odds of a good outcome compared with persistent PEA, it was associated with a better outcome than A-P transitions. Recognizing these patterns may provide prognostic context beyond a single rhythm assessment.

articles.title: Racial and Ethnic Disparities in Postarrest Cardiac Procedures for Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest.
articles.journal_full: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Effective postarrest care facilitates optimal outcomes for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. Relatively little research has evaluated whether there may be racial or ethnic disparities in the workup and management of the patient post arrest.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively studied out-of-hospital cardiac arrests using the TriNetX research database. We defined out-of-hospital cardiac arrest as any emergency department visit (2013-2024) with a diagnosis of cardiac arrest and included patients who survived to admission. Multivariate adjusted logistic regression was used to compare rates of the following cardiac interventions across race or ethnicity: (1) echocardiography; (2) left heart catheterization; (3) percutaneous coronary intervention; (4) ventricular assist device placement; and (5) automated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator placement.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 58 394 cases of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest met inclusion criteria. Compared with White patients (left heart catheterization: 13.9%, percutaneous coronary intervention: 7.1%, ventricular assist device: 3.0%, automated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator: 0.9%), Black patients had lower odds of receiving left heart catheterization (7.2%, adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.60 [95% CI, 0.55-0.64]), percutaneous coronary intervention (2.6%, aOR, 0.47 [95% CI, 0.42-0.53]), ventricular assist device placement (1.6%, aOR, 0.70 [95% CI, 0.60-0.80]), and automated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator placement (0.4%, aOR, 0.53 [95% CI, 0.41-0.70]). Hispanic/Latino patients were also less likely to receive left heart catheterization (8.9%, aOR, 0.72 [95% CI, 0.64-0.80]), percutaneous coronary intervention (3.7%, aOR, 0.63 [95% CI, 0.53-0.74]), and automated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator placement (0.4%, aOR, 0.52 [95% CI, 0.33-0.81]).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Our large multicenter analysis identifies racial or ethnic disparities in postarrest cardiac workup and management. Further research is needed to identify potential causes for these disparities with the hope of developing strategies to address them.

articles.title: Toxicological epidemiology and utilization patterns of Nepal's first institution-based poison information center.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Poisoning remains a major cause of preventable morbidity and mortality in low- and middle-income countries, yet Nepal has historically lacked centralized toxicology surveillance and consultation services. In 2023, piloting of an institution-based poison information center was done at Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital through a multi-national collaboration. We describe the epidemiology, utilization patterns, and clinical characteristics of cases managed during the pilot phase of the Nepal Poison Information Center.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a descriptive analysis of prospectively collected data from all consultations reported to the Nepal Poison Information Center between September 2023 and December 2024. Trained poison center specialists documented demographic characteristics, exposure details, toxicological agents, consultation characteristics, and clinical disposition using a secure database. Data cleaning and descriptive analyses were conducted using SAS statistical software (version 9.4; SAS Institute Inc., Cary, NC).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 393 poisoning cases were managed during the pilot period (September 2023-December 2024). Most patients were aged 18-39 years (53.4%), and 53.7% were female. Suspected intentional self-harm (suicidal-intent) accounted for 55.0% of exposures. Pesticides were the most common toxicological agents (46.1%), with insecticides (50.3%) and rodenticides (26.0%) predominating. Non-pesticide exposures included mushroom poisoning (8.1%), chemical exposures (7.6%), snake envenomation (6.9%), and medication-related poisonings (3.3%). The median time from exposure to poison information center phone call was four hours (IQR 1.0-15.0 hours). International toxicology experts were consulted in 28.2% of cases. The most common initial clinical disposition was observation in the emergency department (39.2%).Discussion:First, cases were dominated by intentional exposures, with suspected suicide accounting for 55% of all consultations. Second, pesticides represented nearly half of all primary toxicological agents (46.1%), with insecticides and rodenticides as the most common subtypes. Third, nearly one in three cases required consultation with international toxicology experts (28.2%), highlighting both the complexity of poisoning presentations and the limited availability of specialized toxicology expertise within Nepal. Together, these findings demonstrate that the pilot institutional PIC successfully operationalized a 24/7 toxicology consultation and follow-up model (previously described) while generating a centralized dataset capable of informing toxicovigilance, suicide prevention strategies, and regulatory policy. The PIC's model requires a daily follow up (and earlier if clinically indicated) of the patient (via phone by calling the treating providers) to acquire patient's clinical status and disposition plan. This study highlights the essential components required for sustainable poison center operations, including dedicated staffing, reliable telecommunications infrastructure, structured training pathways, continuous quality improvement processes, and integration of poisoning management within national emergency care and public health frameworks. Anchoring the pilot at Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital, a government-affiliated academic institution, was a strategic decision that provided institutional credibility, access to clinical pharmacology leadership, and a platform for national advocacy.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: During its pilot phase, Nepal's first institutional poison information center successfully delivered nationwide toxicology consultation and generated a centralized poisoning dataset. The predominance of intentional pesticide exposures and rising burden of other agents underscores the need for integrated suicide prevention strategies, strengthened pesticide regulation, and sustained investment in toxicology capacity and poison center infrastructure in Nepal.

articles.title: Electrical Cardiometry for Non-Invasive Cardiac Output Monitoring in Neonatal and Pediatric Critical Care: A Bayesian Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

abstract.text: ObjectivesTo evaluate the agreement between electrical cardiometry and established reference methods for cardiac output measurement in neonatal and pediatric critical care using Bayesian meta-analysis, while synthesizing evidence on stroke volume bias, prognostic associations, and hemodynamic-guided management.DesignSystematic review and Bayesian hierarchical random-effects meta-analysis conducted according to PRISMA 2020 recommendations.SettingNeonatal and pediatric intensive care units, emergency care settings, and interhospital transport services.Data SourcesMEDLINE via PubMed, Embase, Google Scholar, and ScienceDirect were searched from database inception through March 2026. Reference lists and forward citation tracking were additionally performed to identify eligible studies.Measurements and Main ResultsSix studies including 448 neonates and children met the eligibility criteria. Three method-comparison studies enrolled 223 participants, of which two studies comprising 193 participants and four datasets contributed to the primary Bayesian synthesis. The pooled posterior mean percentage error was 26.9% (95% credible interval [CrI], 24.3%-29.5%), with a 98.3% posterior probability that the true percentage error remained ≤30%. A secondary analysis showed a pooled stroke volume bias of 2.82 mL (95% CrI, 1.71-3.86) and a 99.5% posterior probability that the absolute bias remained <5 mL. Observational evidence associated lower cardiac output with longer mechanical ventilation, while a pilot randomized trial suggested that electrical cardiometry-guided management reduced fluid administration and accelerated vasoactive therapy initiation.ConclusionsPooled evidence indicated a high posterior probability of clinically acceptable agreement between electrical cardiometry and reference methods for cardiac output measurement. Its prognostic and therapeutic value should be confirmed in larger multicenter prospective studies.

articles.title: Informed consent and timely emergency obstetric care in Somalia: Ethical, clinical, and policy perspectives.

abstract.text: Maternal mortality remains a major public-health concern in Somalia, where timely access to emergency obstetric care is affected by referral difficulties, shortages of skilled staff, limited blood and surgical capacity, financial barriers, and weaknesses in facility-level processes. One insufficiently studied contributor to in-facility delay is the way consent for urgent obstetric interventions is discussed, obtained, and documented. In some maternity settings, clinicians may seek approval from husbands or other relatives before proceeding, even when an adult woman is able to make her own healthcare decision. However, direct Somalia-specific evidence measuring the frequency, duration, and maternal consequences of consent-related delays remains limited. Available evidence from Somalia, Somaliland, and the wider sub-Saharan African region suggests that consent practices may be influenced by provider communication, health literacy, family involvement, gender norms, financial constraints, and uncertainty about institutional procedures. This evidence-informed perspective examines the ethical, clinical, and policy implications of consent practices in Somali emergency obstetric care. It emphasizes that competent adult women should be supported to make their own healthcare decisions, while clear emergency protocols are needed for patients who temporarily lack decision-making capacity. Family involvement should support, rather than replace, the decisions of women who retain capacity. Respectful communication, documentation of capacity and consent, separation of financial authorization from clinical consent, and routine review of decision-to-treatment intervals may help reduce avoidable delays. Prospective research is needed to determine how frequently consent-related barriers occur and whether they independently influence maternal outcomes.

articles.title: Integrating neuromuscular and psychological strategies for injury prevention: A narrative review.

abstract.text: Sports-related injuries can have a substantial physical and emotional impact on athletes and physically active populations. In the past, pre- and post-injury prevention programs focused on neuromuscular issues, where the importance of rehabilitation was for joint stability to reduce re-injury. However, more recent literature has begun to recognize the interplay between the neuromuscular and psychological impact they can have. Neuromuscular training programs have continuously demonstrated their effectiveness in improving strength, balance, and movement mechanics in athletes, whereas psychological interventions can help regulate attention and focus. Thus, combining neuromuscular training and psychological strategies has significant potential for improving movement quality and injury prevention in athletes. This narrative review examines the individual roles of neuromuscular and psychological training, as well as the importance of the integration of both approaches to support athletes' readiness to return to play.

articles.title: Caregiver Perception of Procedural Pain and Health Care Provider Empathy During Pediatric Laceration Repair in the Emergency Department.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Pediatric laceration repair is a common and distressing emergency department (ED) procedure. Health care provider (HCP) empathy is considered central to family-centered care and perception of HCP empathy is linked to care outcomes, yet perception of HCP empathy surrounding pediatric ED procedures is understudied. We aimed to characterize caregiver perception of HCP empathy following pediatric laceration repair and examine associations with demographics, treatment factors, and procedural pain.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This cross-sectional study included a convenience sample of child-caregiver dyads (children 2 to 12 y) undergoing ED laceration repair. Children requiring inpatient admission, with developmental disability, or pain-related chronic illness were excluded. After the procedure, caregivers completed the Jefferson Scale of Patient Perceptions of Physician Empathy (range: 5 to 35). Child procedural pain was assessed via caregiver proxy report (Numeric Rating Scale) and researcher observation (Face, Legs, Activity, Cry, Consolability). HCPs self-reported demographics. We performed correlational and mean difference tests to examine associations between variables and caregiver-perceived HCP empathy.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The sample included 176 child-caregiver dyads (60% enrollment rate). Mean caregiver-perceived HCP empathy was 28.25±6.10 (range: 5 to 35). Only one empathy item ("understanding doctor") was strongly endorsed by most caregivers (58.8%). Caregiver-reported child procedural pain, but not researcher-observed pain, was negatively associated with perceived HCP empathy (r=-0.18, P=0.03). At the item-level, caregiver-reported child pain was significantly lower when caregivers strongly agreed with 4 of the 5 empathy items (Z's 2.26 to 3.05, P<0.05). Researcher-assessed pain, demographic, or treatment factors (midazolam, length of stay, laceration length) were not associated with perceived HCP empathy (all P>0.05).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Modest endorsement across empathy items highlight opportunities to enhance empathic, family-centered care surrounding pediatric ED procedures. Caregiver appraisal of child's pain was the only variable associated with perceived HCP empathy. Strategies targeting empathic pain-related communication may improve families' experiences and perception of care in the pediatric ED.

articles.title: Thank You to PEC Reviewers!
Fluorouracil-Associated Coronary Vasospasm and Reversible Cardiomyopathy Mimicking ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction During a First Cycle of FOLFOX: A Case Report.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of case reports

abstract.text: BACKGROUND 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) is a mainstay chemotherapeutic agent for gastrointestinal malignancies but carries a recognized risk of cardiotoxicity, most often manifesting as coronary vasospasm that can mimic acute myocardial infarction. This report describes the case of a 50-year-old woman with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) due to coronary artery vasospasm during continuous infusion of 5-FU as part of the first round of FOLinic acid (leucovorin), Fluorouracil (5-FU), and OXaliplatin (FOLFOX) chemotherapy for colorectal carcinoma. CASE REPORT A 50-year-old woman with colorectal carcinoma receiving her first cycle of FOLFOX developed severe chest pain during a continuous infusion of 5-FU. Initial emergency department evaluation was reportedly unremarkable, and she was discharged after symptomatic improvement with ketorolac. She returned emergently with recurrent crushing chest pain; a repeat electrocardiogram showed hyperacute T waves and ST-segment elevation, prompting ST-elevation myocardial infarction activation and transfer for emergent catheterization. Coronary angiography revealed no obstructive coronary artery disease. Echocardiography demonstrated a severely reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 30% to 35% with apical akinesis, consistent with 5-FU-induced cardiomyopathy. 5-FU was permanently discontinued, and the patient was treated with vasodilator therapy, with complete resolution of symptoms and normalization of ventricular function on follow-up echocardiography. CONCLUSIONS 5-FU can precipitate life-threatening coronary vasospasm and a fully reversible cardiomyopathy even during a first chemotherapy cycle, in the absence of obstructive coronary artery disease. Early recognition, prompt drug interruption, and a multidisciplinary cardio-oncology approach, including an individualized decision between permanent discontinuation and carefully supervised rechallenge, are essential to guide safe oncologic decision-making.

articles.title: Anterior Cruciate Ligament Injury Prevention Should Be Sport Specific: The Judo Case.
articles.journal_full: Clinical journal of sport medicine : official journal of the Canadian Academy of Sport Medicine

articles.title: Nurse-led inferior vena cava assessment using handheld ultrasound within a cardiologist-supported home-care workflow.

abstract.text: Volume assessment in older adults receiving home-based care is challenging because body weight, edema, and symptoms may be insufficient indicators, particularly in patients with cognitive impairment. We describe a 95-year-old woman with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, severe tricuspid regurgitation, atrial fibrillation, and dementia. Trained visiting nurses acquired standardized inferior vena cava (IVC) images during home visits and shared them with a cardiologist through a secure cloud-based platform. At the initial assessment, the maximum IVC diameter was 19.3 mm and the IVC collapsibility index was 29%; at 3 weeks, these values were 11.0 mm and 54.5%, respectively. Because IVC findings alone cannot establish volume status, they were interpreted alongside weight loss and reduced skin turgor, and oral fluid intake was encouraged based on the overall clinical assessment. Follow-up laboratory data were unavailable, and hydration status could not be objectively confirmed. This case illustrates the feasibility of a cardiologist-supported home-care workflow integrating nurse-performed IVC assessment and remote cardiologist review. Its clinical utility requires further evaluation.

articles.title: Multimodal Point-of-Care Ultrasound Indices and Cardiac Surgery-Associated Acute Kidney Injury: An Exploratory Prospective Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Cardiac Surgery-Associated Acute Kidney Injury (CSA-AKI) remains a common and multifactorial complication. Conventional biomarkers such as Serum Creatinine (SCr) detect injury late. This study explored whether perioperative multimodal Doppler ultrasonography could identify early haemodynamic alterations associated with CSA-AKI.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this prospective, single-centre observational study, adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery at Charlotte Maxeke Johannesburg Academic Hospital underwent serial transthoracic echocardiography and renal Doppler ultrasonography at baseline, on postoperative day 1, and on day 4. Clinical and Doppler-derived parameters were compared between patients who developed CSA-AKI and those who did not. CSA-AKI was defined according to the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria. Univariable logistic regression was performed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Fifty-four patients were included; 21 (39%) developed CSA-AKI. CSA-AKI was associated with higher EuroSCORE II (OR 1.22, 95% CI 1.05-1.50), diabetes mellitus (OR 7.47, 95% CI 2.17-29.3), reduced baseline mitral annular plane systolic excursion (MAPSE) (OR 0.79, 95% CI 0.62-0.96), lower renal End-Diastolic Velocity (EDV) at baseline (OR 0.75, 95% CI 0.59-0.91) and Day 4 (OR 0.70, 95% CI 0.51-0.89), and Day 1 elevated Central Venous Pressure (CVP) (OR 1.19, 95% CI 1.04-1.41). SCr increased, and eGFR declined in the CSA-AKI group by Day 4.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: The study findings suggest that CSA-AKI was associated with a perioperative haemodynamic profile characterised by lower MAPSE and renal EDV and higher CVP. These unadjusted associations are consistent with impaired longitudinal ventricular function, reduced renal diastolic perfusion, and venous congestion, respectively, but they do not establish causality. Left-ventricular ejection fraction and Renal Resistive Index (RRI) were not statistically associated with CSA-AKI in this cohort. The findings support a hypothesis regarding possible haemodynamic contributors to CSA-AKI that requires confirmation in adequately powered studies.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: CSA-AKI was associated with lower MAPSE, higher CVP, and reduced renal EDV in univariable analyses. In this observational study, reduced renal EDV may represent a potential haemodynamic marker warranting further investigation; however, no diagnostic threshold or clinical implication can be inferred from these data. Adequately powered prospective studies are required to validate this association and determine its potential clinical utility.

articles.title: Comparison of end-of-life care processes and outcomes for patients treated by allopathic versus osteopathic physicians: a population-based cross-sectional study in the USA.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: The USA has two types of medical schools: allopathic and osteopathic schools. End-of-life (EOL) care requires shared decision-making between patients and physicians and is potentially influenced by physician factors. However, little is known about whether allopathic and osteopathic physicians show different practice patterns in EOL settings. Therefore, this study aimed to compare EOL care processes and outcomes for beneficiaries treated by allopathic and osteopathic physicians.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We used cross-sectional data of a 20% random sample of fee-for-service Medicare beneficiaries aged ≥66 years who died in 2016-2019. Each beneficiary was attributed to a physician responsible for the largest number of evaluation and management visits in the last 6 months of life. Our outcomes were eight EOL care-related measures categorised into (1) advance care planning (ACP) and palliative care and (2) high-intensity care at the EOL. We estimated differences in these measures for beneficiaries treated by allopathic and osteopathic physicians, adjusting for physician and beneficiary characteristics.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 306 335 decedents, 240 907 (78.6%) were treated primarily by allopathic physicians and 65 428 (21.4%) by osteopathic physicians. We observed no differences in the eight measured indicators: billed ACP (adjusted rate, 14.1% vs 14.5%; p>0.99), palliative care counselling or hospice use in the last 180 days of life (62.4% vs 62.2%; p>0.99), emergency department visits (57.0% vs 56.9%; p>0.99), hospital admissions (50.9% vs 50.4%; p=0.31), intensive care unit admissions (27.3% vs 27.2%; p>0.99), mechanical ventilation or cardiopulmonary resuscitation (14.5% vs 14.4%; p>0.99), placement of feeding tubes (1.4% vs 1.4%; p>0.99) in the last 30 days of life, and death in acute care hospital (20.9% vs 20.4%; p=0.13).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: We found no evidence of differences in the eight measured EOL care indicators between beneficiaries treated by allopathic versus osteopathic physicians, although differences in unmeasured aspects of care cannot be excluded.

articles.title: Beyond Access Flow: The FLASH Multiorgan Framework for Assessing High-Flow Arteriovenous Fistulas in Hemodialysis.
articles.journal_full: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association

abstract.text: High-flow arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) impose a continuous hemodynamic burden on patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis, yet access blood flow (Qa) alone does not determine their cardiovascular significance. High access blood flow, high-output physiology, and clinically relevant cardiovascular intolerance represent related but distinct states whose expression depends on the interaction among access-related hemodynamic exposure, systemic flow response, cardiovascular reserve, volume status, and downstream cardiovascular consequences. This review proposes a clinically oriented, multiorgan framework for evaluating patients in whom an AVF is suspected of contributing to cardiovascular deterioration. Assessment begins with the clinical and dialysis context and integrates five interconnected domains: FISTULA, characterizing access-related hemodynamic exposure; LOAD, evaluating the systemic circulatory response; ASSESSMENT OF EXTRAVASCULAR LUNG WATER, identifying pulmonary congestion; SYSTEMIC VENOUS CONGESTION, assessing systemic venous consequences; and HEART, evaluating cardiac adaptation and maladaptation. Integration across these domains may reveal overlapping clinical-hemodynamic patterns, including preserved tolerance despite high flow, predominantly hyperdynamic physiology, cardiac maladaptation, systemic venous- or pulmonary-predominant consequences, and multicompartmental involvement. Discordance between systemic venous and pulmonary findings may provide physiologically relevant information rather than represent conflicting evidence. Serial reassessment after ultrafiltration, clinical change, or access-flow modification further emphasizes the dynamic nature of these patterns. The framework is intended to support physiologic interpretation rather than establish AVF causality, define new diagnostic categories, or propose treatment thresholds. Ultimately, assessment should move beyond asking how much blood flows through the fistula toward determining how the individual patient responds to that flow.

articles.title: [Hybrid Medicine in the 21st Century (Part 2)].

abstract.text: In this second part, are presented the remote practices of hybrid medicine and the applications recognized today in the literature, especially in patients with chronic diseases. Thus, hybrid care pathways use the practices of telemedicine (teleconsultation, teleexpertise and remote medical monitoring) for medical professionals, and those of telecare and teleexpertise for paramedical professionals (pharmacist, medical assistant). These pathways are personalized and are set up with the patient's consent. While remote care is now carried out in patients' homes, it requires innovative professional organizations, as well as precise coordination of pathways where several health professionals are involved.

articles.title: Treatment of clavicle fractures in adolescents.

abstract.text: Clavicle fractures constitute 10% to 15% of all fractures in adolescents. Historically, adolescent clavicle fractures have been treated non-operatively. Although recent data in the adult population has led to an increased rate of operative fixation in the adolescent population, a vast majority of these fractures in adolescents can be managed conservatively. This manuscript provides an overview of the current standard of care for clavicular fractures in adolescents in the context of sports medicine practices. To achieve this, a nonsystematic search of computerized databases of peer-reviewed articles was conducted, and a critical appraisal of existing literature was subsequently performed. Middle third clavicle fractures are by far the most common type and a vast majority of these fractures can be treated non-operatively with a sling given the robust healing and remodeling seen in adolescents. Lateral third fractures are far less common but may pose a risk for nonunion according to adult literature. Medial third fractures are the least common type and while they are typically non-displaced, patients with posteriorly displaced medial third fractures must have concomitant intrathoracic injury ruled out. Additionally, timing of the injury relative to competitive season could play a role in decision making as surgical fixation of clavicle fractures has been shown to yield faster return to play times.

articles.title: Cardiovascular disturbances and ward hypotension after major vascular surgery: a single-centre prospective cohort study.
articles.journal_full: Canadian journal of anaesthesia = Journal canadien d'anesthesie

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Postoperative hypotension can be caused by vasodilation, myocardial dysfunction, severe hypovolemia, and obstruction. We sought to estimate the effects of these causes on the incidence of hypotension after major vascular surgery.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a single-centre prospective cohort study of male and female adult patients undergoing major vascular surgery. We conducted point-of-care ultrasound and sidestream darkfield microscopy imaging to detect vasodilation, myocardial dysfunction, severe hypovolemia, and obstruction. The primary outcome was hypotension (systolic blood pressure < 90 mm Hg or a vasopressor infusion) within 24 hr of surgery.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We recruited 100 patients, of whom 89 had data available for analysis. Hypotension occurred in 20 participants (23%), vasodilation in 30 (34%), and myocardial dysfunction in 11 (12%). Severe hypovolemia and obstruction were not observed. The adjusted marginal risk difference of hypotension was 33% (95% confidence interval [CI], 14% to 53%; P < 0.001) for vasodilation and 41% (95% CI, 3% to 79%; P = 0.03) for myocardial dysfunction. Vasodilation increased the risk of intensive care unit admission by 27% (95% CI, 8% to 45%; P = 0.006) and of requiring a vasopressor infusion by 22% (95% CI, 4% to 39%; P = 0.02).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Vasodilation and myocardial dysfunction increased the risk of postoperative hypotension, providing insight into the mechanistic development of postoperative hypotension. The absence of severe hypovolemia was surprising. Clinicians should assess for vasodilation and myocardial dysfunction as potential preludes to postoperative hypotension, potentially using point-of-care echocardiography and sidestream darkfield microscopy.

articles.title: Diabetic myonecrosis: an under-recognised complication of uncontrolled diabetes.

abstract.text: Diabetic myonecrosis (DMN) is a rare but serious complication of long-standing, uncontrolled diabetes mellitus. We report a woman in her 60s who presented to the emergency department with a 3-week history of atraumatic subacute right thigh swelling, severe pain and muscle weakness leading to a fall. She had a background of type 2 diabetes mellitus, iron deficiency anaemia and sickle cell trait. Fracture and deep venous thrombosis were excluded. Laboratory investigations showed an elevated C-reactive protein without features of infection and mild elevation of creatine kinase, which is atypical for inflammatory myositis. MRI revealed extensive muscle infarction and oedema in the right thigh consistent with DMN. Optimisation of analgesia was central to functional recovery, while glycaemic control remained an essential component of management given its established association with this complication. Physiotherapy further supported recovery of muscle strength. DMN should be considered in atraumatic limb swelling in patients with long-standing uncontrolled diabetes to facilitate conservative management and avoid unnecessary tests and treatments.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of point-of-care ultrasound and radiography for triage of laryngotracheal stenosis in resource-limited settings: a prospective study protocol.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Delayed recognition of laryngotracheal stenosis (LTS) can cause substantial morbidity. Access to CT and specialist airway assessment is constrained in resource-limited settings. This study will evaluate point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) and soft-tissue neck radiography (XR) as potential triage tests for suspected LTS.

abstract.label: METHODS AND ANALYSIS
abstract.text: This prospective, cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study will recruit 109 consecutive patients aged ≥12 years referred for clinically indicated CT for suspected LTS at Frere Hospital, Eastern Cape, South Africa. Participants will undergo POCUS using a Butterfly iQ+device and Antero-posterior (AP) and lateral neck XR in randomised order, followed by CT within 24 hours where clinically feasible. The primary target is CT-defined >50% reduction in airway cross-sectional area from the larynx through the thoracic inlet. Sensitivity and specificity will be estimated for each index test, with 95% CIs, among participants with determinate results for both that test and the CT reference standard. Readers will be blinded to results from the other modalities. Positive, negative, indeterminate and missing results will be recorded separately. Paired comparisons and exploratory Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (ROC) analyses will be performed. Secondary outcomes will include interpretation agreement in 50 randomly selected examinations, technical feasibility, examination time, site-specific accuracy and exploratory acceptability interviews. The triage pathway will be modelled. Index results will not determine access to CT.

abstract.label: ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION
abstract.text: Approvals were obtained from Walter Sisulu University Health Sciences Research Ethics Committee (003/2026) and the Eastern Cape Health Research Committee (EC_202603_022). Written adult consent or adolescent assent with guardian consent will be obtained before research procedures. Findings will be disseminated through open-access publication, conferences and stakeholder engagement.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER
abstract.text: Pan African Clinical Trials Registry, PACTR202510808811458.

articles.title: CHOICE-UTI: protocol for a multicentre randomised non-inferiority trial comparing single versus three daily doses of intravenous antibiotics prior to oral therapy for complicated urinary tract infection in children.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Children with urinary tract infection (UTI) frequently receive intravenous (IV) antibiotics when clinicians consider the infection to be complicated or when oral therapy is not considered appropriate. However, the optimal duration of IV therapy before switching to oral antibiotics in this population remains unknown. The CHOICE-UTI trial aims to determine whether a single dose of IV antibiotic followed by oral therapy is non-inferior to three daily doses of IV antibiotic followed by oral therapy for children with complicated UTI.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This is a multicentre, open-label, non-inferiority randomised controlled trial conducted across emergency departments in Australia and New Zealand. Children aged 3 months to 18 years presenting with febrile UTI and at least one complicating feature for whom the treating clinician determines that IV antibiotics are required are eligible. Participants are randomised 1:1 to receive either one dose or three doses of once-daily IV antibiotics before switching to oral antibiotics, with both groups receiving a total of 7 days of therapy. The primary outcome is treatment failure at 72 hours after the first IV antibiotic dose, defined as persistence or development of fever, vomiting or rigors attributable to UTI. Secondary outcomes include readmission, antibiotic exposure, complications, recurrence of UTI and health-related quality of life. A total of 396 participants will be recruited.

abstract.label: ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION
abstract.text: Ethics approval was obtained from the Royal Children’s Hospital Human Research Ethics Committee (HREC/72065/RCHM-2021). Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and scientific meetings, and participating families will receive a summary of the study findings.

articles.title: Changes in pregabalin use and overdose after government interventions and media coverage: retrospective observational study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To evaluate trends in pregabalin use and overdose in Australia and examine temporal relationships with media coverage (December 2018), prescribing and dispensing restrictions (April 2020), and boxed warnings (February 2021).

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Retrospective observational study of dispensing and overdose data, with changepoint, interrupted time series, and latent class analysis.

abstract.label: SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme data (PBS; 10% random sample of people with drug subsidies) and overdose calls (self-harm, recreational use, and misuse) reported to Australia's largest Poisons Centre (50% national sample), 2016-24.

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES
abstract.text: Population adjusted rates of dispensing and overdose, timing of breakpoints and rate ratios, proportion of people who use pregabalin at high risk of misuse.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 227 864 people were dispensed 3 441 851 pregabalin prescriptions in the PBS 10% sample and 4871 pregabalin overdose calls were made to the Poisons Centre. Pregabalin use peaked in 2018 before plateauing and declining. Three breakpoints were found in dispensing data, with major decreases in level and slope: December 2018, May 2020, December 2021. The combined rate ratio for dispensing was 0.748 (95% confidence interval 0.700 to 0.800). Compared with the projected historical trend in the absence of interventions (counterfactual), approximately 118 390 (93 960 to 140 940) fewer pregabalin prescriptions were recorded nationally in December 2021, and an ongoing reduction of 0.7% (0.5% to 0.9%) was found each month. All breakpoints were associated with declines in overdose rates, with a combined rate ratio of 0.532 (95% CI 0.406 to 0.695). This reduction corresponded to approximately 41.3 (26.9 to 52.4) fewer pregabalin overdose calls in December 2021 and an ongoing reduction of 1.6% (1.0% to 2.3%) each month. Latent class analysis of 57 744 people dispensed pregabalin in the 12 months after the final breakpoint revealed four groups. The high risk group (7790, 13.5%) were more likely male, younger, dispensed more pregabalin, with shorter refill interval and high rates of opioids and benzodiazepine co-use (5120 (65.7%) and 2455 (31.5%), respectively).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Pregabalin use and overdose in Australia have declined in recent years. Major decreases in trend corresponded with media coverage (December 2018) and prescribing and dispensing restrictions (May 2020). The third breakpoint may be a delayed impact of boxed warnings (implemented February 2021). These findings suggest that regulatory and risk communication measures may contribute to reducing pregabalin related harm.

articles.title: Post-Antibiotic Lyme Arthritis in Children Presenting to the Emergency Department.

abstract.text: Of 124 children with Lyme arthritis enrolled in a pediatric emergency department, 19 [15%; 95% confidence interval (CI) 10-22%] had received > 4 weeks of antibiotics and 6 (5%, 95% CI 2-10%) had post-antibiotic Lyme arthritis, defined by requirement for an immunomodulator and/or intra-articular steroid injection to achieve symptom resolution.

articles.title: SUDDEN CARDIAC ARREST IN NEW SOUTH WALES (NSW), AUSTRALIA: A DATA LINKAGE STUDY.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) is a global health challenge. Routinely collected health data represents a potential source of data to identify SCA.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Evaluate whether routinely collected health data can retrospectively identify community-based SCA (1-50 years) in NSW.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Potential SCA cases (aged 1-50yrs; occurring in NSW; cardiac-related ICD-9/10/SNOMED codes) were identified by the Centre for Health Record Linkage (CHeReL) in the NSW Ambulance OHCA Register (OHCAR) and NSW Emergency Department Data Collection (EDDC). Probabilistic data linkage was undertaken between ambulance, hospital and mortality datasets. External causes were excluded at case identification in ambulance records. Cardiac aetiology was assigned where a cardiac diagnosis appeared in hospital admission or cause of death records.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: From 1.7 million linked records, 13,345 presumed SCA cases were identified; 54% had cardiac aetiology and 83% were fatal. Cardiac cases were older than non-cardiac cases (median 42 vs 37 years, p < 0.001) and more likely to be admitted to hospital (58% vs 7%, p < 0.001). Within cardiac cases, rhythm-related and structural diagnoses dominated in 1-11 year olds, while ischaemic disease dominated in 35-50 year olds. Older cardiac cases were more likely to die pre-hospital (adjusted OR 3.56, 95% CI 2.66-4.85, for 35-50 vs 1-11 years).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONX
abstract.text: Multi-source administrative data linkage identifies age-related patterns in SCA aetiology and clinical trajectory. Findings extrapolated nationally suggest approximately 370 cardiac SCA deaths per year in Australians aged 1 to 35, a substantial burden that could be tracked through routine data linkage.

articles.title: Transcatheter Arterial Embolization for Pediatric Renal Trauma: A National Trauma Data Bank Analysis (2017-2024).
articles.journal_full: Journal of vascular and interventional radiology : JVIR

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: To describe pediatric renal embolization outcomes and compare transcatheter arterial embolization (TAE) with surgery and conservative management in transfused children with high-grade renal trauma.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: Children younger than 18 years undergoing kidney embolization in the National Trauma Data Bank (2017-2024; n=101) were assessed using registry-based clinical-success proxies. Transfused American Association for the Surgery of Trauma (AAST) grade III-V patients were classified as TAE (n=86), therapeutic renal surgery (n=348), or conservative management (n=634). Separate propensity models supported 1:1 matching without replacement for TAE versus surgery and conservative management, exactly by grade, age band, and blunt/penetrating mechanism. Mortality included emergency department and inpatient deaths.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Median time to embolization was 3.08 hours. Primary and secondary clinical success were 90/101 (89.1%) and 93/101 (92.1%). Under the broader composite, primary success was lower after penetrating than blunt injury (68.8% vs 92.7%; P=.016), but the renal-specific comparison was inconclusive (P=.253). TAE was used in 5.7% of transfused grade III-V injuries. In 59 TAE-surgery pairs, mortality was 6/59 (10.2%) versus 10/59 (16.9%; conditional odds ratio [cOR] 0.56, 95% CI 0.15-1.85; P=.424). In 70 TAE-conservative pairs, mortality was 7/70 (10.0%) in each arm (cOR 1.00, 95% CI 0.27-3.74; P=1.000). Measured injury and admission-year imbalance remained.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Nearly 9 of 10 children avoided qualifying reintervention after kidney embolization. The penetrating-injury association included potentially extra-renal laparotomy and did not establish greater renal-specific embolization failure. Matched mortality comparisons were inconclusive.

articles.title: Bedside diaphragm ultrasound for early risk stratification in patients with sepsis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: This study aimed to evaluate the relationship between early bedside diaphragmatic ultrasonography findings and clinical outcomes in patients diagnosed with sepsis.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This prospective observational study included adult patients who presented to the emergency department with sepsis. Diaphragmatic ultrasonography was performed within the first hour of admission, and diaphragmatic thickness (DT), diaphragmatic thickening fraction (DTF), and diaphragmatic excursion (DE) were measured. Intensive care unit (ICU) admission, invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV), need for vasoactive therapy, and mortality were recorded.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 110 patients were included in the study and the in-hospital mortality rate was found to be 21.8%. The mean DE was 3.15 ± 1.31 cm, and the mean DTF was 27.5 ± 13.1%. DD and DA were detected in 30.9% and 26.4% of patients, respectively. ICU admission, IMV, NIMV, vasoactive treatment requirements, and mortality rates were significantly higher in patients with DD or DA (p < 0.01 for all comparisons). Furthermore, SOFA, qSOFA, MEWS, and APACHE II scores were significantly higher in patients with DD and DA.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In multivariate regression analysis DTF<20% + age + SOFA was independently associated with in-hospital mortality (adjusted (OR: 70.59; 95% CI: 15.27-60.26; p < 0.001).For mortality, DTF<%20 discriminated outcome with an AUC of 0.92 (95% CI 0.86-0.97), DT < 2 mm with an AUC of 0.70 (95% CI: 0.60-0.81), and DE < 2 cm with an AUC of 0.55 (95% CI 0.44-0.65). Bedside diaphragm ultrasound, and DTF in particular, may therefore be a useful adjunct for early risk stratification in emergency department patients with sepsis.

articles.title: Withdrawal-related calls to a statewide poison control center: a ten-year review.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Poison control centers are commonly utilized by the public and healthcare providers following potentially harmful substance exposures. Less frequently, poison control centers are contacted regarding substance withdrawal. This study characterizes a decade of withdrawal-related calls to a statewide poison control center and explores their potential value in identifying emerging public health concerns.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective review of all calls to a statewide poison control center from 2015-2024 that were classified as "withdrawal" for reason of call. Variables assessed included year of call, patient demographics, substance(s) involved, disposition, and medical outcome. Medical outcomes were categorized using National Poison Data System® definitions as minor, moderate, or major. Descriptive statistics were performed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
