abstract.text: During the study period, 198 withdrawal-related calls were identified, averaging approximately 20 annually. Most calls originated from hospitals (58.1%), while 36.9% came from private residences. The most frequently implicated substances were tianeptine (24.2%), opioids (20.7%), and benzodiazepines (14.1%). Tianeptine first appeared in 2019 and contributed substantially to an increase in withdrawal-related calls beginning in 2020. The median patient age was 35 years, and 53.0% were male. Overall, 37.4% of cases resulted in at least a moderate medical outcome (34.8% moderate, 2.5% major). Tianeptine accounted for the largest proportion of moderate or major outcomes, followed by opioids, benzodiazepines, gamma-hydroxybutyrate, antidepressants, and phenibut. Sixty-three patients (31.8%) required hospital admission, including 36 (18.2%) admitted to an intensive care unit; tianeptine was associated with 27.8% of ICU admissions. No deaths were documented.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: This ten-year review demonstrates that withdrawal-related calls represent a small but clinically important component of PCC utilization. Although PCCs are traditionally associated with the management of acute toxic exposures, our findings highlight their broader role in providing consultation for substance withdrawal syndromes and their value as a real-time toxicovigilance resource. An important finding of this study was the changing pattern of substances associated with withdrawal over time.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Poison control center utilization extends beyond substance exposure and includes management of substance withdrawal. Withdrawal-related calls may provide valuable surveillance data regarding emerging substance use trends and public health concerns, particularly involving tianeptine and opioids.

articles.title: AquaMamba: Selective state space modeling for underwater scene segmentation in marine robotics.

abstract.text: Underwater scene segmentation is challenging because image degradation and domain shift vary greatly in marine environments, and the behavior of selective state-space models (SSMs) in this environment remains insufficiently characterized. We propose AquaMamba, a ResNet34-UNet segmentation framework that replaces the bottleneck operator with stacked Mamba layers, and compare it with five established CNN-based methods and a constructed Transformer-bottleneck baseline in the SUIM benchmark. AquaMamba achieves an mIoU of 0.669, 1.9 percentage points higher than the controlled Trans-UNet baseline (0.650), while using fewer parameters (29.5M vs. 33.9M). DeepLabV3 + remains the strongest overall model, reaching 0.712 mIoU. On the unlabeled UIEB dataset, AquaMamba shows the highest confidence retention among four representative models, retaining 93.5% of its source-domain prediction confidence. Due to the lack of semantic annotation in UIEB, this result reflects prediction confidence rather than target-domain segmentation accuracy. Scale- and boundary-specific diagnostics within the selected representative subset further show complementary behavior among AquaMamba, Trans-UNet and DeepLabV3 + : AquaMamba is competitive in several large object categories and obtains the lowest boundary error point estimate, while DeepLabV3 + remains stronger for human divers and plant/seagrass, and AquaMamba is limited on the reported small-RO subset. These findings position AquaMamba as a controlled SSM baseline for underwater semantic segmentation and emphasize the need for future SSM designs to better integrate multi-scale and high-resolution features.

articles.title: Prolonged length of stay in the Italian emergency departments: A competing risks frailty model.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Emergency department (ED) overcrowding has increased worldwide in recent years. This paper provides quantitative information based on data collected immediately before the COVID-19 outbreak, which can serve as a baseline for developing systematic approaches to prolonged length of stay (LoS) in EDs.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: We analysed a random sample of 10,077 ED accesses drawn from the 503,797 eligible accesses recorded in 2019 in the 16 largest hospitals of Sicily, Italy. LoS was modelled using a cause-specific competing-risks Cox frailty model with Discharge and Hospitalization as competing endpoints. Two log-normal frailty components were included to account for unobserved heterogeneity between EDs and between patients. Non-proportionality was addressed by stratifying on pathology and by including time-varying effects for triage. Cumulative incidence functions (CIFs) were computed to estimate the probability of each endpoint and strata over time.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Median LoS was 1.70 hours for Discharge and 3.77 hours for Hospitalization, and the gap widened markedly in the upper tail (90th percentile: 7.10 vs 34.95 hours). Discharge was associated with pathology, age, triage, sex and season; Hospitalization with pathology, age, triage and season. The hazard of Discharge decreased by 2% per additional year of age (HR = 0.98, 95% CI 0.977-0.983) and was 10% higher for accesses in summer (HR = 1.10, 95% CI 1.03-1.16). The hazard of Hospitalization increased by 0.4% per year of age (HR = 1.004, 95% CI 1.001-1.007). The effect of triage was time-dependent: at 10 hours of LoS, red-coded accesses had a 69% lower hazard of Discharge (HR = 0.31) and a 53% higher hazard of Hospitalization (HR = 1.53) than other codes. Circulatory and respiratory diseases and blood diseases showed the highest CIFs for Hospitalization and prolonged LoS for both endpoints, whereas skin and musculoskeletal diseases, injuries and poisoning, and nervous system diseases showed the highest CIFs for Discharge.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Prolonged LoS in Sicilian EDs was driven mainly by pathology, and the exit process differed systematically across disease groups: patients with circulatory and respiratory diseases and with blood diseases waited longest before both Discharge and Hospitalization.The large between-ED heterogeneity in the hazard of Hospitalization, indicates that admission delays reflect organisational as well as structural constraints. Interventions to reduce overcrowding - in particular any expansion of inpatient capacity - should therefore be targeted at the specific wards receiving these patients, rather than applied uniformly across the hospital.

articles.title: Comprehensive Multimodal Analgesia Protocol with TAP Block Reduces Postoperative Opioid Use in Bariatric Surgery.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Perioperative opioid use after bariatric surgery carries substantial risk of opioid-related harm, and multimodal analgesia (MMA) protocols limit opioids while maintaining effective pain control. We evaluated whether adding an intraoperative laparoscopic transversus abdominis plane (TAP) block to an established MMA regimen reduces inpatient and outpatient opioid use, pain scores, and 30-day perioperative outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study at a high-volume MBSAQIP-accredited academic medical center of patients who underwent minimally invasive bariatric surgery from 2015 to 2024. Patients with concurrent ventral hernia repair, cholecystectomy, or preoperative opioid use were excluded. Two cohorts were compared: MMA alone (January 2015-June 2017) and MMA + TAP block (July 2017-December 2024). The primary outcome was inpatient morphine milligram equivalents (MME).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 2,660 patients (MMA alone, n = 618; MMA + TAP, n = 2,042), baseline characteristics were similar despite a small difference in procedure mix (p < 0.0001). The MMA + TAP cohort required fewer inpatient opioids (median MME 76 vs. 134, p < 0.0001) and had lower median inpatient pain scores (3 vs. 4, p < 0.0001). Opioid use at 12 months was lower with MMA + TAP (17% vs. 24%, p < 0.0001) and remained reduced at 36 months. Length of stay, readmissions, and emergency department visits were comparable.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: A comprehensive multimodal pain regimen including laparoscopic TAP block reduced opioid use and pain scores without increasing 30-day emergency department visits or readmissions.

articles.title: Academic collaboration with industry: Case studies from health care delivery operations.

abstract.text: Business and engineering scholarship's relevance largely relies on its practical applicability. As health care delivery grows to represent a major portion of the global economy, its distinct culture and unique challenges necessitate stronger relationships between health care practice and academia. This paper explores academic collaborations with the health care delivery industry, emphasizing the compelling benefits for health care organizations (and their patients), researchers, and students in the context of care delivery operations. Through four case studies, and by drawing upon our experiences as a diverse set of operations scholars, we highlight successful models of collaboration between operations academia and health care institutions. These models enable many of the benefits realized, such as reductions in patient wait times and visit lengths, more equitable physician scheduling, faster ambulance dispatch, and reduced surgical appointment cancellations, among others, while also improving relevance for students and practical application for theory. While the potential benefits are clear, challenges persist, often emanating from cultural differences, funding uncertainties, and the nuances of industrial vs. academic objectives. However, when navigated effectively, these collaborations can advance both sectors, bridging the gap between academic theory and real-world application. Drawing from existing literature and supplemented by rich case study evidence, this article offers guidance for care institutions and individual scholars seeking to establish and foster similar partnerships. By delineating the parameters of successful collaborations and drawing from a diverse portfolio of experiences, this paper hopes to encourage and enable more synergistic efforts, potentially transforming health care operations and leading to improved outcomes for patients, institutions, and academia.

articles.title: [Resilience and crisis robustness of trauma networks: mass casualty incident, major incidents and security of care provision].

abstract.text: Trauma networks are essential structures for the coordinated care of severely injured patients; however, in addition to maintaining high-quality routine care, they must be prepared for mass casualty incidents, major incidents, terrorist attacks, natural disasters, pandemics, cyberattacks, infrastructure failures and supply chain disruptions. Resilience describes the capability of a healthcare system to anticipate hazards, maintain essential functions during crises, adapt to changing conditions, recover and learn from experience. The German TraumaNetwork DGU® provides important prerequisites for resilient trauma care through regional cooperation between trauma centers, defined supply standards, established communication pathways, quality management and continuous documentation in the TraumaRegister DGU®; however, crisis resilience extends beyond individual hospital capacities. It requires adequate and redundant personnel, space, equipment, blood products, medicines, information technology, communication systems and organizational resources. During a crisis, the patient distribution must be dynamically adapted to injury severity, treatment requirements, transport options and actually available regional hospital capacity. Recent developments in Germany, including the German Society for Trauma Surgery's framework for "Traumatological care in catastrophes, crises and wars", emphasize the need to further develop existing trauma networks into resilient regional systems. Future preparedness should combine structural redundancy, crisis-specific training, secure supply chains, analogue fallback procedures, resilient digital infrastructure and coordinated crisis management. Resilience should become an explicit quality dimension of trauma networks and be evaluated through defined indicators and regular exercises.

articles.title: [Disaster medicine in undergraduate medical education in Germany: curricular integration, relevance of learning objectives and barriers to implementation : A nationwide survey of faculty leads for multidisciplinary course 8].

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Previous nationwide surveys demonstrated a heterogeneous implementation of disaster medicine education across German medical faculties. This study aimed to provide an updated assessment from the perspective of the teaching personnel responsible for multidisciplinary course 8 (QB 8), including predefined learning objectives, teaching formats and implementation barriers.

abstract.label: MATERIAL AND METHODS
abstract.text: A nationwide quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among QB 8 faculty leads at the 35 medical faculties affiliated with the German Medical Faculty Association at the time of data collection. Data were collected from 1-31 October 2025 using a standardized REDCap® (Research Electronic Data Capture) online questionnaire. Complete questionnaires were analyzed descriptively. Item-specific subpopulations were reflected in the predefined questionnaire routing.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Overall, 23 out of 35 questionnaires were completed (65.7%). Disaster medicine was taught at 18 out of 23 faculties (78.3%) and was mandatory in QB 8 at 10/23 (43.5%). Anesthesiology and intensive care medicine were involved at 16/18 faculties (88.9%). Foundations and strategies of care during mass casualty incidents were rated highly/very highly relevant by 19/20 respondents (95.0%); triage, differentiation between individual and disaster-adapted care and ethical/legal conflicts each by 18/20 (90.0%). The most frequent barriers were insufficient funding/resources (15/20; 75.0%), low curricular priority (11/20; 55.0%) and insufficient integration into mandatory teaching (10/20; 50.0%). Simulations (17/20; 85.0%) and case-based seminars with realistic scenarios (14/20; 70.0%) were most frequently considered particularly suitable.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Disaster medicine education is widely implemented among the participating faculties but remains heterogeneous regarding mandatory curricular implementation. The findings support the necessity for an expert consensus on priority learning objectives and further evaluation of competency-based teaching formats that are feasible within undergraduate medical curricula.

articles.title: Voluntariness of same-day versus advance consent in low-risk clinical research: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal_full: Canadian journal of anaesthesia = Journal canadien d'anesthesie

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: The solicitation of same-day consent for participation in clinical research is commonly prohibited by research ethics boards because of concerns about limited decision-making time and patient vulnerability. However, these concerns lack empirical support and restrict both research efforts and patient participation opportunities, particularly in medical specialties such as emergency medicine, critical care, and anesthesiology, in which clinicians and patients interact for the first time on the day of a procedure. We aimed to assess the voluntariness of research consent solicited on the day of surgery compared with consent obtained in advance.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We performed a prospective, noninferiority randomized controlled trial examining the voluntariness of informed consent to participate in a low-risk clinical research trial at Women's College Hospital in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. The trial design included active deception (invitation to participate in a fabricated research trial) to capture authentic measurements of participants' perceptions of any perceived coercion.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We randomized 114 patients scheduled to undergo anterior cruciate ligament repair for recruitment into a fabricated low-risk perioperative research trial at one of two time points: at a virtual preanesthesia clinic appointment in advance of the day of surgery, or on the day of surgery. Regardless of their decision, all participants received the (same) standard of care. Overall, 71/114 patients (62%) either consented to participate in the fabricated trial or declined participation but consented to a feedback session during which perceptions of coercion were assessed. Greater participation was observed among patients approached on the day of surgery (fabricated trial, 26/58 [45%]; feedback session only, 18/58 [31%]) than in advance (fabricated trial, 17/56 [30%]; feedback session only, 10/56 [18%]). Perceived coercion, measured using two validated psychometric instruments, did not differ between patients recruited on the day of surgery and those recruited in advance. A subset of patients in each group reported modest perceptions of undue influence, but regardless of recruitment time point, these patients demonstrated their agency to decline participation.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Our findings suggest that restrictive same-day consent policies, when based on concerns regarding undue influence, may represent a structural barrier to participation in low-risk trials that lacks empirical justification.

abstract.label: STUDY REGISTRATIONS
abstract.text: 1) Open Science Framework ( 46twc ); first submitted 17 March 2023; 2) ClinicalTrials.gov ( NCT07380035 ); first submitted 16 January 2026.

articles.title: Handheld Ultrasound Confirmation of Pediatric Endotracheal Intubation in a Resource-Limited Country.
articles.journal_full: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Chest radiograph (CXR) and colorimetric capnography for confirmation of endotracheal tube (ETT) placement may be costly and inaccessible in resource-limited countries. Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is considered a low-cost, fast alternative. We sought to study the accuracy of bedside POCUS as compared with CXR, using a pocket-sized handheld device, for confirmation of ETT placement in the neonatal ICU and PICU.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Prospective, observational study.

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: PICU and neonatal ICU in a tertiary care center in Nepal between October 1, 2023, and April 30, 2024.

abstract.label: PATIENTS
abstract.text: Newborns to 14-year-old children.

abstract.label: INTERVENTIONS
abstract.text: POCUS using a handheld device at the bedside.

abstract.label: MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS
abstract.text: POCUS was performed on 59 intubated children; 37 (62%) were males. Median age was 3 hours (interquartile range [IQR], 1-5 hr) in newborns (n = 27) and 24 months (IQR, 12-84 mo) in children (n = 32). POCUS demonstrated tracheal-confirmed ETT placement in 53 children (89.8%), suspected endobronchial in four, and indeterminate in two. CXR agreed with all 53 POCUS tracheal-confirmed intubations. There were three additional tracheal-confirmed cases on CXR and three endobronchial intubations. Sensitivity and specificity of POCUS for detection of ETT placement in the trachea, compared with CXR, were 94.6% (95% CI, 85.1-98.9%) and 100% (95% CI, 29.2-100%), respectively. Based on this, accuracy was calculated at 94.9%.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Our study demonstrated good accuracy of POCUS using a handheld device to confirm ETT placement in neonates and children. It could be a reliable and effective method in a resource-limited country like Nepal.

articles.title: From sirens to systems: Characterizing EMS and trauma care across America.
articles.journal_full: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: State emergency medical services (EMS) and trauma systems determine prehospital triage, transport, trauma center designation, data reporting, and quality improvement, yet their contemporary organization has not been systematically characterized. We sought to describe state-level EMS and trauma system structures, policies, resources, and perceived gaps across the United States.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a cross-sectional survey of EMS and trauma system leaders in all 50 states and the District of Columbia from July 2025 through March 2026. A 56-item instrument utilizing categorical, Likert-type, rank-order, and free-text items assessed oversight, prehospital triage and transport, clinical protocols, trauma center verification, registries, quality improvement, and funding. Respondents were recruited by email and phone. Multiple respondents could contribute complementary domain-level information to a single state profile. Responses were summarized descriptively.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: All 51 jurisdictions participated. Most states reported a state EMS medical director (84%), statewide trauma triage protocols (84%), and mandatory participation in their state trauma registry (88%). However, operational coordination varied: only 29% had a centralized trauma communications center, only 6% of states reported a single point of contact for helicopter EMS dispatch, and 35% required a certificate of need for new helicopter services. Trauma center verification relied on American College of Surgeons (ACS) verification in 59% of states, while others used state-administered processes. More than half of states rated EMS financial resources in the two lowest adequacy categories, and 55% reported that their trauma system required at least moderate improvement. Rural populations were most frequently identified as underserved (96%) and as experiencing worse outcomes (92%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: State EMS and trauma systems share broad adoption of national clinical standards but differ substantially in governance, coordination, verification, data integration, and funding.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE AND STUDY TYPE
abstract.text: Level V, Prognostic/epidemiological.

articles.title: High-Entropy Materials for Electrochemical Gas Conversion.

abstract.text: High-entropy materials (HEMs) are composed of multiple principal elements stabilized by the configurational entropy. They establish a new design paradigm in electrocatalysis by leveraging local disorder and multielement synergy to create diverse and tunable active site environments. While HEMs have been broadly reviewed, a focused and reaction-specific assessment of their role in gas-involved electrocatalysis is absent. This review fills that gap by examining entropy-driven design principles, entropy-guided synthesis, nanoscale structural control, and advanced characterization of HEMs and by linking these aspects to their reaction-specific catalytic behavior in gas-involved electrocatalysis. We build a unified framework linking high-entropy chemistry to catalytic function across five key reactions: the CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR), hydrogen oxidation reaction (HOR), oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), nitrogen reduction reaction (NRR), and nitrogen oxidation reaction (NOR). We provide comprehensive coverage across all major HEM families, including high-entropy alloys, oxides, chalcogenides, hydroxides, fluorides, MXenes, and single-atom configurations, highlighting features unique to each system. Key challenges and future directions are outlined, including scalable synthesis, active-site identification, machine-learning-guided discovery, and interfacial engineering. This review provides a reaction-focused framework for advancing HEM-based electrocatalysis and offers guidance for designing next-generation materials for clean energy technologies.

articles.title: Preventive use of hyperbaric oxygen therapy and nitroglycerin ointment in high-risk lipoabdominoplasty.
Video of the inciting event in emergency trauma care: a narrative review and measurement framework.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Video is already used in crash reconstruction, sports injury research, prehospital triage, and emergency care. The unresolved question is whether video of the inciting traumatic event provides clinically useful exposure information beyond a strong clinical assessment and a structured verbal history, without confusing selective video availability or selective diagnostic verification with biology.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a narrative methodological review of representative literature identified in PubMed/MEDLINE and by citation chaining through 1 September 2026. We synthesized work on crash reconstruction, sports video analysis, emergency video use, equestrian trauma, measurement validity, diagnostic verification, and clinical prediction. On this basis, we developed a staged framework using equestrian falls as an exemplar testbed. If Phase 2 proceeds, its primary predictive estimand is the incremental value of video among adults with usable inciting-event video who undergo clinically indicated head computed tomography (CT), with acute CT-visible intracranial traumatic abnormality as the endpoint.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Existing studies show that video can characterize injury mechanisms, support injury-versus-non-injury comparisons, and influence emergency decisions. Routine trauma introduces four practical problems: video is available selectively, prior viewing can alter baseline information, head CT is obtained selectively, and acute CT-visible intracranial injury may be uncommon. We therefore propose a two-phase program: first measure video availability, history-video agreement, rater reliability, verification, event yield, and burden; only if prespecified feasibility and sample-size criteria are met should prediction proceed.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Inciting-event video should be evaluated as a measurement instrument before it is promoted as a clinical predictor. A gated measure-first, predict-second design can determine whether seeing the event adds information beyond asking about it carefully and can stop early when the testbed is not statistically or operationally viable.

articles.title: Comparison of Risk Assessment Tools in Patients Diagnosed With Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding in the Emergency Department: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal_full: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research

abstract.text: BACKGROUND Upper gastrointestinal bleeding (UGIB) is a common and potentially life-threatening condition in the emergency department (ED), and accurate risk stratification is essential for guiding management decisions. The comparative performance of disease-specific scores (Glasgow-Blatchford Score [GBS] and AIMS65) and general early warning scores (National Early Warning Score 2 [NEWS2] and Modified Early Warning Score [MEWS]) in predicting ED-specific outcomes remains unclear. MATERIAL AND METHODS This retrospective cohort study was conducted in a tertiary-care ED between January 1, 2021, and December 31, 2022. Adult patients (≥18 years) with endoscopically confirmed non-traumatic UGIB were included. We extracted demographic data, clinical findings, endoscopic findings, and transfusion requirements from electronic medical records. We calculated GBS, AIMS65, NEWS2, and MEWS. The primary outcome was the need for red blood cell (RBC) transfusion in the ED. The secondary outcome was an adverse ED outcome. RESULTS A total of 905 patients were included (mean age 63±18 years; 65.6% female). RBC transfusion was required in 41.0% of patients, and 40.7% experienced adverse ED outcomes. Median GBS, NEWS2, and MEWS scores were significantly higher in patients requiring transfusion and in those with adverse ED outcomes (all P<0.001). AIMS65 showed the lowest discriminative performance, it demonstrated poor predictive ability for both RBC transfusion (AUC 0.514, 95% CI 0.475-0.552) and adverse ED outcomes (AUC 0.525, 95% CI 0.468-0.563). For predicting RBC transfusion, GBS demonstrated the highest discriminative performance (AUC 0.795), followed by NEWS2 (0.601), MEWS (0.570), and AIMS65 (0.514). Similarly, for predicting adverse ED outcomes, GBS showed the highest AUC (0.664), followed by NEWS2 (0.655), MEWS (0.623), and AIMS65 (0.525). CONCLUSIONS Among the scores assessed in this study cohort, GBS showed the highest discriminative point estimates for predicting both RBC transfusion requirement and adverse ED outcomes, although overall predictive accuracy was modest, and AIMS65 showed no significant association with either outcome.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence in Valvular Heart Disease: Imaging, Quantification, Risk Prediction, and Potential Clinical Decision Support.

abstract.text: Valvular heart disease (VHD) affects a substantial proportion of the population and remains a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality worldwide. Despite advances in surgical and transcatheter therapies, important challenges persist. VHD remains underdiagnosed, assessment of disease severity is often variable, and the optimal timing of intervention continues to evolve. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising tool across the spectrum of VHD care. AI-based electrocardiogram analysis can identify both existing and future VHD, while AI-guided point-of-care ultrasound extends screening to nonspecialist settings. Across multimodality imaging, machine learning (ML) and deep learning algorithms enable automated, reproducible assessment of VHD. In echocardiography, AI supports grading of disease severity across the main valvular lesions, including Doppler interpretation and automated report generation. AI-enhanced cardiac magnetic resonance facilitates automated assessment of ventricular remodeling and myocardial fibrosis, while AI-assisted cardiac computed tomography improves procedural planning for transcatheter interventions. In parallel, ML has identified distinct patient phenotypes in multiple valvular lesions with differing clinical trajectories and responses to intervention. This review summarizes current applications of AI in detection, multimodality imaging, and potential clinical decision support for VHD and discusses opportunities and challenges for integration into routine practice.

articles.title: Overnight stay in the emergency department and mortality in sepsis patients.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Sepsis management in the emergency department (ED) faces challenges due to overcrowding and prolonged boarding, yet the impact of overnight ED stays on outcomes remains unclear. This study evaluated whether sepsis patients who spend a night in the ED waiting for admission to a ward/intensive care unit (ICU) are at increased risk of in-hospital mortality or morbidity.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This was a retrospective cohort study of sepsis patients who visited the ED and were admitted to the hospital between January 2021 and August 2024 across the ED of a large general hospital in China. Patients were stratified into an overnight ED stay (midnight-8:00 AM) and a non-overnight (admitted to a ward/ICUs before midnight) group. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality; secondary outcomes included septic shock, ICU admission, invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) and length of stay (LOS). Multivariable logistic regression and sensitivity analyses were used to compare end points between groups.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 1,208 sepsis patients were enrolled in the study, including 503 (42%) female and 705 (58%) male, with 624 (51.7%) in the overnight ED stay group and 584 (48.3%) in the non-overnight ED stay group. Baseline characteristics were balanced between groups. Unadjusted in-hospital mortality was similar (21.2% vs. 21.7%; risk difference (RD) 0.59 [-4.04 to 5.23]). Adjusted logistic regression analyses confirmed no mortality association (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) (95% confidence interval (CI)), 1.090 [0.805-1.477]; P = 0.579). No higher risk was observed for secondary outcomes: septic shock (aOR (95% CI), 1.020 [0.747-1.393]; P = 0.903), ICU admission (aOR 1.362 [0.983-1.895]; P = 0.064), or IMV (aOR (95% CI), 1.048 [0.710-1.549]; P = 0.813). Compliance with the Surviving Sepsis Campaign (SSC) guidelines was comparable between groups(31.6% vs. 29.1%; RD, -2.46 [-7.63 to 2.73]). These findings were consistent across subgroups and sensitivity analyses.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this retrospective cohort study, overnight ED boarding was not associated with increased in-hospital mortality or morbidity among sepsis patients when care adhered to SSC guidelines. These results suggest that high compliance with the SSC 1-h bundle may help mitigate potential risks associated with overnight ED boarding.

articles.title: An Emergency Department and Emergency Medical Services Superutilizer - A Case Report of a Multidisciplinary Approach to Resolution.
articles.journal: J Am Coll Emerg Physicians Open
articles.journal_full: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians open

abstract.text: Frequent emergency department (ED) visitors, referred to as high-need, high-cost, or "superutilizers," are a challenging population for the health care system. Superutilizers account for a disproportionate share of overall health care spending (5% of the population accounts for 50% of health care spending) and have therefore been a focus of research and intervention over the past decade. Although ED superutilizers have been described previously, we report a case that demonstrates the additional strain on the emergency medical services (EMS). A 65-year-old woman was the highest 9-1-1 caller for a major metropolitan area, averaging 1.6 transports per day. Identifying the root causes of a patient's frequent utilization can be difficult and sometimes requires stepping back, gaining a fresh perspective, or returning to basic questions, including "why is this patient failing home therapy?" In this case, undetected cognitive impairment was a significant contributor to her frequent utilization. A hospital/EMS paramedicine partnership facilitated detection and care for this root cause and stopped the frequent ED and 9-1-1 use. This case highlights the impact of superutilizers on EMS, the promising role of intervention teams, and the complexity of cognition/capacity determination in the ED.

articles.title: Candidate biomarkers predicting clinical outcome after hyperbaric oxygen against chronic radiation cystitis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Hyperbaric oxygen (HBO2) is effective against radiation cystitis. In this exploratory analysis we employed proteomics to assess biomarkers predicting clinical efficacy and the pharmacodynamics of HBO2 in radiation cystitis.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Global quantitative proteomics was performed on biopsies taken before and after HBO2 in patients with radiation cystitis from the RICH-ART trial (NCT01659723). The proteome of HBO2 responders (R) was compared to non-responders (NR) and between R and NR at baseline. Immunohistochemistry was employed to assess the expression of potential biomarkers in urinary bladder biopsies. Biological processes were identified by using the STRING database.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among proteins more expressed in R than NR at baseline were neutrophil defensin 1 and less expressed were chymase and mast cell carboxypeptidase A (CPA3). Among processes differentiating R from NR at baseline were processes regulating translation and complement activation. The top enriched biological processes in NR after HBO2 were processes regulating antigen processing and presentation. Only a few processes were affected by HBO2 in responders. No significant differences in the number of chymase+, CPA3 + and tryptase+ mast cells were observed in bladder specimens between R and NR before and after HBO2. The staining intensity of tryptase, chymase, CPA3 and complement factors C3, C4 and C8 were similar between R and NR and after HBO2.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Multiple processes regulating the immune system, complement activation and translation in radiation cystitis are changed after HBO2. However, only a few processes were associated with the clinical efficacy of HBO2. The involvement of mast cells in the pathogenesis of radiation cystitis is suggested.

articles.title: [How should a prehospital tourniquet be managed in Swedish hospitals?].

abstract.text: Tourniquets are life-saving in severe extremity hemorrhage but may cause serious complications if misused. The absence of Swedish national guidelines for handling prehospital tourniquets in emergency departments leads to clinical uncertainty and patient safety risks. Prehospital tourniquet use reduces mortality and transfusion needs without increasing risk of amputation if applied for less than two hours. However, overuse and prolonged tourniquet duration increase the ischemic injury and risk of severe systemic complications. In-hospital management should prioritize patient physiology and follow structured protocols, particularly in mass casualty settings. Early conversion to alternative methods of bleeding control or distal reduction of the tourniquet can minimize ischemia in selected stable patients. Hemodynamically unstable patients, prolonged tourniquet duration or suspected major vascular injury require urgent surgical management.

articles.title: Pediatric Penetrating Neck Injury Complicated by Significant Subcutaneous Emphysema in Rural Australia.

abstract.text: Although uncommon in the pediatric population, penetrating neck injuries (PNIs) in children carry a high risk of morbidity and mortality. This is due to the concentration of major blood vessels and organs within the neck, making them vulnerable to severe injury even when external wounds appear minor. Management strategies have evolved from traditional mandatory surgical exploration to a more selective approach based on clinical assessment and imaging. Here, we present the case of a three-year-old boy from a remote and rural region of Australia who sustained a small penetrating injury to zone I of the anterior neck. Despite being clinically stable at initial presentation, he rapidly deteriorated, developing significant and expanding subcutaneous emphysema. The patient was successfully managed with airway stabilization via fiberoptic bronchoscopy and transfer to a tertiary center for surgical exploration. This case emphasizes the unique challenges of managing PNIs in rural and remote health care settings, where care is complicated by geographical isolation, limited access to specialist services, and the need to achieve clinical stability before aeromedical retrieval. It also highlights the importance of continuous monitoring and reassessment to recognize clinical deterioration in these high-risk patients.

articles.title: The clinical and economic burden of rare-earth magnet ingestion in children: A national study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: We aimed to determine the case load and morbidities of magnet ingestion-related injuries in children of Qatar, as well as the medical costs associated.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We reviewed the medical records for cases seen in Qatar from 2011 to 2024 across two tertiary care centers.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 37/45 (82.2%) cases admitted required intervention, while 8/45 (17.7%) needed none. 20/37 (62.5%) underwent laparotomy, 4/37 (12.5%) underwent laparoscopy as the sole or combined modality, and 4/37 (12.5%) had endoscopic removal. Post-intervention complications were reported in 9/37 cases (28.1%), including superficial wound infection (5/32), collection (3/32), adhesive bowel obstruction (1/32), and incisional hernia (1/32). No deaths were seen. In logistic regression, presence of symptoms was the only predictor for the need of intervention (odds ratio [OR] 7.09 [95% confidence interval, CI 1.23-40.75]). The total cost of care for 39 patients seen was USD 524,660.87 for a total of 229 hospital days, with a median hospital related cost per patient of USD 7901.96 (interquartile range [IQR] 3922.06, 13,699.88). Costs associated with observation only were about a fifth of that where intervention was needed (a median of USD 2056.92 per patient (IQR 1074.46, 2658.53) versus USD 10,564.37 per patient (IQR 6374.11, 14,899.4) respectively). Costs related to use of operating room and inpatient admission contributed the most, compared to medications and emergency care.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Magnet ingestion in children in Qatar carries a significant morbidity and has significant hospital-related costs. Policymakers should consider product recall to reduce these effects. Raising public awareness of the hazards and limiting access to strong magnets in toys would be important prevention steps.

articles.title: Analgesic and clinical side effects of paracetamol and meloxicam in female dogs after elective ovariectomy or ovariohysterectomy - randomized clinical trial.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: This prospective, randomized, blinded, controlled clinical trial aimed at comparing the analgesic and antihyperalgesic effect of paracetamol and meloxicam following elective ovariectomy or ovariohysterectomy in healthy female dogs. In addition, it aimed at evaluating gastrointestinal side effects up to 48 h after surgery. Standardised anaesthesia protocol was utilised in all dogs and, at the end of the surgery, either meloxicam (0.2 mg/kg, Group M, n = 15 dogs) or paracetamol (10 mg/kg, Group P, n = 15 dogs) was administered intravenously. Pain was evaluated at 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 h after the administration of either paracetamol or meloxicam using short form of Glasgow composite pain scale (GCPS-SF). Rescue analgesia with intravenous methadone (0.2 mg/kg) was administered in case of ≥ 6 over 24 points. The success rate of each treatment was calculated based on the need of rescue analgesia within 6 h after surgery. Subsequently, the success rate was assessed for non-inferiority between treatments. The non-inferiority margin was set as -33%. Mechanical nociceptive thresholds and sensitivity to Von Frey filaments were tested at 2, 4 and 6 h after the administration either paracetamol or meloxicam. Once discharged, animals were remotely evaluated through a standardized questionnaire.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Rescue analgesia was administered at the hospital during the 6-hour post-operative period in a total of 15 dogs without difference between groups (p = 0.358). The success rate for analgesia was (9/15) 60% and (6/15) 40% in group M and P, respectively. The lower limit of the 95% CI of the difference for success rate (-55%, 15.5%) was lower than the margin set for non-inferiority (-33%) and therefore the non-inferiority of the group P versus group M was not confirmed. Mechanical sensitivity increased in both group after surgery. Mild self-limiting gastrointestinal side effects were detected in both groups.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Dogs receiving paracetamol needed more rescue analgesia than dogs receiving meloxicam in the post-operative period. The rate of success with both drugs was lower than expected. Frequent assessment of pain is mandatory to ensure efficient analgesia also beyond the first post-operative day and future studies are warranted to validate methods for out-of-hospital pain assessment.

articles.title: Global, regional, and national burden of non-communicable diseases among adolescents and young adults from 1990 to 2021, with global projections to 2035.

abstract.text: This study estimated the global, regional, and national burden of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) among adolescents and young adults aged 10-24 years during 1990-2021. Temporal trends were assessed using average annual percentage changes, and Spearman's rank correlation evaluated associations between age-standardized rates and the Socio-demographic Index (SDI). Autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) models were applied to project global age-standardized rates of mortality, disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), and years lived with disability (YLDs) through 2035. In 2021, NCDs accounted for approximately 404.87 thousand deaths, 129.49 million DALYs, and 100.62 million YLDs in this population. Neoplasms and cardiovascular diseases were the leading causes of NCD-related death, whereas mental disorders were the predominant source of non-fatal burden. Mortality declined in both absolute numbers and age-standardized rates during 1990-2021, whereas absolute DALYs and YLDs increased despite modest reductions or stability in age-standardized rates. Age-standardized DALY and YLD rates were higher in females, but mortality rates were higher in males. In 2021, age-standardized mortality rates were strongly negatively correlated with SDI at the country level (ρ =- 0.80, P < 0.001), whereas YLD rates showed a moderate positive correlation (ρ = 0.56, P < 0.001). ARIMA projections indicated continued declines in mortality through 2035, with DALY rates remaining stable and YLD rates declining modestly toward pre-pandemic levels. Conclusion: Despite mortality reductions, non-fatal NCD burden driven by mental disorders continues to rise. Marked disparities persist by sex and SDI levels, with high-SDI regions facing escalating disability burden and low-SDI regions confronting elevated mortality. Targeted interventions are urgently needed to advance Sustainable Development Goal Target 3.4.

articles.title: Neonatal bilirubin neurotoxicity: An emergency response framework from referral to follow-up.

abstract.text: A neonate with a total serum bilirubin at or approaching the exchange transfusion threshold represents a life-threatening neurologic emergency that demands a coordinated, time-critical response. The 2022 American Academy of Pediatrics clinical practice guideline revision formally defines an escalation-of-care threshold at 2 mg/dL below the exchange transfusion threshold to trigger prompt, aggressive therapeutic interventions. However, the vast majority of extreme hyperbilirubinemia cases undergo triage in low-resource or community settings, such as outpatient pediatric clinics, general emergency departments, or level I/II nurseries. These settings often lack the specialized capabilities required to perform an emergency exchange transfusion. Consequently, clinical outcomes and long-term neurodevelopmental prognoses depend on rapid recognition of transfer criteria, immediate initiation of temporizing management at the referring site, and stabilization during transport. This review has been developed at an academic level IV neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) and translates AAP guidelines into an actionable, role-specific protocol for referring clinicians, transport teams, receiving NICU staff, and institutional quality bodies. Emphasis is placed on immediate treatment at first clinical contact, specifically continuous intensive phototherapy and intravenous hydration within minutes rather than delaying until arrival at a higher-level center, alongside parallel exchange transfusion preparation, standardized neurologic assessment, proactive family counseling, and institutional follow-up.

articles.title: Dust Storm-Associated Pediatric Allergic Morbidity in Primary Care in Chicago, Illinois.

abstract.text: We examined the effect of a rare Midwestern dust storm on pediatric allergic morbidity in a Chicago, Illinois primary care setting. As climate and land-use changes expand the geographic range of dust storm activity, primary care clinicians will increasingly encounter environmentally triggered asthma and allergy exacerbations. We performed a retrospective analysis of daily clinic visits before and after the May 16, 2025 dust storm and observed an increase in allergy-related visits, with a significant increase in the first 3 days after the storm. Visit diagnoses included eczema, asthma/reactive airway disease, allergic rhinitis, allergic conjunctivitis, allergic dermatitis, and seasonal allergies. By focusing on primary care rather than emergency department visits, this work highlights the broader burden of dust-related allergic morbidity in the pediatric population. These findings underscore the need for primary care preparedness and community-level mitigation strategies as extreme weather events become more frequent.

articles.title: Association of Early Palliative Care with End-of-Life Care Quality and Nonbeneficial Treatments in Taiwan: A Nationwide Population-Based Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Early palliative care has been associated with reduced aggressive care near the end of life (EOL), particularly among patients with cancer. However, evidence regarding the association between early palliative care and potentially nonbeneficial treatments near the EOL remains limited, particularly among patients with noncancer terminal illnesses and in real-world clinical practice.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To examine the association between early palliative care, EOL care quality indicators, and nonbeneficial treatments among terminally ill cancer and noncancer patients under a universal health insurance system.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective population-based study used Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database to identify adults who received palliative care within one year before death in 2019. Early palliative care was defined as initiation of any palliative care service more than 90 days before death. Outcomes included indicators of EOL care quality and nonbeneficial treatments within the last 30 days of life. Multivariable logistic and linear regression models were used to adjust for demographic characteristics, comorbidities, and terminal diagnoses.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 46,343 decedents, 17.2% received early palliative care. Early palliative care was associated with lower odds of aggressive EOL care, including more than one emergency department visit, more than one hospitalization, a hospital stay exceeding 14 days, intensive care unit admission, in-hospital death, use of an endotracheal tube, ventilator support, and cardiopulmonary resuscitation. Early palliative care was also associated with reduced use of nonbeneficial treatments, including blood transfusion and tube feeding or intravenous nutrition.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In a nationwide cohort, early palliative care was associated with improved EOL care quality and reduced use of nonbeneficial treatments among terminally ill patients. These findings underscore the clinical importance of earlier palliative care involvement in supporting patient-centered decision making near the EOL and reducing potentially nonbeneficial interventions.

articles.title: Fitness to dive referrals to UK defence occupational medicine for obstructive spirometry in service divers 2015-2024: a retrospective cohort study.
Advanced Age in Acute Myocardial Infarction-Related Cardiogenic Shock by Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Status.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Cardiogenic shock (CS) remains a leading cause of in-hospital mortality in acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Although advanced age is associated with worse outcomes, associations across out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) strata remain incompletely characterized.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: The objective of the study was to evaluate the association between octogenarian status and in-hospital mortality in patients with AMI-related CS (AMI-CS) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and to examine this association in analyses stratified by OHCA status.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We analyzed patients with AMI-CS enrolled in the multicenter Kanagawa-ACuTe cardIoVascular rEgistry who underwent PCI. Octogenarian status (≥80 years) was the primary exposure. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate associations with in-hospital mortality, with additional analyses stratified by OHCA status.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 658 patients, 177 (26.9%) were octogenarians, and 279 (42.4%) died during hospitalization. Octogenarian status was independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality (adjusted OR: 2.14; 95% CI: 1.32-3.48; P = 0.002). In stratified analyses, octogenarian status was associated with higher mortality among patients without OHCA, whereas no statistically significant association was observed among those with OHCA. The interaction between octogenarian status and OHCA was not statistically significant (P for interaction = 0.422). Higher heart rate, unmeasurable heart rate, higher serum creatinine, and lower serum albumin were independently associated with mortality.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In patients with AMI-CS undergoing PCI, octogenarian status was independently associated with in-hospital mortality. Although estimates differed numerically across OHCA strata, the interaction was not statistically significant, precluding a conclusion that the association differed according to OHCA status. These stratified findings should therefore be regarded as hypothesis-generating. Chronological age should be considered within a comprehensive clinical assessment rather than in isolation.

articles.title: Severity-Based Triage for Direct Transportation to Nearest Comprehensive Stroke Center: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: The efficacy of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion (LVO) is time dependent. Patients initially transported to a primary stroke center (PSC) may require secondary transfer, potentially delaying EVT. For severely affected patients, bypassing the PSC for direct transport to a comprehensive stroke center may expedite EVT but risks delaying IV thrombolysis. Effects of prehospital bypass strategies on functional outcomes are thus uncertain.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: For this systematic review and meta-analysis, PubMed and Web of Science were searched until December 2025. Randomized and nonrandomized studies comparing transport to the nearest stroke center with transport to a more distant comprehensive stroke center in patients with suspected stroke were included. Two investigators independently screened records, selected eligible studies, extracted summary data, and assessed risk of bias. Random-effects meta-analysis was used to quantify associations between prehospital bypass, endovascular therapy, and functional outcomes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Literature search identified 1,991 distinct reports. Of 18 eligible studies, 2 were randomized controlled trials (RCTs, n = 1,540 patients), 11 before-after studies (n = 11,837), and 5 cross-sectional studies (n = 1,139), comprising a total of 14,516 patients (52% men/48% women). Risk of bias was high in nonrandomized studies. Patients undergoing prehospital bypass and control patients had similar likelihoods of receiving EVT (odds ratio [OR] 1.52, 95% CI 0.98-2.35) or thrombolysis (OR 1.12, 0.92-1.35). Prehospital bypass was associated with earlier groin puncture (median difference -63.9 minutes, 95% CI -84.1 to -43.7). Time to needle in bypass patients was longer than in control patients in RCTs (median delay 34 minutes, 23.1-44.9 minutes), but similar in nonrandomized studies. Functional independence (modified Rankin Scale 0-2) at 90 days was more frequent in bypass patients (OR 1.23, 1.04-1.45). In patients with intracerebral hemorrhage, bypass was associated with increased mortality (risk ratio 1.30, 1.02-1.64).

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: For patients with LVO stroke, benefits of expedited thrombectomy may outweigh possible risks associated with longer prehospital transport times. However, evidence is insufficient to recommend the routine implementation of prehospital bypass protocols. Further research is needed to determine circumstances under which direct access to comprehensive stroke centers should be prioritized for patients with severe stroke symptoms.

articles.title: Climate, Air Quality, and Emergency Department Use in Northern Germany: Protocol for a Multicenter Register Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Climate change threatens population health through temperature extremes, air pollution, and altered infectious disease patterns. Emergency departments (EDs) are sensitive indicators of climate-related health impacts; however, comprehensive multicenter investigations integrating meteorological factors, air quality, and infectious disease surveillance across different health care provision levels remain scarce in Germany, particularly in maritime climate regions.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study aims to characterize the impact of meteorological factors, air quality, and infectious disease dynamics on ED presentations across multiple health care facilities and care provision levels in northern Germany over an 11-year period.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective, multicenter, observational study will examine ED presentations across 4 facilities representing different care provision levels in the greater Lübeck area and southeastern Schleswig-Holstein, Germany, from January 2014 to December 2024. Clinical data, including ICD (International Classification of Diseases)-coded diagnoses, patient demographics, and temporal information, will be linked with meteorological data from the German Weather Service, air quality measurements from state environmental monitoring, and infectious disease surveillance from the Robert Koch Institute. The primary outcomes will be daily ED visits overall and stratified by disease category (cardiovascular, respiratory, psychiatric, infectious, renal, neurological, and surgical/traumatic). Distributed lag nonlinear models within a generalized additive modeling framework will be used to characterize temperature-health relationships, accounting for delayed and nonlinear effects, and adjusted for temporal trends, seasonality, and infectious disease incidence. Subgroup analyses will examine vulnerable populations by age, sex, and socioeconomic status.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Project planning and conceptualization began in June 2024, and ethical approval was granted in July 2025. Following approval, clinical data were transferred sequentially across participating sites in July 2025, August 2025, and October 2025. Data from 3 of the 4 participating hospitals have been successfully received, while the final outstanding dataset is expected in the second half of 2026. Meteorological data collection was completed in October 2025 and air quality data in January 2026. While preliminary descriptive statistical analyses have already commenced, inferential statistics will be performed once data collection is fully completed.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This multicenter study will provide systematic evidence on climate-sensitive ED utilization in a maritime climate region of northern Germany. By integrating clinical, meteorological, air quality, and infectious disease data across 4 hospitals of varying care complexity, the study is well positioned to characterize nonlinear and delayed health effects of temperature extremes across a broad spectrum of acute conditions. Results are expected to inform regional health care capacity planning, early warning systems, and public health preparedness, while contributing to the broader evidence base on climate and health.

articles.title: Berta, an Open-Source, Modular AI Scribe for Clinical Documentation: Implementation Report.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Clinical documentation is a major contributor to physician workload and burnout, particularly in high-acuity settings such as emergency departments. Ambient AI scribes have emerged as a response, but commercial products cost US $99 to more than US $600 per physician per month, operate as opaque systems, and often process data on vendor-controlled infrastructure. These characteristics limit organizational control over data sovereignty, quality improvement, and clinical workflows and create barriers to adoption in resource-constrained settings.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: We aimed to develop an open-source, modular AI scribe platform that could be deployed entirely within institutional infrastructure, and to evaluate its real-world use across a provincial health system.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We developed Berta, an open-source, modular platform that pairs a Next.js front end and a FastAPI back end with configurable automatic speech recognition and large language model components. A closed-source implementation developed in parallel with Berta was deployed at Alberta Health Services (AHS), Canada's largest provincially integrated health system at the time of implementation, and operated within AHS's existing Snowflake AI Data Cloud infrastructure. All clinical audio and text remained within the secure AHS environment. Use and session metadata were automatically recorded during routine clinical use by emergency physicians across AHS between November 2024 and July 2025, and physicians were emailed an optional survey. Operating costs were estimated from Snowflake service consumption over the same period.

abstract.label: UNLABELLED
abstract.text: During the 9-month study period, 197 emergency physicians registered at 105 urban and rural facilities used the system, generating 21,548 clinical sessions and more than 2700 hours of audio. Monthly session volume grew from 675 sessions in November 2024 to 5463 in July 2025. Mean recorded session length was 7.6 minutes, and 42% (82/197) of users customized at least 1 documentation template. Operating costs averaged less than US $30 per physician per month, representing a 70% to 95% reduction in cost compared with commercial subscription prices; this comparison excludes personnel costs for development and maintenance. Survey respondents (69-73 per item) rated user-friendliness as good (median 5, IQR 4-6), reported a median time saving of 16 to 30 (IQR 0-15 to 46-60) minutes per shift, and rated documentation quality the lowest. After the pilot, access was opened to other departments, and by September 30, 2026, approximately 2000 users had registered.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: An in-house AI scribe can be deployed at provincial scale within existing health system infrastructure at a fraction of the operating cost of commercial alternatives while preserving data sovereignty and institutional control. The full cost of ownership and documentation quality require further evaluation. By releasing Berta publicly, we provide a reproducible foundation that health systems can adapt to evaluate and deploy AI documentation technology within their own secure environments.

articles.title: Prehospital Whole Blood Resuscitation in Pediatric Patients: A San Antonio Cohort Descriptive.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: The objective of this study is to describe the demographic, clinical, and prehospital care characteristics of pediatric patients receiving whole blood (WB) resuscitation by San Antonio Fire Department (SAFD).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted an observational retrospective cohort study to evaluate pediatric patients who received prehospital low-titer group O positive WB transfusion through the SAFD prehospital blood program between October 2018 and June 2025. The objective was to characterize patient demographics, injury patterns, resuscitative interventions, shock physiology, and outcomes among pediatric recipients in a mature civilian emergency medical services WB program.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 1703 WB transfusions, 73 (4.3%) were pediatric. Most patients were male (76%), age range 1-17 years old with a mode of 17 years, adolescents represented 78%. Trauma accounted for 96% of cases, firearm injury (74%); all penetrating (84%), blunt (12%), with the remainder classified as medical/unknown. Vascular access was intravenous (73%), intraosseous (26%). Tranexamic acid was co-administered in 39%; 12% received ceftriaxone. When analyzed using age-adjusted Shock Index Pediatric Age-Adjusted (SIPA) thresholds (>1.2 for 1-6 years, >1.0 for 7-12 years, and >0.9 for 13-17 years), based on the initial available prehospital heart rate and systolic blood pressure, 45% of patients had an elevated SIPA, 22% had a normal SIPA, 20% were pulseless and therefore could not undergo SIPA calculation, and 14% lacked sufficient vital-sign data for classification. Survival was 50%; died 39%, and unknown outcomes 11%. Mean delta shock index values were most negative in toddlers (1-4 years) -0.97 ± 1.29, followed by children (5-11 years) -0.76 ± 1.07 and adolescents (12-17 years) -0.16 ± 0.46, indicating a greater physiologic response to resuscitation among younger pediatric patients.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Pediatric WB recipients were predominantly adolescent males who sustained penetrating trauma and presented with moderate-to-severe shock. Younger age groups had larger descriptive decreases in shock index during the prehospital encounter; however, these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the small subgroup sizes and observational design.

articles.title: A novel diagnostic method for carbon monoxide poisoning using body cavity fluids other than blood.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Carboxyhemoglobin saturation (COHb%) in blood is essential for diagnosing carbon monoxide (CO) poisoning; however, postmortem blood is not always available. Few previous studies have investigated substitutes for blood. We determined whether body cavity fluids could substitute for blood using a simple method to concentrate low-Hb samples.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We selected autopsy cases with measurable COHb% in blood and body cavity fluids (pleural fluid, pericardial fluid, ascites, and bile). They were classified based on the presence of CO poisoning and decomposition, and where they were discovered. COHb% was measured using a CO-oximeter, and correlations between COHb% in blood and the corresponding body cavity fluids were examined. Low-Hb samples were concentrated using ultrafiltration filters.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: COHb% was measured in 55 cases for pleural fluid, 43 cases for pericardial fluid, 4 cases for ascites, and 1 case for bile. In non-putrefied cases, COHb% in pleural and pericardial fluid showed significant correlations with those in blood. Ascites exhibited a similar trend. In putrefied cases with CO poisoning, correlations were unclear because of emergence outliers and the limited sample size. In putrefied non-CO poisoning cases, COHb% was rather higher, reaching 12% in bodies recovered on land and 48% in those recovered from water.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The concentration method was useful for analyzing low-Hb samples. COHb% in pleural and pericardial fluids may serve supportive information for estimating CO inhalation, with careful consideration of analytical characteristics of CO oximeters, putrefaction, and sample conditions. In decomposed cases found in water, body cavity fluids were not suitable for diagnosis.

articles.title: Hospital cost structures and resource utilisation across representative treatment pathways relevant to complex orthopaedic infection care: a nationwide DRG-based analysis in Germany.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Implant-associated orthopaedic infections require prolonged inpatient treatment, repeated surgery and multidisciplinary care, yet nationwide evidence on how hospital resources are distributed across clinically distinct treatment pathways is limited. This study characterised hospital-side case costs, resource utilisation and aggregate expenditure across representative German diagnosis-related groups (DRGs) relevant to complex orthopaedic infection care.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Publicly available 2024 data from the German Institute for the Hospital Remuneration System (InEK) were analysed. Twelve representative DRGs were selected a priori from official definitions and diagnostic/procedural profiles and grouped into six treatment pathways. The InEK cost matrix reflects standardised hospital-side resource costs from participating calculation hospitals and does not represent actual DRG reimbursement. National case frequencies, length of stay and mean case costs were analysed using frequency-weighted pathway estimates, while pathway-level cost composition was calculated from aggregate component expenditure.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The included DRGs represented 36,212 hospitalisations and €305.2 million in aggregate annual hospital-side expenditure represented by the selected DRGs. Mean hospital-side costs ranged from €5,859 to €22,495 per case. Ward care accounted for approximately 34-69% of pathway expenditure; operating theatre services contributed up to 39% in revision arthroplasty. Geriatric rehabilitation generated the largest aggregate expenditure (€119.0 million; 39.0%) because of high case volume, whereas complex vacuum-assisted wound care had the highest per-case cost but only 2.9% of aggregate expenditure. At the aggregated DRG level, mean length of stay was associated with mean case cost (Pearson r = 0.87, 95% CI 0.60-0.96; P < 0.001); leave-one-out correlations ranged from r = 0.79 to r = 0.96.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Resource requirements differ markedly across representative DRG pathways relevant to complex orthopaedic infection care. Because the selected DRGs are not infection-exclusive, the reported expenditure should not be interpreted as the national economic burden of implant-associated orthopaedic infection. The findings may inform hospital resource planning and future cost-revenue analyses.

articles.title: Elevated Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio Predicts Early Aggravation of Organ Dysfunction in Septic Patients in the Emergency Department.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To investigate whether neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), a simple marker of immune dysregulation, is associated with early organ dysfunction progression in emergency department (ED) patients with sepsis.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Exploratory secondary analysis of observational clustering cohort.

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: Single-center ED.

abstract.label: PATIENTS/SUBJECTS
abstract.text: Among 999 patients with adjudicated infection, 364 fulfilled Sepsis-3 criteria for sepsis or septic shock and had available Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) scores at admission and 24 hours.

abstract.label: INTERVENTIONS
abstract.text: None.

abstract.label: MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS
abstract.text: Organ dysfunction trajectory was defined according to the evolution in SOFA score during the first 24 hours (ΔSOFA) and categorized as improving (ΔSOFA ≤ -2), stable (ΔSOFA -1 to +1), or worsening (ΔSOFA ≥ +2). Of the 364 patients, 135 (37%) were classified as improving, 187 (51%) as stable, and 42 (12%) as worsening. NLR differed significantly across trajectory groups, with median values of 12 (7-21), 12 (7-22), and 23 (10-37), respectively (p = 0.015). In multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, lactate concentration, and baseline SOFA score, NLR remained independently associated with worsening organ dysfunction trajectory (odds ratio [OR] 5.55, 95% CI, 1.86-18.18; p = 0.003). Patients with worsening trajectories more frequently required ICU admission (26% vs. 5% vs. 4%; p < 0.001) and experienced higher 28-day mortality (36% vs 17% vs 17%; p = 0.013).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: NLR was independently associated with early worsening of organ dysfunction in ED patients with sepsis. Beyond its prognostic value, NLR may provide complementary information to conventional severity assessment by reflecting immune dysregulation.

articles.title: Univariate Time Series Forecasting of ED Admissions and Hospital Discharges with Prophet and Azure Databricks MLflow.
articles.journal_full: Journal of healthcare management / American College of Healthcare Executives

abstract.label: GOAL
abstract.text: Bed capacity is a key limitation for patient throughput at high trauma-level hospitals. By leveraging existing operational data and incorporating relatively simple quantitative methodology, future bed balancing can be predicted primarily via forecasting of incoming ED admissions and hospital discharges. These predictions can inform a number of key decisions related to bed planning, potentially enhancing provider satisfaction and mitigating negative patient outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Univariate time series forecasting with the Prophet procedure was applied to generate daily forecasts of admissions and discharges over a 28-day period at Vanderbilt University Adult Hospital in Nashville, Tennessee, the largest facility within the Vanderbilt University Medical Center system. Models for ED admissions and hospital discharges were each developed independently as custom-built and Automated Machine Learning (AutoML)-produced models, respectively.

abstract.label: PRINCIPAL FINDINGS
abstract.text: Both models performed well in terms of accurately producing 28-day forecasts, compared to naive alternatives, and were expected to improve as historical data become more available. Although these models were limited by a lack of consistent data availability due to the emergency response during the COVID-19 pandemic years, they were effective in improving the accuracy of bed balancing estimates by hospital operations staff with relative ease, regarding model development and operational application.

abstract.label: PRACTICAL APPLICATIONS
abstract.text: Although simple, univariate models benefit from relatively trivial data requirements and adequate time to implement operationally. This cost-effective approach provides an effective solution for health systems seeking to support bed-planning efforts.

articles.title: Ketamine Vs. Etomidates and Cardiovascular Collapse During Emergency Tracheal Intubation: A Secondary Analysis of the DEVICE and PREOXI Trials.

abstract.label: IMPORTANCE
abstract.text: Emergency tracheal intubation in critically ill adults is a high-risk procedure.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To evaluate associations of ketamine vs. etomidate with cardiovascular collapse and other peri-intubation outcomes.

abstract.label: DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: Secondary analysis of individual-participant data from the DEVICE and PREOXI trials, treating induction medication as an observational exposure. The cohort included 2357 adults intubated in emergency departments or ICUs; 1822 received etomidate, 312 ketamine, and 223 other induction regimens.

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES
abstract.text: The primary outcome was cardiovascular collapse, defined as new or increased vasopressor use, nadir systolic blood pressure below 65 mm Hg, or cardiac arrest between induction and 2 minutes after intubation. Secondary outcomes included severe hypoxemia (oxygen saturation < 80%) and procedural outcomes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In weighted analyses, cardiovascular collapse occurred in 14.0% of etomidate recipients and 20.4% of ketamine recipients. In weighted, covariate-adjusted models, ketamine was associated with higher odds of cardiovascular collapse (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.80; 95% CI, 1.24-2.62) and new or increased vasopressor use (aOR, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.02-2.23), nominally lower odds of severe hypoxemia (aOR, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.28-0.88), and shorter modeled time to successful intubation (hazard ratio, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.02-1.33). The latter two associations were not significant after multiplicity adjustment. Estimates for systolic blood pressure below 65 mm Hg and cardiac arrest were too imprecise for reliable inference. Successful intubation on the first attempt and 28-day in-hospital mortality did not clearly differ between ketamine and etomidate.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE
abstract.text: Compared with etomidate, ketamine was associated with higher odds of cardiovascular collapse, primarily reflecting new or increased vasopressor use. Associations with severe hypoxemia and intubation time did not remain significant after multiplicity adjustment. Because induction medication was not randomized and residual confounding remains possible, these associations should not be interpreted as causal.

articles.title: A Case Report of Severe Leptospirosis After a Rat Bite in an Urban Setting.

abstract.text: A 21-year-old healthy male presented with a sepsis syndrome approximately 17 days after a wild urban rat bite. In the emergency room, he was initiated on piperacillin-tazobactam, and after receipt of the first dose, he developed worsening tachycardia, rigors, and hypoxia, followed by hypotension. Given the rodent exposure, the medical team suspected leptospirosis and attributed his decline to a Jarisch-Herxheimer (JH) reaction. A BioFire Global Fever Special Pathogens Panel was obtained the morning after admission and was positive for Leptospira DNA. A CDC lipL32 nucleic acid amplification test from admission was also positive, as was the microscopic agglutination testing (MAT) at 5 weeks. Notably, admission IgM and MAT results were negative. The patient received a 7-day course of ceftriaxone with resolution of most of his symptoms. Leptospirosis is a zoonotic infection typically acquired via exposure to water contaminated with the urine of infected animals, most commonly rodents. This case of severe leptospirosis contributes to the growing literature on leptospirosis occurring in association with rat bites and demonstrates that clinical suspicion combined with nucleic acid testing early in the disease course can enable rapid diagnosis.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of prehospital capillary high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I in patients with acute chest pain: the prospective multicenter VALIDATE study.
articles.journal_full: European journal of emergency medicine : official journal of the European Society for Emergency Medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) plays a central role in the diagnosis and management of non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI), including rule-out and rule-in strategies in the emergency department. Extending hs-cTnI testing to the prehospital setting could accelerate patient orientation and clinical decision-making, but the diagnostic performance of prehospital capillary hs-cTnI remains insufficiently studied.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
