abstract.text: The study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of prehospital capillary hs-cTnI for the diagnosis of NSTEMI at hospital discharge.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: The study is a prospective multicenter diagnostic accuracy study with blinded index test results.

abstract.label: SETTINGS AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: Four French emergency medical service systems with 10 mobile intensive care units. Adult patients presenting with acute chest pain were included.

abstract.label: INDEX TEST
abstract.text: Prehospital hs-cTnI measurement using a point-of-care device (Atellica VTLi) on capillary samples. Treating clinicians were blinded to hs-cTnI results.

abstract.label: OUTCOME MEASURES AND ANALYSIS
abstract.text: The primary outcome was the diagnostic performance of capillary hs-cTnI for the diagnosis of NSTEMI at hospital discharge. Diagnostic performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Clinically relevant thresholds were defined a priori based on predefined safety criteria.

abstract.label: MAIN RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 659 patients included in the primary analysis, 71 (10.8%) had NSTEMI. Prehospital capillary hs-cTnI demonstrated good diagnostic performance [area under the curve (AUC) = 0.83, 95% CI = 0.78-0.88]. A rule-out threshold of <2.2 ng/L, evaluated according to prespecified performance criteria, identified 7.1% of patients, with a negative predictive value of 1.00 (95% CI = 0.92-1.00). A rule-in threshold of >43.6 ng/L identified 6.5% of patients, with a positive predictive value of 0.65 (95% CI = 0.51-0.79). In the predefined sensitivity analysis, venous hs-cTnI showed similar diagnostic performance (AUC = 0.84, 95% CI = 0.79-0.89).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Prehospital capillary hs-cTnI showed good diagnostic performance for NSTEMI, although feasibility in routine practice was challenged by unavailable or uninterpretable measurements. Further external validation is warranted before implementation in prehospital diagnostic pathways.

articles.title: Neurological Pupil Index and Delirium at Emergency Department Presentation: A Retrospective Analysis of Prospectively Collected Data.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: We aimed primarily to examine the association between automated infrared pupillometry parameters, particularly the neurological pupil index (NPi), and delirium at emergency department presentation. The discriminative performance of NPi and its incremental value beyond clinical variables was evaluated as a secondary exploratory analysis.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective analysis included prospectively collected clinical data from patients aged ≥20 years who were transported by ambulance to a tertiary emergency department in Japan between April 1, 2023, and March 31, 2024. Delirium was assessed using the brief confusion assessment method (bCAM) during the initial emergency department evaluation. Automated infrared pupillometry parameters were obtained using an automated infrared pupillometer.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 1,121 patients, 225 (20.1%) had delirium at presentation. Patients with delirium were older and had a higher prevalence of dementia and psychiatric disease. Mean NPi was significantly lower in patients with delirium and remained independently associated with delirium after multivariable adjustment. In secondary exploratory discrimination analyses, NPi alone showed limited discriminative performance. The addition of NPi to the clinical model increased the area under the curve from 0.694 to 0.708, but this difference was not statistically significant (DeLong P = .170).

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Lower NPi values measured on emergency department arrival were independently associated with a subsequent bCAM-based delirium determination during the same early emergency department evaluation. However, in secondary exploratory analyses, +NPi showed limited discriminative performance and did not significantly improve discrimination when added to the clinical model. Therefore, the present findings do not support the use of automated infrared pupillometry as a stand-alone screening or diagnostic tool for delirium.

articles.title: A novel interprofessional experience caring for post-intensive care and long COVID patients: the optimal clinic experience.

abstract.text: This short report describes the development of an interprofessional ambulatory care clinic with an interprofessional education program at an academic medical center providing comprehensive care to patients previously hospitalized in the intensive care unit (ICU) or with COVID-19 from May 2020 to May 2026. The OPTIMAL Clinic (lOng COVID/PosT-Icu MultidisciplinAry cLinic) was created during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic, with limited staff and temporary funding. Our team consisted of clinical pharmacy and physician trainees, nurse practitioners, occupational therapists, physical therapists, pharmacists, physicians, and social workers, who collaborated strategically and synergistically to optimize patient care. Across repeated evaluations, the clinic model was associated with increased preventive care and financial sustainability, and decreased emergency department visits and unplanned hospitalizations. Our interprofessional education program achieved high ratings from trainees in preceptor support, onboarding, clinical activities, and interprofessional education. Our OPTIMAL clinic exemplifies a model for interprofessional care and education for the support of complex patients after ICU or COVID-19 hospitalizations.

articles.title: POCUS in cardiopulmonary resuscitation. Towards a new milestone.
Is cardiac arrest still a binary clinical diagnosis? Toward electro-mechanical-hemodynamic phenotyping in the era of point-of-care ultrasound.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Cardiac arrest (CA) remains operationally recognized through clinical signs of absent effective circulation and classified primarily by electrical rhythm. Point-of-care ultrasound (PoCUS) challenges this rhythm-pulse paradigm by directly revealing cardiac mechanical activity and, with Doppler, circulatory flow, exposing physiologically distinct states concealed within current CA categories.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This physiology-based conceptual manuscript proposes an integrated electro-mechanical-hemodynamic framework for CA and translates it into PoCUS-consistent phenotyping, portraying CA presentations (CA phenotypes) as pathophysiological states that may transition from one to another along a spontaneous or treatment-modified continuum.

abstract.label: CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS
abstract.text: The framework distinguishes three principal phenotypes: shockable CA (ventricular fibrillation/pulseless ventricular tachycardia); zero-flow CA, encompassing Asystole and PEA without organized ventricular contraction (S-PEA) or with agonal mechanical activity (A-PEA); and severe low-flow CA (C-PEA), in which organized ventricular contraction persists despite absent palpable pulse, and may generate residual circulation. PoCUS can define mechanical states, identify reversible causes, contextualize diagnostic findings, reveal occult shockable activity, and track phenotype transitions. Doppler and invasive arterial-pressure monitoring further characterize spontaneous flow and pressure and may support phenotype-informed treatment.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Electro-mechanical-hemodynamic phenotyping extends established ALS classification by providing a standardized physiological language for distinct CA states, enabling more homogeneous research populations, phenotype-specific resuscitation research, and rigorous evaluation of PoCUS-informed management. Taken together, these physiological distinctions provide a rationale for reconsidering how cardiac arrest is characterized and how PoCUS-derived information could inform future research, evidence reviews, and resuscitation recommendations.

articles.title: Clinical and Economic Impact of Non-Opioid Analgesia Guidelines in Pediatric Adenotonsillectomy: A Multi-Institutional Database Study.
articles.journal_full: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate the impact of the paradigm shift toward opioid-sparing analgesia following the 2019 AAO-HNS clinical practice guideline on postoperative complications and healthcare costs after pediatric adenotonsillectomy (AT).

abstract.label: STUDY DESIGN
abstract.text: Retrospective cohort study.

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: TriNetX, a multi-institutional federated electronic health record database.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Patients < 18 years old undergoing AT were stratified by surgical year: pre-2019 (Jan 2014-Dec 2017) or post-2019 (Jan 2021-Dec 2025). Opioid prescription data was recorded. Using 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM), the incidence of postoperative dehydration, hemorrhage, throat pain, intravenous (IV) fluid administration, and emergency department (ED) visits were compared. A number needed to treat (NNT) analysis was performed based on inflation-adjusted costs per ED visit to estimate economic cost savings.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Following 1:1 PSM (n = 66,844 per cohort), the pre-2019 cohort demonstrated significantly higher risk ratios (RR) of dehydration (1.27; 95% CI 1.17-1.38), IV fluid needs (1.27; 95% CI 1.17-1.37), ED visits (1.21; 95% CI 1.16-1.27), and nausea/vomiting (1.24; 95% CI 1.12-1.39) compared to the post-2019 cohort (P < .0001). Postoperative hemorrhage rates were statistically stable (P = .145). Post-2019 opioid prescriptions decreased significantly (RR 1.47; 95% CI 1.44-1.50; P < .0001), notably with a 25-fold reduction in codeine prescriptions. The NNT to prevent one ED visit was 101.7, resulting in an estimated cost avoidance of $3.2 million within the studied cohort.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The incidence of post-tonsillectomy dehydration, pain, and ED utilization has decreased over time, concomitant with decreased opioid prescribing, suggesting that opioid-sparing protocols have been consistent with broadly improved patient outcomes.

articles.title: Perceptions of Workplace Culture Among Emergency Physicians: Insights From In-Depth Interviews.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Recently, the PEOPLE+ (Philosophy, Economics, Operational, Providers, and Leadership) model improved performance metrics in an emergency department (ED). However, ED provider perceptions of current workplace culture compared with previous ED work experience were not explored.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Using descriptive phenomenology, 18 physicians participated in semi-structured interviews that underwent reflexive thematic analysis. Interviews included open-ended questions related to physicians' perceptions of the PEOPLE+ model compared with prior ED experiences.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Fifty-three codes about previous work culture and 61 codes about current culture were identified. Participants described previous work settings as profit-driven, understaffed, and individualistic, with limited leadership engagement and high turnover. These conditions were perceived to cause burnout, poor work-life balance, and decreased perceptions of support. The PEOPLE+ model was associated with positive perceptions across all domains, with participants reporting feeling valued, supported, and included in decision-making. Adequate staffing, fair scheduling, team-based care, and accessible leadership contributed to satisfaction and stability in the views of the participants.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The PEOPLE+ model's primary characteristic is being provider-centered, employing simultaneous changes to philosophic, economic, operational, leadership, and staffing models, and workplace culture was perceived as improved following employment of the model. Participants characterized a positive workplace culture as team-based with a nontraditional compensation model and leadership that embraces listening.

articles.title: Impact of a national ban on highly hazardous pesticides on suicide and agricultural productivity in Nepal.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Pesticide self-poisoning is a major contributor to suicide in low- and middle-income countries. Between 2019 and 2021, Nepal banned several highly hazardous pesticides and replaced high-concentration aluminium phosphide tablets (3 g 56%) with products of alternative formulations and lower concentration. This study examines the impact of these regulations on pesticide suicides and agricultural productivity.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: National data on pesticide suicides (April 2017-August 2024) were obtained from two forensic toxicology laboratories. Pesticides were grouped into categories. Logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs) for changes in pesticide involvement between the pre-ban (April 2017-February 2020) and post-ban (September 2021-August 2024) periods. Post-ban provincial variation in pesticide suicides was assessed using age-standardised rates and standardised mortality ratios (SMRs). Joinpoint regression was used to assess trends in crop yields (2005-2023).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 3,005 and 1,331 pesticide suicides were analysed in pre- and post-ban periods, respectively. The mean monthly number of identified pesticide suicides declined by 56.9% (85.9 to 37.0). The proportions of pesticide suicides involving the categories of organophosphorus pesticides, carbamates, and organochlorines, including banned pesticides such as dichlorvos and triazophos, decreased. In contrast, phosphine gas-generating pesticides increased proportionally (31.1% to 48.2%), largely driven by aluminium phosphide. Post-ban suicides were more common amongst males (56.0%), individuals aged 15-44 years (52.8%), and in Bagmati and Lumbini Provinces (SMRs = 1.26 and 1.35) than their counterparts. No adverse changes in rice, pulse, or vegetable yields were observed.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Nepal's 2019-2021 pesticide regulations were associated with reduced involvement of banned organophosphorus pesticides, carbamates, and organochlorines. However, continued aluminium phosphide deaths warrant surveillance and further regulatory action. Our findings were similar compared to previous studies monitoring pesticide exposures after a ban. There are potential policy implications from this study.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In Nepal, the 2019-2021 bans were followed by fewer suicides involving banned pesticides without declines in major crop yields, but aluminium phosphide remained prominent after regulation.

articles.title: Rethinking how poison centres engage with the pesticide industry.

abstract.text: Poison centres help to prevent, diagnose and manage poisonings. Part of their prevention activities involves identifying sources of harm, such as toxic pesticides, and working with others to address these, including removing hazardous products from the market. This raises important questions about how poison centres and the health professionals who support their work should interact with commercial actors whose business interests conflict with the public health mission and purpose of poison centres. Partnership working with industries like the pesticide industry may appear intuitively appealing, particularly when access to funds and data are limited. However, such partnerships create considerable risks, including a shift towards industry-favourable interventions that blame pesticide users. This commentary examines these complex issues using examples of partnerships between the pesticide industry, clinical toxicology societies and poison centres. We argue that these interactions have received inadequate attention compared to other areas of medicine and public health. We call for a rethinking of how poison centres engage with the pesticide industry. Among other changes, this requires a strengthening of the international guidance on the provision of poison centres, building on approaches to managing conflicts of interest and engaging with commercial actors in other areas such as food and nutrition. Reflecting critically on industry partnerships and strengthening of governance systems are core to ensuring poison centres prioritise the prevention of harm by removing poisons and not blaming the poisoned.

articles.title: Results of a Training Intervention to Improve Employer Crisis Preparedness.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: The objective of this study was to evaluate the feasibility and effectiveness of a brief Total Worker Health® Employer Crisis Preparedness asynchronous training consisting of ten modules. These modules emphasized domains of preparedness related to employee well-being in the face of disasters that are not regularly included in traditional emergency preparedness, such as leave policies and mental health support.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We assessed participants' pre- to post-training confidence in their preparedness capabilities, intention to conduct preparedness planning, and their perspective on the value of the training. Trainees also reported on their employer's level of preparedness in our Total Worker Health Employer Crisis Preparedness domains.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The course was well received by survey participants. Post-training intention to undertake Total Worker Health Employer Crisis Preparedness activities such as speaking to management about preparedness and conducting vulnerability analyses increased significantly. Improvements in self-reported confidence in undertaking employee-centered preparedness pre- to post-training were also statistically significant.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Our findings suggest that this course is a feasible and well-received way to promote an employee-centered preparedness approach in business and organizational practices that can prevent or mitigate the impacts of disasters on working populations.

articles.title: Concussion Management Practices Among Primary Care Professionals Who Care for Children and Adults With Concussions-2023 DocStyles Survey.
articles.journal_full: The Journal of head trauma rehabilitation

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: The objective of this study was to assess whether primary care professionals' self-reported concussion management practices are consistent with clinical guideline recommendations from leading health organizations.

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: 2023 DocStyles online national market research survey of US primary care professionals.

abstract.label: PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: One thousand three hundred eighteen primary care professionals who see patients with concussion.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Cross-sectional.

abstract.label: MAIN MEASURES
abstract.text: Primary care professionals' self-reported practices related to return to activity (physical, cognitive, social), work/school accommodations, provision of follow-up instructions, and screening for risk factors for persistent symptoms. All data were analyzed using SAS and differences were examined using χ2 tests.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among the 1318 primary care professionals who saw a patient with a concussion in the past 12 months, about one-third of participants self-reported that they do not provide recommendations or provide recommendations on return to physical (42.6%), cognitive (33.5%), and social (38.5%) activities that do not align with clinical recommendations. Most (78.0%) provided follow-up instructions more than 75% of the time. Only about half of participants self-reported providing work/school accommodations (52.0%) and screening for risk factors of persistent symptoms (54.6%) more than 75% of the time; findings varied by specialty, years of medical practice, and urbanicity of healthcare facility.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This study found that many participants' self-reported concussion management practices do not align with clinical recommendations from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and others. Use of clinical care pathways, and other promising strategies to improve adherence to guideline recommendations, may be beneficial.

articles.title: Clinical and Epidemiologic Characteristics of Pediatric Tularemia: A Case Series With a Waterborne Cluster.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Tularemia may be difficult to recognize in children because of its nonspecific presentation. We aimed to describe the epidemiologic, clinical and diagnostic characteristics of pediatric tularemia in Amasya, Türkiye, emphasizing water exposure, diagnostic delay and public health response.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively reviewed 8 patients <18 years of age diagnosed with tularemia between January 2021 and January 2026. Demographic data, epidemiologic exposures, clinical and laboratory findings, diagnostic timelines, treatment, complications and outcomes were obtained from medical records.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The median age was 12.1 years (range: 7-16 years), and 4 patients were female. All reported consumption of untreated spring or fountain water; 7 (87.5%) reported similar illness in the surrounding community, and 7 (87.5%) initially presented to the emergency department. Five patients had glandular, 2 oropharyngeal and 1 typhoidal tularemia. The median interval from symptom onset to first healthcare presentation was 4.5 days, and the median interval from symptom onset to submission of the initial serum sample for tularemia serologic testing was 17 days. All patients had received antibiotics before tularemia was confirmed. Two developed lymph node abscesses, 1 required incision and drainage, and 1 relapsed. Five temporally clustered cases shared exposure to the implicated source. Microbiologic culture of the implicated source yielded Francisella tularensis, and the source was subsequently closed to public use.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In endemic areas, the actual source of drinking water should be specifically assessed regardless of residence. Tularemia should remain in the differential diagnosis even without cervical lymphadenopathy. Early recognition of clustered cases and timely public health communication may reduce diagnostic delay and facilitate source-control measures.

articles.title: Hospital-Based Surveillance of Respiratory Pathogen Positivity and Distribution: A Six-Year Epidemiological Study in Beijing, 2020-2025.

abstract.text: Objective: Respiratory tract infections (RTIs) are imposing a great economic burden, morbidity, and mortality on the healthcare system. Eleven common respiratory pathogens, based on age of onset, clinical setting, season and calendar year during and after the COVID-19 pandemic, were analyzed to optimize clinical diagnosis and prevention. Methods: In this retrospective cross-sectional study, respiratory pathogen testing results of 9882 samples from RTI patients from January 2020 to December 2025 were included to statistically analyze the positivity, distribution and trend of change. Multiplex PCR combined with capillary electrophoresis was used to simultaneously detect 11 respiratory targets. Results: The overall positive detection rate was 24.71%, with the top three pathogens being human rhinovirus (HRV) (6.20%), influenza A virus (InfA) (4.28%), and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) (4.13%). The patients aged under 18 had the highest detection rates (≤6 years: 39.80%; 7 to 17 years: 37.95%). HRV, RSV and Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP) were the primary pathogens among pediatric patients, while InfA was predominant in adults (including those >65 years). The 11 pathogens were most common in emergency department patients (29.14%), followed by outpatient patients (28.57%). InfA was the most predominant virus, followed by HRV and RSV, in the intensive care unit, emergency department, and outpatient settings. The detection rate was highest in autumn (33.22%), followed by winter (26.61%). MP had the highest rate in autumn, and InfA was the most frequent in winter. During the COVID-19 pandemic (2020-2022), the respiratory pathogen spectrum was dominated by HRV, RSV, and human parainfluenza virus (HPIV). And the prevalent pathogens shifted to InfA, MP and HRV during 2023-2025. Co-detections were observed in 8.03% of the positive cases, and 82.65% occurred in patients aged < 18 years. The dominant co-detections were HRV + MP, HRV + RSV and HRV + HPIV. Conclusions: The distribution of respiratory pathogens exhibited specific variations based on age, clinical setting, season, and calendar year, suggesting that differentiated prevention should be developed for different patients.

articles.title: The Triage Frailty and Comorbidity Tool for Risk Stratification of Older Patients Admitted from the Emergency Department to a Geriatric Ward.

abstract.text: Introduction: Frailty assessment in the Emergency Department (ED) may provide prognostic information beyond triage, but the value of the Triage Frailty and Comorbidity Tool (TFC) in older patients admitted to geriatric wards is uncertain. Methods: This retrospective study included patients aged ≥75 years admitted directly from the ED to Merano Hospital Geriatric Ward between May and September 2025. The primary outcome was 90-day mortality; in-hospital mortality was secondary. Analyses included logistic regression, AUROC estimation, predefined TFC ≥ 10% threshold performance, and Kaplan-Meier curves. Results: A total of 225 patients were included. Median age was 86 years (IQR 82-90), median length of stay was 9 days (IQR 6-13), 90-day mortality was 27.6% (62/225), and in-hospital mortality was 11.5% (26/225). Patients who died within 90 days had higher TFC values than survivors [49.5 (31.4-72.3) vs. 19.4 (6.5-43.8); p < 0.001]. Each 10-point increase in TFC was associated with higher odds of 90-day mortality (OR 1.43, 95% CI 1.26-1.63; p < 0.001) and in-hospital mortality (OR 1.38, 95% CI 1.18-1.62; p < 0.001). The AUROC was 0.747 for 90-day mortality and 0.732 for in-hospital mortality. TFC ≥ 10% identified 54/62 deaths, with a sensitivity of 87.1% and NPV of 87.9%. Survival was lower in patients with TFC ≥ 10% (log-rank p = 0.001). Conclusions: The TFC showed prognostic value in older patients admitted from the ED to geriatric care. Although discrimination was moderate, the TFC may support risk stratification during ED-to-ward transition.

articles.title: Job Satisfaction Among Healthcare Professionals During and Directly After the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Systematic Review of Psychosocial, Organizational and System-Level Factors.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: The COVID-19 pandemic substantially changed working conditions in healthcare and increased the workload of healthcare professionals. This systematic review aimed to identify factors associated with job satisfaction among physicians, nurses, and paramedics during the COVID-19 pandemic, with particular emphasis on psychosocial, organizational, and system-level factors.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Searches were performed in ScienceDirect (10 January 2026), PubMed (16 January 2026), and Scopus (22 January 2026). Original studies published between 2020 and 2025 in English or Polish were eligible. Three researchers independently conducted the study selection and methodological assessment. Methodological quality was assessed using JBI critical appraisal tools. Fifteen studies involving physicians, nurses, and paramedics were included. Findings were synthesized narratively because of substantial heterogeneity among the included studies. The review was registered in the Open Science Framework.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Higher job satisfaction was associated with older age, longer length of service and higher remuneration. In contrast, lower job satisfaction was associated with direct work with patients infected with SARS-CoV-2, higher levels of stress and burnout, and poor work organization.

abstract.label: LIMITATIONS
abstract.text: The main limitations were related to the fact that only three databases were searched, the heterogeneity of the studies, and a language restriction, as only articles in Polish and English were included in the search.

articles.title: Pediatric cardiopulmonary resuscitation in the emergency department: Factors associated with outcome.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Pediatric cardiac arrest is usually studied either before hospital arrival or after admission, although the emergency department (ED) team resuscitates both. We examined factors associated with return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), recurrent arrest and mortality in an ED cohort including both out-of-hospital cardiac arrests (OHCA) and in-ED cardiac arrests.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective cohort of all 83 children who received cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) in a university pediatric ED over 14 years (January 2010-March 2024). The primary outcome was survival to hospital discharge; multivariable logistic regression identified factors independently associated with ED mortality.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Median age was 35 months; 54.2% occurred out of hospital. ROSC was achieved in 42.2% and 30.1% survived the ED phase, but 9.9% survived to discharge. Epinephrine given later than 2 min was independently associated with ED mortality among the 27 patients with documented timing (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 7.73; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.27-46.97). Beyond 20 min of CPR, each additional minute was associated with ED death (aOR 1.32; 95% CI 1.01-1.73). Recurrent arrest after ROSC in the ED occurred in 42.9%, of whom 6.7% survived versus 38.9% without recurrence (p = 0.039). Survival did not differ by arrest location, initial rhythm or timing of advanced airway management.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Resuscitation in the ED restored spontaneous circulation in many children, but few survived to discharge. Time to first epinephrine was independently associated with ED mortality in this cohort, whereas prolonged resuscitation and recurrent arrest after ROSC in the ED identified children at very high risk.

articles.title: Successful delivery of a live infant from an advanced abdominal pregnancy: a case report from MSF mother and child hospital, Kenema, Sierra Leone.

abstract.text: Abdominal pregnancy accounts for 1%-4% of ectopic pregnancies and 0.5-18% of maternal deaths, primarily from hemorrhage. We report a successful delivery of a live infant from an advanced abdominal pregnancy at 32 weeks' gestation in a low-resource setting. A 29-year-old multiparous woman, initially admitted for severe anemia in pregnancy, developed hemorrhagic shock on hospital day 3 and was referred to a gynecologist. Point-of-care ultrasound diagnosed an abdominal pregnancy, and an emergency exploratory laparotomy was performed. Both mother and preterm neonate survived. The mother was discharged on post-operative day 4; the neonate was discharged on day 7 after intravenous antibiotics for suspected sepsis, with a left clubfoot deformity referred for follow-up. Timely diagnosis and surgical intervention can save both lives, but this case highlights gaps in antenatal care and the need for wider point-of-care ultrasound training and improved capacity in the management of abdominal pregnancy.

articles.title: Airway management during missions of a neurologist-staffed mobile stroke unit: a retrospective registry study.
articles.journal: Scand J Trauma Resusc Emerg Med
articles.journal_full: Scandinavian journal of trauma, resuscitation and emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Following their endorsement by international guidelines, mobile stroke units (MSUs) are increasingly being integrated into emergency medical services worldwide. In real-world use, physician-staffed MSUs can be dispatched beyond their intended indication, exposing on-board neurologists to non-stroke emergencies. This raises important clinical and regulatory questions about the competencies MSU physicians need. Advanced airway management is one of the most critical prehospital interventions. Yet, its frequency, indications, procedural characteristics and success rates have not been investigated in neurologist-staffed MSU services.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively analysed a prospective registry of mission documentation from a neurologist-staffed MSU service in Berlin, Germany from 31 August 2024 to 15 March 2026. Dispatches of the MSU were classified as stroke or non-stroke dispatches using the recorded activation code. The primary outcome was the dispatch-based frequency of endotracheal intubation (ETI), defined as a documented intubation attempt. All ETIs were performed by the on-board neurologist. Secondary outcomes included supraglottic airway (SGA) use, first-pass success rate, procedural characteristics and self-reported post-mission National Aeronautics and Space Administration Task Load Index (NASA-TLX) workload. Proportions are reported with 95% Wilson confidence intervals (CI).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We analysed 3,887 dispatches. ETI occurred in a total of 49 dispatches (1.26%; 95% CI 0.95-1.66) with 2 in 1,755 stroke- (0.11%; 95% CI 0.03-0.41) and 47 in 2,132 non-stroke dispatches (2.20%; 95% CI 1.66-2.92). SGA use occurred in 22 dispatches (0.57%; 95% CI 0.37-0.86). All 49 intubation attempts were successful (100.0%; 95% CI 92.7-100.0). First-pass success was achieved in 43/49 (87.8%; 95% CI 75.8-94.3) with no ETI requiring more than two attempts. Videolaryngoscopy was used in all ETIs and capnographic confirmation of tube position in 48/49 (98%). Non-traumatic cardiac arrest was the most frequent indication (30/49). In the exploratory workload analysis, the median NASA-TLX score was 59.8 [IQR 50.0-68.7] in 49 dispatches with ETI and 27.0 [15.5-41.7] in 2,700 dispatches without ETI.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: ETI was infrequent overall and particularly rare during stroke dispatches, yet first-pass success was high. Prospective studies are needed to define airway management requirements and training standards for MSU physicians.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy for Fatigue and Neurocognitive Symptoms in Long COVID: A Prospective Observational Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Long COVID or post-COVID-19 condition is characterized as the continuation or development of new symptoms 3 months after the initial SARS-CoV-2 infection, with these symptoms lasting for at least 2 months with no other explanation. Fatigue and brain fog are among the most prevalent symptoms of long COVID, which significantly impact individuals' quality of life, but treatment options for these symptoms have been limited. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) is suggested as a possible treatment option for long COVID. This study aimed to investigate the effect of HBOT on fatigue and the neuropsychiatric symptoms of long COVID.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This study included 49 long COVID patients with fatigue caseness, as defined by a Chalder Fatigue Scale (CFQ) bimodal score of ≥ 4. The subjects underwent 10 HBOT sessions, once daily at 2 atmospheres for 90 minutes over 12 days. The clinical outcomes were assessed using the bimodal and Likert scores of the CFQ, selected cognitive function tests, validated neuropsychological scales, and a subjective post-COVID-19 symptom checklist before and after HBOT. The adverse events were also assessed. Paired t-tests were performed, and the safety evaluations were conducted.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Out of the 49 subjects included in the analyses, 37 completed the treatment. After HBOT, 36 out of 49 (73.5%) subjects recovered from fatigue (CFQ bimodal score of < 4). The overall fatigue severity significantly decreased (CFQ Likert score mean ± standard deviation, 22.67 ± 5.12 at baseline vs. 6.46 ± 7.14 post-treatment, P < 0.001). Following HBOT, a significant improvement in the mental health outcomes, as well as a reduction in the number of post-COVID-19 symptoms, was observed. Moreover, verbal memory as well as working memory showed significant improvements. Of the 12 dropouts, 7 discontinued treatment due to adverse events, and 5 withdrew their consent. The safety evaluations revealed middle ear barotrauma in 7 subjects, resulting in premature HBOT termination. However, they fully recovered without complications.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The significant reduction in fatigue, improvements in several cognitive function domains, mental health outcomes, and post-COVID-19 symptoms suggest that HBOT could be a potential therapeutic option for long COVID.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: Clinical Research Information Service Identifier: KCT0008274.

articles.title: Pickleball Pain: Point of Care Ultrasound Used to Diagnose Midfoot Pain: Erratum.
Pickleball Injuries in Adults: A Narrative Review.

abstract.text: Pickleball has emerged as the fastest-growing sport in the United States, with an estimated annual health care burden of $250 to $500 million. Emergency department visits for pickleball-related injuries increased 18-fold between 2014 and 2023, with a diverse and expanding range of injuries documented. Women are disproportionately affected by pickleball-related fractures, particularly distal radius fractures, reflecting postmenopausal bone loss combined with fall-dominant injury mechanisms. A striking finding among Achilles tendon injuries is the "first-month phenomenon," with most ruptures occurring within the first month of play and nearly one-third on the player's very first day, challenging the perception of pickleball as a low-impact sport. Ocular injuries represent an emerging concern, as nearly 88% of injuries documented over a 20-year surveillance period occurred within the last three years; however, no governing body currently mandates protective eyewear. Targeted prevention strategies addressing the distinct vulnerabilities associated with age, sex, and experience level are warranted.

articles.title: A Review of Platelet-Rich Plasma as Treatment for Partial Elbow Ulnar Collateral Ligament Tears.

abstract.text: Platelet-rich plasma injections are increasingly utilized for partial-thickness ulnar collateral ligament tears in throwing athletes. This narrative review evaluates platelet-rich plasma's efficacy, safety, and cost-effectiveness for partial ulnar collateral ligament tears using literature from 2020 to 2026. A systematic search identified four studies, including cohorts and an economic simulation model. The largest cohort demonstrated that 60% of athletes with partial tears returned to play when platelet-rich plasma was combined with rehabilitation. Smaller case series reported successful return to play with similar treatment, though limited by a lack of comparison groups and small sample sizes. Complications included ulnar nerve dysfunction, particularly in athletes with preexisting nerve instability. Early surgery was often more cost-effective for long-term career durability. Current evidence suggests platelet-rich plasma alongside rehabilitation may benefit select athletes with partial ulnar collateral ligament injuries but is limited by retrospective designs, heterogeneous protocols, and inconsistent outcome measures. Future research is needed regarding patient selection and standardized treatment protocols.

articles.title: Boxing Medicine Beyond the Ringside.

abstract.text: Boxing is widely regarded as one of the oldest and most physically demanding sports, dating back to 3000 BC, and it first appeared at the modern Olympics in 1904. Boxers require a multidisciplinary approach to healthcare, and this review focuses on care beyond the ringside. Chronic injuries, particularly involving the upper extremity, require individualized management plans to get the athlete back into the ring on fight night. Team physician-guided return to play for boxers with concussions is another evolving pillar of boxing medicine. Weight management and nutrition are critical yet often underappreciated aspects of performance and safety, with attention to safe weight-cutting practices and hydration. Finally, the psychological toll of training, competition, and postcareer transition underscores the need for integrated mental health support. This review aims to synthesize current evidence and best practices in boxing medicine and to advocate for a comprehensive, athlete-centered approach that extends well beyond the ring.

articles.title: Lower Extremity Neuropathies in Athletes.

abstract.text: Lower extremity neuropathies are an important and often underrecognized cause of pain and dysfunction in athletes. While classic neuropathic symptoms such as numbness, paresthesias, and weakness in the distribution of the affected peripheral nerve may be present, clinical presentations are frequently subtle and nonspecific. On physical examination, clinicians may identify focal neurological deficits, a positive Tinel sign at the site of suspected compression, and symptom reproduction with provocative maneuvers. Diagnostic evaluation may include electromyography/nerve conduction studies, as well as imaging modalities such as radiographs, ultrasound, and magnetic resonance imaging, to support the diagnosis. Initial management is typically nonoperative, although surgical intervention may be considered for persistent or progressive symptoms. This article provides an updated review of the evaluation and management of common lower extremity neuropathies in athletes.

articles.title: The Growing Popularity of Youth Hockey: A Review of Injury Patterns and Prevention Techniques.

abstract.text: Ice hockey is growing in popularity not only in the United States and Canada, but also throughout the world with today's youth. Due to the nature of the sport, there are common and unique injuries that occur in young athletes which differ from adult counterparts. Injuries occur more frequently with age. With the introduction of body checking, there is a considerable increase in injuries, especially concussions. Concussions are the most common youth hockey injury with the greatest number of publications in the past several years. Acromioclavicular joint sprains and clavicle fractures are common upper body injuries, whereas hip muscle strains, knee sprains, and contusions are common lower body injuries. Most injuries occur during competition and result in at least a week off from sports participation. Protective gear, such as properly fitting helmets, full-face protection, and mouthguards, along with rule changes such as restrictions on body checking and avoidance of direct head contact, have been shown to lower the risk of injuries. This paper reviews the most recent literature on youth hockey injuries and how these injuries can ultimately be prevented.

articles.title: Web Alert.
Our Climate Is Getting Hotter Faster than Coaches Are Getting Smarter.
FAST Performance Changes After a Training Sequence Including Augmented Reality Guidance Among Paramedic Students.
articles.journal_full: Simulation in healthcare : journal of the Society for Simulation in Healthcare

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Point-of-care ultrasound is an essential diagnostic tool in emergency medicine. Among its applications, Focused Assessment with Sonography for Trauma (FAST) is a rapid imaging method used in initial trauma evaluation. Augmented reality (AR) may provide visual guidance during procedural learning. This study examined changes in FAST performance following a short-term training sequence that included AR-assisted guidance among paramedic students.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: An interventional study was conducted with 18 undergraduate paramedic students who participated in a two-hour program consisting of a 60-minute lecture and a 60-minute hands-on session. Each participant performed four FAST examinations: 2 conventional and 2 AR-assisted. The primary outcome was total FAST performance time; secondary outcomes were the time for each view and the Quality of Ultrasound Imaging and Competence score, including the Task-Specific Checklist and Global Rating Scale.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The median total FAST time was significantly reduced after the training sequence (difference: 263.5 s; 95% CI: 177-352.5; P<0.001). Significant time reductions were observed in the pericardial, Morison's pouch, and perisplenic views, but not in the Douglas pouch view. Both Task-Specific Checklist and Global Rating Scale scores improved significantly (both P<0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Improvements in procedural efficiency and technical performance were observed after a short training sequence that included AR-assisted guidance for FAST among paramedic students. Given the fixed examination sequence and absence of a parallel control group, these findings should be interpreted cautiously.

articles.title: Violent Reinjury Trajectories Across Injury Mechanisms: A Multicenter Cohort Study.

abstract.label: STUDY OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Survivors of violent injury often experience reinjury. We sought to identify demographic and clinical factors associated with violent reinjury across different injury types.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted an observational cohort study of individuals with violent injury (ie, blunt assaults, stabbings, and firearm injuries) across 2 adult and 2 pediatric Level I trauma centers from 2016 to 2023. Covariates included age, sex, race, hospital type, insurance status, and social vulnerability. Our primary outcome was time to reinjury. We used multivariable Cox proportional hazards models to measure associations between each covariate and time to reinjury across injury types.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: There were 29,038 individuals with nonfatal violent injuries. Male sex (n=19,273; 66.4%), Black and other race (n=21,403; 73.7%), presentation to adult hospitals (n=24,200; 83.3%), public insurance (n=13,879; 47.8%), and living in an area with high social vulnerability (n=21,044; 72.5%) were associated with a greater risk of any violent reinjury, adjusting for covariates. For index firearm injuries, patients younger than18 years had greater risk of firearm reinjury than patients aged 18 to 26 years (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR]:0.65 [0.47 to 0.91]) and for those older than 26 years (aHR:0.47 [0.34 to 0.66]). Although women with firearm injury had a lower risk of firearm reinjury compared with men (aHR:0.46 [0.36 to 0.58]), they had greater risk of blunt reinjury (aHR:1.77 [1.34 to 1.24]). Patients living in areas with high social vulnerability had a higher risk of escalating reinjury mechanism (eg, blunt to firearm; aHR:1.46 [1.11 to 1.90]) versus patients in areas with low/average social vulnerability.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This research underscores how sequelae of violent reinjury are shaped by certain demographic and clinical characteristics, highlighting opportunities to strengthen reinjury prevention in key subgroups.

articles.title: Utilization of Medications for Alcohol Use Disorder in United States Emergency Departments.
Hemorrhagic Cardiac Tamponade in an End-Stage Renal Disease Patient on Apixaban.

abstract.text: Direct oral anticoagulants are used for stroke prevention in selected patients with atrial fibrillation who receive hemodialysis. Randomized trial data remain limited in this population, and the anticoagulant effect of a given dose may vary considerably between patients. We report a 56-year-old man receiving hemodialysis three times weekly who was taking apixaban 5 mg twice daily and developed persistent hypotension and abdominal pain during dialysis. The early findings suggested dialysis-associated hypotension or sepsis. Emergency department point-of-care cardiac ultrasound showed a large circumferential pericardial effusion, leading to urgent cardiology evaluation for obstructive shock. Computed tomography obtained during the same evaluation described the effusion as large and possibly hemorrhagic. Pericardiocentesis was unsuccessful because most of the fluid was posterior. Shortly after transfer to the intensive care unit, the patient developed pulseless electrical activity arrest and underwent an emergent subxiphoid pericardial window. Approximately 450 mL of bloody fluid was drained, followed by hemodynamic improvement. Cytology showed no malignant cells, and fluid cultures were negative. This case also highlights the uncertainty surrounding the use of full-dose apixaban in patients receiving hemodialysis, particularly after a major bleeding event.

articles.title: Near-Infrared Spectroscopy Sensors Placed Frontally and Parietally to Detect Large Vessel Occlusion Stroke.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: We aimed to determine whether two-channelled near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) was feasible for recognising anterior large vessel occlusion (LVO) with a device suitable for prehospital use and whether probe placement (frontal vs. parietal) made a difference.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We analysed NIRS readings of six computed tomography angiography (CTA)-confirmed LVO-stroke patients at Tampere University Hospital during the six-month study period. We placed four sensors on patients' heads: two frontally and two parietally. We provided a detailed description and analysis of these recordings and their correlation with imaging-confirmed changes in perfusion.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In the frontally placed sensors, the rSO2 was 1-8 percentage points higher on the affected side before and 0-9 percentage points higher on the affected side after endovascular treatment (EVT). rSO2 values did not change significantly. One patient showed higher rSO2 on the healthy side (5 percentage points) before and after EVT. We could not recover frontal values from one patient. In parietally placed censors, all patients had 3-9 percentage points higher rSO2 on the healthy side before EVT. After EVT, 3 patients had 3-7 percentage points higher rSO2 on the healthy side. In two cases, after EVT, the difference in rSO2 changed to 1-2 percentage points higher on the affected side. We could not record parietal readings in one patient.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Neither NIRS sensor placement detected differences in rSO2 in LVO; therefore, NIRS appears unsuitable as a diagnostic tool for LVO. Future research should focus on other technologies.

articles.title: When the Filter Becomes the Source: POCUS Detection of Inferior Vena Cava Filter Thrombosis Extending Into the Right Atrium.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Inferior vena cava (IVC) filters are used to prevent pulmonary embolism in patients with venous thromboembolism when anticoagulation is contraindicated. Although uncommon, filter thrombosis can result in thrombus propagation and potentially life-threatening embolic complications. Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) provides a rapid bedside assessment of the heart, lungs, and may facilitate the prompt recognition of unexpected thromboembolic complications.

abstract.label: CASE PRESENTATION
abstract.text: A 43-year-old man with hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage was admitted to the intensive care unit requiring mechanical ventilation and vasopressor support. Six days after admission, he developed sudden severe hypoxemia, tachycardia, and hypotension requiring reinitiation of norepinephrine. POCUS demonstrated bilateral anterior A-lines, left femoral and popliteal deep vein thrombosis, and preserved right ventricular (RV) function without echocardiographic evidence of RV strain. Catheter-based pulmonary angiography confirmed subocclusive thrombosis involving segmental branches of the right middle and lower lobes, which was treated with mechanical thromboaspiration, followed by IVC filter placement because anticoagulation was initially contraindicated. Four days later, he developed a new episode of acute hypoxemia despite remaining hemodynamically stable. Repeat POCUS demonstrated a large mobile thrombus in transit within the right atrium. Subcostal longitudinal imaging of the IVC demonstrated a large elongated thrombus attached to the IVC filter, with a freely mobile portion extending into the right atrium. Urgent mechanical thrombectomy and IVC filter replacement were performed. The new filter was positioned approximately 2 cm below the confluence of the hepatic veins with the inferior vena cava. Approximately 24 h later, follow-up POCUS showed no evidence of new thrombus formation. More than 2 weeks after admission, following a follow-up brain CT showing no significant progression of the intracerebral hemorrhage, anticoagulation with enoxaparin was initiated and progressively increased to a full therapeutic dose.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This case highlights the value of POCUS for the prompt bedside recognition of an established and potentially life-threatening complication of IVC filter placement. Systematic bedside cardiac and venous ultrasound may identify thrombus propagation into the right atrium even in the absence of RV dilation or echocardiographic evidence of RV strain, facilitating timely endovascular intervention.

articles.title: Reverse Balloon Anchoring for Retrieval of an Entrapped Side-Branch Balloon During the Jailed Balloon Technique.
articles.journal_full: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

abstract.text: The jailed balloon technique (JBT) is an effective strategy for side branch (SB) protection during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for coronary bifurcation lesions; however, jailed balloon entrapment is a rare but serious complication. We report the case of a man in his 70s who was successfully resuscitated after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest due to ventricular fibrillation and underwent emergency PCI for a right coronary artery bifurcation lesion. A drug-eluting stent was deployed from the mid right coronary artery to the posterior descending branch using JBT. The jailed SB balloon became entrapped and could not be retrieved despite repeated inflation and deflation, traction, and rotational torque. Further traction resulted in deep engagement of the guiding catheter and an accordion phenomenon of the right coronary artery, raising concern about vascular injury. A balloon was therefore inflated within the stented main vessel, and forward pressure was applied to its shaft to provide counterforce against traction on the entrapped SB balloon. Using this technique, which we termed the "reverse balloon anchoring technique," the entrapped balloon was successfully retrieved without apparent device damage. Final angiography and intravascular ultrasound demonstrated preserved SB flow and adequate stent apposition. The reverse balloon anchoring technique may represent a useful bailout option for jailed balloon entrapment when conventional retrieval maneuvers fail.

articles.title: Rate of subsequent emergency department and inpatient hospital visits among individuals with cannabis-associated diagnoses: A retrospective cohort study of Arizona, USA hospital discharge data.

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: To track people with a cannabis-associated diagnosis during a hospital visit and examine rates of subsequent hospital visits over one year, including visits with mental health- and substance use-associated diagnoses.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Retrospective cohort study of Arizona, USA hospital discharge data. Patients were observed for one year before and after their 2018 index visit to capture hospital encounters with mental health- and substance use-associated diagnoses.

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: Data were patient-level emergency department and inpatient hospital records from Arizona, USA 2017-2019.

abstract.label: PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: Four groups of patients were identified based on diagnoses during their index visit in 2018. These included people who had 1) a cannabis-associated diagnosis and a co-occurring mental health-associated diagnosis (C+/MH+; n = 16 699), 2) a cannabis-associated diagnosis but not a mental health-associated diagnosis (C+/MH-; n = 21 406), 3) a mental health-associated diagnosis but not a cannabis-associated diagnosis (C-/MH+; n = 230 519), and 4) neither a cannabis-associated nor a mental health-associated diagnosis (C-/MH-; n = 1 096 939).

abstract.label: MEASUREMENTS
abstract.text: Records included diagnosis codes from the International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM), which were used to identify cannabis-associated diagnoses, other substance use-associated diagnoses, and mental health-associated diagnoses. In analyses predicting subsequent hospital visits, covariates included demographic factors; index visit month; total number of past-year visits, visits with a mental health-associated diagnosis, and visits with a substance use-associated diagnosis; concurrent (to the index visit) non-cannabis substance use-associated diagnosis and the Elixhauser readmission index.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: After adjusting for covariates, people with a cannabis-associated diagnosis during their index visit in 2018 had 1.23 times the rate of subsequent hospital visits as those without a cannabis-associated diagnosis (99.8% confidence interval (CI) [1.20, 1.26]), 2.74 times the rate of subsequent visits with a mental health-associated diagnosis (99.8% CI [2.64, 2.84]), and 1.76 times the rate of subsequent visits with a substance use-associated diagnosis (99.8% CI [1.69, 1.83]). Elevated visit rates were observed among individuals with a cannabis-associated diagnosis, regardless of whether they had a concurrent mental health-associated diagnosis, though associations were stronger among those without a concurrent mental health-associated diagnosis.

abstract.label: SUMMARY
abstract.text: A cannabis-associated diagnosis during a hospital visit appears to signal risk for higher rates of subsequent hospital use.

articles.title: Different Clinical Profile of Cannabis Intoxication Cases: Children Versus Adults.
articles.journal_full: Journal of paediatrics and child health

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: This observational, descriptive, retrospective study aimed to evaluate whether cannabis exposure presents distinct clinical patterns between paediatric and adult populations.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Data were obtained from the Toxicological Information and Assistance Center of Santa Catarina (CIATox/SC), and analyses were performed using Microsoft Excel 365.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 697 suspected cannabis intoxication cases were identified, including 112 paediatric and 585 adult cases. Male patients predominated (67%), and the most affected age group was 20-29 years (39.7%). Most cases were classified as mild (76.9%) and evolved favourably. In children aged 0-14 years, the most frequent clinical manifestations were drowsiness (64.2%), lethargy (19.7%) and altered level of consciousness (14.8%), indicating a clinical profile distinct from that observed in adults. Paediatric cases were mainly associated with oral ingestion and central nervous system depression, suggesting the need for prolonged observation and careful neurological monitoring. In adults, cardiovascular and neuropsychiatric manifestations were more common. Although most cases had low severity and favourable outcomes, greater severity was associated with high doses and polysubstance use. Seven deaths were recorded, all involving concomitant use of other substances, mainly cocaine.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: These findings support the hypothesis that cannabis intoxication presents age-dependent clinical patterns, providing relevant information for risk assessment, clinical management and decision-making in poison centre and emergency care settings.

articles.title: Comparison of emergency department-measured optic nerve sheath diameter according to early neurological outcome in pediatric patients with traumatic brain injury.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Early risk stratification in pediatric traumatic brain injury (TBI) is challenging, and readily available bedside markers may help identify children at risk of an adverse clinical course. This study compared emergency department (ED)-measured optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD) and related ocular ultrasound measurements according to early neurological outcome in children with TBI.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This perspective observational study was conducted at Mardani-Azar Pediatric Medical Center, Tabriz, Iran, between January and December 2025. Children younger than 18 years with TBI underwent ocular ultrasonography during their ED evaluation. Bilateral ONSD, eyeball transverse diameter (ETD), and interocular distance (IOD) were measured, and the ONSD/ETD and ONSD/IOD ratios were calculated. Neurological status was assessed 3-5 days after admission using the Glasgow coma scale (GCS). Associations between ultrasound measurements and early clinical outcomes were evaluated using between-group comparisons and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 100 patients, 84 patients (84%) had no CT findings suggestive of raised ICP, whereas 16 patients (16%) had at least one such finding. Mean ONSD was higher in the unfavorable-outcome group than in the favorable-outcome group (5.84 ± 0.67 vs. 4.55 ± 0.41 mm; P < 0.001). The ONSD/ETD and ONSD/IOD ratios were also higher in the unfavorable-outcome group (both P < 0.001), whereas ETD and IOD did not differ significantly. Mean ONSD showed an area under the ROC curve of 0.961 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.913-0.994) for discriminating the study-defined outcome groups.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: ED-measured ONSD was associated with early neurological status in this pediatric TBI cohort. These findings suggest that ONSD may warrant further evaluation as an adjunctive bedside risk-stratification marker. Prospective validation using standardized outcome definitions and appropriate adjustment for initial injury severity is needed before its independent prognostic value can be established.

abstract.label: CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER
abstract.text: Not applicable.

articles.title: ACMT Position Statement: Administer Expired Naloxone When Unexpired Naloxone Is Unavailable.
articles.journal_full: Journal of medical toxicology : official journal of the American College of Medical Toxicology

articles.title: LLM ensemble PREVIA predicts future PTSD risk from emergency department trauma narratives with expert-level accuracy.

abstract.text: Post-traumatic stress disorder affects numerous trauma survivors following emergency department discharge, making this encounter vital for early risk stratification. Yet emergency clinicians face severe time constraints, making existing screening tools impractical. We introduce PREVIA, a clinically-informed large language model ensemble, that predicts post-traumatic stress disorder risk from unstructured patient trauma narratives, collected in response to a routine-care question asked in the emergency department, by extracting early post-traumatic stress symptoms, peri-traumatic symptoms, risk, and protective factors. Within an ongoing longitudinal study, we included N = 145 patients across two New York City level-1 trauma centers within 24 hours of trauma and assessed post-traumatic stress disorder 1-month post-trauma. In this work, PREVIA accurately forecasts post-traumatic stress disorder (AUROC = 78.49% ± 5.75%, sensitivity=95.4% ± 3.99%, precision=46.76% ± 8.66%), performs comparably to an emergency clinician specialized in post-traumatic stress disorder on 30 randomly selected patients (PREVIA: AUROC = 84.39%, sensitivity=100.00%, precision=50.00%; clinician: AUROC = 83.86%, sensitivity=88.89%, precision=50.00%), and generates interpretable explanations without additional clinical burden. These initial findings support PREVIA's potential as a scalable emergency department screener for timely, targeted interventions, and warrant validation in larger, independent cohorts.

articles.title: Oxygen-tension modulation and hyperbaric oxygen therapy as an investigational adjunct in Guillain-Barré syndrome: A narrative review.
articles.journal_full: The Journal of international medical research

abstract.text: Guillain-Barré syndrome is an acute immune-mediated polyradiculoneuropathy. Severe disease and axonal variants may cause oxygen mismatch through edema, microvascular dysfunction, respiratory compromise, critical illness, and inflammatory metabolic demand. However, human studies of Guillain-Barré syndrome have not yet measured nerve-root oxygenation or microvascular changes before and after hyperbaric oxygen therapy. This narrative review evaluates whether oxygen-tension biology provides a framework for studying hyperbaric oxygen therapy as an adjunctive investigational intervention in selected Guillain-Barré syndrome phenotypes. Targeted searches of PubMed and CrossRef, updated through 20 August 2026 and conducted without a database language filter, were combined with reference tracking and appraised using narrative review transparency principles. The five reports included in this review comprise one case report involving a mechanically ventilated patient with Guillain-Barré syndrome, two acute motor axonal neuropathy case reports, one small retrospective series, and one acute motor axonal neuropathy animal model. Four of the five reports originate from the same author group and clinical setting and have not been independently reproduced. Mechanistic support comes mainly from experimental autoimmune neuritis, hyperbaric oxygen therapy-hypoxia-inducible factor studies outside Guillain-Barré syndrome, peripheral nerve injury research, and general hyperbaric oxygen therapy biology. Overall, oxygen-tension modulation is biologically plausible but remains unproven in severe or axonal Guillain-Barré syndrome. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy should not replace intravenous immunoglobulin, plasma exchange, respiratory support, or rehabilitation. It should be tested only as an adjunctive intervention, with phenotype selection, standardized protocols, independent replication, blinded outcome assessment, safety monitoring, and a candidate biomarker panel whose analytical feasibility is established before it is considered a core panel.

articles.title: Practice models for implementing Rehabilitation in international cooperation.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The demand for rehabilitation services is increasing globally, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Physiotherapists dispatched as Japan Overseas Cooperation Volunteers (JOCV) through the Japan International Cooperation Agency support capacity strengthening in diverse health systems; however, the combinations of elements that enable rehabilitation practice to function effectively in international cooperation, and the conditions under which practice stagnates, remain insufficiently systematized.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: To develop practice models describing how professional expertise, contextual adaptation, and collaboration shape effective and stagnated practices among JOCV physiotherapists.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A qualitative content analysis was conducted using activity reports of JOCV physiotherapists whose service periods fell between 2014 and 2024. Report sets with all five reports completed were included. Item 3 of Report 4, which describes successful and unsuccessful practices, was the primary analytical material. Practice-related descriptions were extracted, classified as effective or stagnated (i.e. showing limited progress), and interpreted to construct practice models.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Overall, 123 report sets were included, of which 117 contributed 258 text segments to the qualitative analysis. Effective practices were classified into four categories: design, sharing of processes and outcomes, and embedding of professional interventions; establishment of working relationships and conditions through contextual understanding; development of collaborative practices respecting local autonomy; and reflective repositioning of professional identity. Stagnated practices were also grouped into four categories: stagnation in relationship-building and collaboration; weakened structures for activity design and evaluation; insufficient conditions for sustaining activities at placement sites; and failed implementation of professional expertise and role confusion.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: International rehabilitation cooperation by physiotherapists is not merely technical transfer but also a professional practice integrating rehabilitation knowledge with local relationships, organizational structures, and environmental factors.

articles.title: Preparedness for Imported Malaria in Non-Endemic Europe: Healthcare Workforce Knowledge and Travel-History Practice in Poland.
articles.journal_full: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Imported malaria remains a diagnostic challenge in non-endemic countries, where timely recognition depends on healthcare workers eliciting recent travel history and initiating appropriate testing. We assessed malaria knowledge, training exposure and self-reported travel-history practice across healthcare worker roles at two reference centres in northern Poland.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted an online cross-sectional survey between October 2023 and April 2024 among doctors, nurses, paramedics and allied healthcare personnel. A 25-item instrument covered aetiology, transmission, prevention, pharmacology, diagnosis and epidemiology. Knowledge scores were compared using non-parametric tests. Regression models exploring sociodemographic and occupational predictors were unstable because few respondents scored highly and are reported as supplementary sensitivity analyses.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 402 respondents, the mean knowledge score was 7.4 of 25 (29.6%); 91.3% scored below the predefined threshold and no respondent exceeded 64%. Knowledge gaps were greatest for complete transmission routes (4.0% correct), prevention measures (8.7%), diagnostic methods (12.7%) and contemporary pharmacology. Only 14.4% of doctors reported always asking febrile patients about travel to malaria-endemic regions. Malaria exposure in training was limited: 22.1% recalled coverage in parasitology classes and 3.5% had attended relevant symposia or conferences. No sociodemographic or occupational factor was independently associated with knowledge in any model specification.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Preparedness for imported malaria was weak across this non-endemic healthcare workforce. Strengthening case detection requires routine travel-history prompts in febrile-patient assessment, targeted continuing education and structured coverage of imported tropical infections in pre-graduate curricula.

articles.title: Advancing patient care: innovations and enhancements in massive haemorrhage response and treatment at the Royal Victoria Regional Health Centre.

abstract.text: Timely transfusion in massive haemorrhage is critical, with each minute of delay associated with increased mortality. In September 2023, a review of massive haemorrhage protocol (MHP) processes at Royal Victoria Regional Health Centre (RVH), a 459-bed Level III Trauma Centre in Barrie, Ontario, Canada, identified delays in blood component delivery, fragmented data capture, inconsistent team communication and absence of a paediatric-specific protocol. Baseline audit data demonstrated a mean time of 14.1 min from MHP activation to first red blood cell transfusion, exceeding the provincial benchmark of 10 min. This quality improvement initiative aimed to reduce this interval to 10 min or less across the emergency department, operating room, intensive care unit, postanaesthesia care unit and obstetrical areas by 31 December 2025. Guided by the Model for Improvement and provincial recommendations, a multidisciplinary team conducted diagnostic analyses and iterative Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles between November 2023 and December 2025. Interventions included redesign of the electronic MHP order set, a standardised overhead ‘Code Transfusion’ announcement, a designated blood component runner supported by a digital escalation platform, a paediatric MHP order set and a structured data monitoring framework aligned with the 7Ts of transfusion. Following implementation, mean time to first blood component decreased from 14.1 to 9.4 min, representing a 4.7-minute (approximately 33%) reduction from MHP activation to receipt of the first blood component at bedside. Process adherence improved, including 100% use of the revised order set and appropriate administration of tranexamic acid when indicated. Twenty-four hour all-cause mortality among patients receiving definitive care at RVH decreased from 15% to 5.88%. System-level redesign improved coordination and reliability, achieving the 10-minute target alongside improvements in early clinical outcomes. These findings support multidisciplinary, technology-enabled approaches to advancing haemorrhage care and demonstrate a scalable model for similar institutions.

articles.title: Patient-reported measures in non-invasive respiratory support for adults presenting with acute respiratory failure: a scoping review protocol.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: International guidance endorses patient engagement and informed treatment choices; however, research often neglects patient-reported measures (PRMs) potentially significant for patient intervention tolerance and informed decision-making. Omitting patient experience data prevents informed decision-making and limits the capture of non-physiological factors that may significantly impact treatment success. Sparse research on PRMs in non-invasive respiratory support (NIRS) may explain their absence in clinical trials. This scoping review will address this research gap by identifying PRMs used for NIRS in acute respiratory failure (ARF) in acute hospital settings.

abstract.label: METHODS AND ANALYSIS
abstract.text: This scoping review will adhere to the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology for scoping reviews and the PRISMA-ScR reporting guidelines. Web of Science, Scopus, PubMed, Cochrane CENTRAL, Embase, PsycINFO and CINAHL will be searched for literature reporting PRMs in adults (≥16 years) receiving NIRS (continuous or bi-level positive airway pressure or high flow nasal oxygen for ARF in acute hospital settings (emergency and inpatient care). Publications will be excluded if solely community-based, lacking use of PRMs for NIRS, using other indications for NIRS, unavailable or incomplete (eg, abstracts, protocols). Although confined to the English language, no limits will exist for publication date or geographical location. Google Scholar will be searched for grey literature. Publications will be screened against inclusion/exclusion criteria and data extracted into pre-designed tables. Each step will be undertaken by two independent reviewers, with a third resolving disagreements. Data tables will be combined and findings described narratively with graphical and/or tabular displays as appropriate.

abstract.label: ETHICS/DISSEMINATION
abstract.text: No ethical approval is required as no original data will be used; however, ethical principles will be followed throughout. Dissemination of results will be through peer-reviewed publication and scientific conference presentations. Interested parties, such as the Royal College of Emergency Medicine, will undergo direct result-sharing.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: This project is registered with the Open Science Framework.

articles.title: Feasibility of handheld nonmydriatic fundus camera use for optic disk assessment in pediatric patients.
articles.journal_full: Journal of AAPOS : the official publication of the American Association for Pediatric Ophthalmology and Strabismus

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Optic disk assessment is a frequent reason for pediatric ophthalmology consultation, but evaluation can be challenging in emergency as well as inpatient settings. Handheld nonmydriatic fundus cameras (NMFCs) may help to make pediatric examination easier, but data is limited.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively analyzed 118 pediatric patients (236 eyes) at a tertiary hospital who underwent imaging with handheld NMFC. A fellowship-trained neuro-ophthalmologist graded each image as adequate or inadequate for optic disk edema assessment. Age, sex, systemic and ophthalmic diagnoses, and nystagmus were recorded. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of feasibility.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Gradable images of both eyes were obtained in 99/118 patients (83.9%; 95% CI, 76.2-89.4). Adequacy increased with age: 23.1% (0-3 years), 87.5% (3-6 years), 92.6% (6-9 years), and 90.3% (9-18 years) (P < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, children 0-3 years had reduced odds of gradable imaging versus 9-18 years (OR = 0.011; 95% CI, 0.001-0.092, P < 0.001). Nystagmus (OR = 0.10; 95% CI, 0.01-1.05; P = 0.056) tended to be associated with lower feasibility, but this association did not reach statistical significance.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Successful imaging was least likely in children <3 years. NMFCs may reduce the need for in-person evaluation by an ophthalmologist and improve documentation in pediatric ophthalmology and emergency care.

articles.title: Emergency Response and Patient Transport in Remote Indigenous Communities: A Scoping Review.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Prehospital and inter-facility transport, such as air medical retrieval and pre-birth evacuation, often move Indigenous patients in rural and remote settings out of their communities, where care is already shaped by fragmented funding and structural inequities; no review has mapped these pathways globally. This scoping review mapped evidence on prehospital emergency response and patient transport for this population.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A librarian-assisted PubMed, Embase, and Scopus search was conducted for English-language publications on March 9, 2026. Eligible studies included an explicit rural Indigenous population with a defined prehospital pathway. Two reviewers independently screened titles and abstracts and assessed full texts, and a third reviewer resolved disagreements.
