We uploaded facial photographs and simulated medical profiles to a secure cloud-based app. Participants used a tablet to scan the patient's face (standardized patient or actor). Successful matches returned identifying information, medical history, emergency contacts, preferred hospital, and primary care physician contact information. The 48 experimental participants had access to this patient information, while the 42 controls did not, even if they scanned the face. Standardized patients (SP) portrayed a noncommunicative urosepsis patient. Participants reported their findings to the facilitators and evaluated the technology on a 5-point Likert scale.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We analyzed 90 study participants (48 experimental, 42 control), of whom 40/48 (83.3%) experimental group identified the SP compared with 9/42 (21.4%) control group (OR [odds ratio], 13.87; 95% CI, 5.03-38.25; P < .001). Identification of important medical information of the SP by the study participants occurred in 30/48 (62.5%) in the experimental group versus 4/42 (9.5%) in control (OR, 15.83; 95% CI, 4.84-51.76; P < .001). Correct transport decision to the preferred hospital occurred in 27/48 (56.3%) experimental participants compared with 10/42 (23.8%) controls (OR, 4.11; 95% CI, 1.65-10.23; P = .02). Overall, 80% of participants reported that the technology would benefit their day-to-day clinical work.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The use of a cloud-based facial-recognition application significantly improved firefighter-paramedics' ability to identify noncommunicative patients and access critical medical information, with an appropriate transport decision to the patient's preferred hospital.

articles.title: Perspectives on Influenza Vaccination Among COVID-19 Unvaccinated Patients in US Emergency Departments: A Qualitative Study.
articles.journal_full: The western journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Efforts to increase influenza vaccine acceptance must consider the importance of patient education and familiarity with vaccinations and influenza in the emergency department (ED), particularly for populations without another primary source of healthcare. This is the first study, to our knowledge, to assess in-depth perceptions regarding the influenza vaccine and identify barriers and facilitators to influenza vaccination among COVID-19 unvaccinated adult ED patients.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a qualitative idiographic interview study from July 12, 2021, to September 24, 2021, at four EDs in urban cities across the United States. We recruited adult ED patients (18 years and older) unvaccinated for COVID-19, without a primary care clinician, who were fluent in either English or Spanish. The primary finding was a detailed understanding of patient perceptions regarding the influenza vaccine, with secondary findings assessing influenza vaccination rates, barriers and facilitators to being vaccinated, sources of information, and future vaccination intentions. We used a content analysis approach to identify themes around patient experiences, concerns, barriers, information sources, and future intentions regarding influenza vaccination.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 65 participants interviewed, 48 discussed the influenza vaccine and were included in this analysis. Among these participants, the median age was 34 years, 21 (43.8%) were women, and 14 (29.2%) were Hispanic. We found three core themes influencing influenza vaccine hesitancy: 1) previous experiences with influenza illness and/or the vaccine; 2) knowledge about the influenza vaccine; and 3) confidence in vaccine safety and effectiveness. In our cohort, 10 (20.8%) participants demonstrated knowledge of the purpose and mechanism of the influenza vaccine. In addition, 14 (29.2%) patients suggested they would accept the vaccine if offered, while 18 (37.5%) patients stated they did not plan to receive the influenza vaccine and/or expressed strong hesitancy due to concerns about lack of vaccine effectiveness, fear of side effects, and lack of concern regarding influenza illness.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Our findings identify an important barrier that could be overcome by ED-based vaccine education, particularly for underserved patient populations. Interventions to increase influenza vaccine uptake could focus on overcoming hesitancy related to prior experiences and understanding of vaccine safety and effectiveness.

articles.title: Modern management of third nerve palsy: neuroimaging triage and surgical rehabilitation.

abstract.text: Third nerve palsy (TNP) is a complex neuro-ophthalmic condition that requires rapid differentiation between benign microvascular ischemia and life-threatening or otherwise serious causes, including aneurysmal, neoplastic, inflammatory, infectious, demyelinating, traumatic, and cavernous sinus pathologies. Given the high prevalence of diabetes, understanding both pupil-involving and pupil-sparing presentations is critical. Current literature often fragments TNP management across isolated medical specialties. Rather than presenting an evidence-based consensus guideline, this paper provides an expert narrative synthesis proposing a bipartite clinical framework. This framework sequences acute neuro-ophthalmic triage (Weeks 1-12) and chronic ophthalmic rehabilitation (>6 months) to coordinate immediate etiological workup with subsequent surgical and rehabilitative planning. TNP manifestations vary based on the dual anatomy of the third nerve. Compressive lesions typically paralyze superficial pupillomotor fibers, whereas ischemic insults preserve them. Because pupillary status alone cannot definitively rule out emergencies, acute care triage requires neuroimaging tailored to the clinical context. Magnetic Resonance Angiography (MRA) and Computed Tomography Angiography (CTA) serve as primary modalities when an aneurysm is suspected; contrast-enhanced MRI is preferred when brainstem, cavernous sinus, orbital, inflammatory, infectious, or neoplastic pathology is suspected; and CT is used first in acute trauma. Digital Subtraction Angiography (DSA) is reserved for specific cases to detect microaneurysms smaller than 3 mm when initial imaging is inconclusive. Chronic or unresolving cases are managed through sequentially planned interventions, where strabismus alignment is typically prioritized before ptosis repair. Ultimately, this review proposes an evidence-informed, phase-based framework designed to support the timely identification of potentially fatal etiologies and guide individualized functional and esthetic rehabilitation. Multidisciplinary collaboration, utilizing prospective registries, is essential to address current data gaps and enhance long-term rehabilitative success in patients with TNP.

articles.title: Immediate changes in self-reported apprehension and uncertainty across 41 emergency scenarios following a structured emergency medicine course.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Emergency physicians face high cognitive and emotional stress in acute care, especially in prehospital settings. Structured training is an essential component of emergency medicine education and may increase familiarity with high-pressure clinical situations. In Germany, an 80-hour standardized emergency physician course is mandatory for certification.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE/DESIGN
abstract.text: This study evaluated the impact of this course on physicians' self-perceived apprehension and uncertainty in acute emergency scenarios using a prospective pre-post design.

abstract.label: SETTINGS AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: The study was conducted in five consecutive emergency courses. 162 physicians from different specializations and departments throughout Germany completed pre- and post-course questionnaires.

abstract.label: INTERVENTION
abstract.text: Participants completed the standardized 80 h course, which combines theoretical instruction, structured decision-making, team communication, and high-fidelity simulation.

abstract.label: ANALYSIS
abstract.text: The primary endpoint was the change in a single combined self-reported rating of apprehension and uncertainty, assessed using a 5-point Likert scale across 41 questionnaire items. Analyses of the predefined categories constituted secondary analyses, while analyses of the 41 individual items and subgroup analyses were exploratory.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A significant overall reduction in combined self-reported apprehension and uncertainty was observed. Improvements occurred across all seven predefined categories. The greatest reductions were found for intraosseous access and ocular emergencies. Pediatric and neonatal emergencies remained the most apprehension-provoking scenarios. Exploratory subgroup analyses provided no evidence of differences in improvement across medical specialties or according to board certification status, whereas participants with prior EMS experience showed a smaller improvement than those without prior EMS experience.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Course participation was associated with lower immediate post-course self-reported apprehension/uncertainty scores.

articles.title: Synovial fluid biomarker changes after acute anterior cruciate ligament injury: comparison with primary osteoarthritis as a biological comparator.

abstract.label: BACKGROUNDS
abstract.text: Post-traumatic osteoarthritis (PTOA) typically develops 10-20 years after anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury, but reliable early biomarkers are lacking. We examined synovial fluid biomarker changes in patients with acute ACL injury (PTOA-risk group) and in patients with primary OA. The primary OA group served as a biological comparator representing established degenerative OA, not as a healthy or matched control.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Our study included patients from January 1, 2021 to September 30, 2023: 51 with primary OA biological comparator and 53 with acute ACL injury (PTOA-risk group). Levels of Interleukin (IL)-1β, sulfated glycosaminoglycans (sGAG), aggrecan neoepitope fragment (ARGS-aggrecan), and cartilage oligomeric matrix protein (COMP) were measured in synovial fluid and compared between the two groups at baseline and one year later. Patients underwent unilateral knee MRI and bilateral weight-bearing radiography at follow-up.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The findings demonstrated that synovial fluid from acute ACL injury (PTOA-risk group) and primary OA biological comparator contained inflammatory mediators, collagen markers, and aging-related indicators such as CRP. Following one year of surgical follow-up, PCT, GAG, CTxI, osteocalcin, β-aspartate, and COMP all showed significant decreases. Biomarker comparisons between groups revealed that the primary OA biological comparator had significantly lower levels of CRP, GAG, ARGS, BMP2, FGF-10, and ADAM-TS5 than the ACL-injured (PTOA-risk) group, while CTX-II showed no discernible difference. The Spearman rank correlation was used to examine synovial fluid biomarker concentrations relative to injury duration. Significant time-dependence was observed for: IL-1b (p = 0.025, Rs=-0.112), GAG (p = 0.011, Rs=-0.265), ARGS aggrecan (p = 0.032, Rs=-0.021), C1,2 C (p = 0.002, Rs=0.665), CTxI (p = 0.025, Rs=0.251), C2C (p = 0.011, Rs=0.055), CPII (p = 0.015, Rs=0.336), Osteocalcin (p = 0.029, Rs=0.114), β-aspartate (p = 0.001, Rs=-0.77), D-Asx (p = 0.0215, Rs=-0.425), MMP-3 (p = 0.0201, Rs=0.356), and WOMAC (p = 0.001, Rs=0.264). Univariate regression analysis demonstrated significant associations of IL-1β and osteocalcin with ACL-injured (PTOA-risk) group membership. Multivariate logistic regression revealed significant associations with increased levels of β-aspartate, WOMAC, GAG, IL-1β, and osteocalcin. LASSO regression analysis was employed as an exploratory feature selection method to identify the biomarker panel that best distinguished between the ACL-injured (PTOA-risk) group and primary OA biological comparators within this cohort. Among the 20 variables included in the analysis, five demonstrated non-zero coefficients in the LASSO model: WOMAC, GAG, β-aspartate, IL-1β, and osteocalcin. These findings suggest that inflammatory markers, matrix turnover products, and functional status are prominent features differentiating the acute post-injury state from chronic degenerative OA in this dataset. However, given the exploratory nature of this analysis and the lack of external validation, these results should be interpreted with caution and require confirmation in independent cohorts.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Our findings demonstrate that patients with acute ACL injury (PTOA-risk group) exhibit distinct synovial fluid molecular signatures compared with a primary OA biological comparator. These signatures encompass acute inflammatory responses and early matrix remodeling. However, this study cannot explain why only approximately 18.8% of ACL-injured patients later develop PTOA. Future longitudinal studies including ACL-injured non-progressors and age-, sex-, and activity-matched controls are required.

articles.title: Cost and operational impact of a molecular point-of-care test for sexually transmitted infections in the emergency department.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Female patients presenting to the emergency department (ED) with suspected sexually transmitted infections (STIs) have historically been evaluated using centralized laboratory testing (CLT), with results unavailable during the visit. Point-of-care (POC) tests enable real-time diagnosis but have higher direct costs than CLT.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To compare hospital and societal costs of CLT and POC STI testing (chlamydia, gonorrhea, trichomonas) among female ED patients with suspected infection, and to assess effects on underdiagnosis, overtreatment, undertreatment, and ED recidivism.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Decision analysis through cost tables using data from a pre-post implementation study.

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: Large urban academic ED (Johns Hopkins Hospital).

abstract.label: INTERVENTIONS
abstract.text: CLT (nucleic acid amplification test [NAAT]/wet preparation) versus molecular POC STI testing.

abstract.label: MEASUREMENTS
abstract.text: Direct testing costs, follow-up costs for informing patients after discharge, costs of overtreatment/undertreatment, and ED return visits within 30 days. Analyses were conducted from hospital and societal perspectives over 12-month horizon.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Direct POC testing costs for 1000 women exceeded CLT by $16,502. This difference was not offset by lower follow-up costs for undertreatment or by societal costs of under- or overtreatment. From the hospital perspective, costs may be offset by increased margins from maximizing ED Examination room utilization. Threshold analysis shows room time need not be fully occupied, nor margins equal full revenue, to achieve net revenue gain.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: POC testing for STIs, given current pricing and unchanged reimbursement, increases societal costs and reduces hospital revenue versus CLT. However, EDs and hospitals may increase net revenue, by improved patient throughput thereby generating revenue if ED wait times are long.

articles.title: Teaching Modalities for Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy Education: A Systematic Review and Narrative Synthesis.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To systematically identify and synthesise the available evidence on teaching modalities for hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) education across all learner levels.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang, SinoMed, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library from inception to 15 June 2026 for studies evaluating any HBOT teaching or training intervention against traditional instruction or another comparator, with knowledge, skills, or learner satisfaction as outcomes. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool for randomised trials, ROBINS-I for comparative non-randomised studies, and MMAT/JBI checklists for descriptive and survey designs. Because of marked design heterogeneity, findings were synthesised narratively following the SWiM guideline. An exploratory synthesis of extractable effect sizes was undertaken to characterise the direction and magnitude of reported effects. The protocol was retrospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261462169).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Thirty studies met the inclusion criteria (nine English-language, 21 Chinese-language). The evidence base was dominated by single-group pre-post evaluations, descriptive curriculum reports, and cross-sectional surveys; only four randomised controlled trials were identified. Technology-enhanced modalities-simulation-based education, blended/online learning, and Web-based simulation-were generally associated with promising improvements in knowledge and skills, although most studies lacked an active comparator. The exploratory synthesis identified only two studies with extractable knowledge outcome effect sizes, both implausibly large (g > 2.0), likely reflecting small-sample bias, absence of blinding, and practice effects.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The available evidence suggests that technology-enhanced teaching modalities are promising for HBOT education, but the field lacks methodologically rigorous comparative studies and no study yet demonstrates consistent superiority over traditional didactic teaching. The anomalously large effect sizes in the few quantitative studies signal a high risk of bias and an urgent need for adequately powered randomised trials with blinded outcome assessment, standardised outcome measures, and a consensus-derived competency framework.

articles.title: Focused Cardiac Ultrasound and Doppler Hemodynamics in Nephrology Practice.

abstract.text: Point-of-care ultrasonography (POCUS) in nephrology is evolving beyond kidney imaging and procedural guidance toward integrated hemodynamic assessment. Distinguishing reduced forward flow from elevated filling pressures and venous congestion remains challenging in patients with acute kidney injury and cardiorenal syndromes. This educational review discusses the clinical reasoning behind incorporating basic and advanced cardiac POCUS into nephrology practice. We highlight the interpretation and limitations of ventricular size and function, inferior vena cava assessment, stroke volume and left ventricular outflow tract Doppler, left ventricular filling pressures, right-sided and pulmonary artery pressures, and right ventricular outflow tract Doppler, with emphasis on how these findings may influence fluid removal, volume administration, and vasoactive therapy. The complementary role of venous excess ultrasound (VExUS) in assessing the downstream consequences of systemic venous congestion is also discussed. Rather than relying on isolated sonographic parameters or rigid cutoffs, cardiac POCUS findings should be integrated with multisystem ultrasound and the broader clinical context. Familiarity with these principles can help nephrologists obtain focused, repeatable hemodynamic information at the bedside and translate sonographic findings into more physiologically informed clinical decisions.

articles.title: Case Report: Delayed epirubicin extravasation-induced ulceration in a dog managed without surgical intervention using adjunctive hyperbaric gaseous cryotherapy.

abstract.text: Extravasation of anthracyclines can result in progressive tissue injury, ulceration, and necrosis, and may ultimately require surgical intervention. Management of delayed presentations remains challenging, as recommended treatments, including dexrazoxane, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), and cold compresses, are most effective when initiated promptly after the extravasation event. A 9-year-old spayed female Poodle with suspected stage IV multicentric lymphoma developed a progressive ulcerative lesion 17 days after suspected epirubicin extravasation, by which time the recommended treatment window for standard interventions had elapsed. Given the progressive ulceration, severity of tissue injury, and delayed presentation, surgical debridement was considered. However, conservative management was pursued owing to the patient's limited prognosis and the owner's preference to prioritize quality of life. Treatment included hyperbaric gaseous cryotherapy (HGC) as the principal adjunctive modality, based on prior clinical experience in wound management and pain control. Dexrazoxane, topical DMSO, and ice-pack application were also incorporated despite the elapsed therapeutic window, as few alternative treatment options remained at that stage. Progressive wound healing was observed over the course of treatment, with complete re-epithelialization achieved by day 93 without surgical intervention. The wound remained fully healed until the patient died of progressive lymphoma on day 138. This case documents complete wound resolution without surgery in a dog with delayed epirubicin extravasation managed with multimodal conservative treatment incorporating adjunctive HGC.

articles.title: The golden hour: the feasibility of a quality improvement project to decrease the time to antibiotic administration in children with cancer and febrile neutropenia in Jordan.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Febrile neutropenia (FN) is a potentially life-threatening condition in pediatric oncology; early antibiotic initiation is associated with improved survival. A quality improvement (QI) project was implemented in the Pediatric Emergency Room (ER) to improve the timeliness of antibiotic administration.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Starting in July 2019, the project was designed using the Find, Organize, Clarify, Understand, and Select-Plan, Do, Check, and Act (FOCUS-PDCA) framework. We aimed to give antibiotics within 60 min of ER arrival for children with suspected FN. High-risk patients received antibiotics without waiting for blood count confirmation. A structured staff education campaign was conducted over 6 months, and performance metrics were continuously monitored. Outcomes were compared with retrospective data from December 2018 to June 2019.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The pre-intervention cohort included 119 children with cancer, accounting for 158 FN episodes. From July 2019 to December 2024, during the intervention period, 697 children with cancer (median age 4.7 years; IQR 2.6-9.2 years; 54% male) presented with FN, accounting for 1,164 ER visits (median 1 visit/patient; range, 1-11). The median absolute neutrophil count (ANC) at presentation was 50 cells/μL (IQR, 0-180 cells/μL). Median time from ER arrival to antibiotic administration decreased from 120 min (IQR, 97-143) at pre-intervention baseline to 50 min (IQR, 40-65) across the implementation period (p < 0.01). The time from antibiotic ordering to first dose remained stable (median 32 min; IQR, 25-40), while time from arrival to antibiotic ordering decreased from 53 to 15 min (p < 0.01). Compliance with the 60 min target improved from 22% in the pre-intervention period to a sustained 85%-90% range across 2021-2024, with the ≥90% target met in all 12 months of 2021 and compliance declining to 85.8% in 2024. The target was increased to 90% in September 2020.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: A structured Golden Hour QI initiative is feasible, effective, and associated with substantial and sustained improvement in antibiotic timeliness in the Middle East region, without additional funding, staffing, or technology. The core drivers of sustained improvement were automatic Category-A triage for children with cancer presenting with fever, pre-ANC antibiotic initiation for high-risk cases, and monthly audit-feedback cycles - all implementable within existing workflows.

articles.title: Directional immuno-metabolic signatures following severe trauma are associated with organ-specific clinical endpoints in a prospective cohort.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Severe trauma elicits evolving immune-metabolic responses that may differ across clinical endpoints. We characterized time-resolved innate and adaptive immune patterns associated with higher or lower endpoint odds during the first 96 h after injury.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Of 62 patients prospectively enrolled in the observational PRIME study (ISS >15), 52 met the prespecified analytical completeness criterion. Clinical and immune biomarkers were assessed at emergency room admission (ER), 24, 48, and 96 h. Time-point-specific quartile deviations were evaluated using logistic regression against microbiological culture positivity during hospitalization, creatinine-defined renal impairment, Berlin-defined ARDS of any severity, hepatic enzyme elevation, and four hemodynamic endpoints. Complementary sensitivity analyses and bootstrap resampling assessed the exploratory associations and their internal stability.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Microbiological culture positivity was associated with lower admission base excess and temperature, reduced CD4/CD8 ratios and CD4+ T-cell proportions at 24-48 h, and lower monocyte measures with higher IL-8 at 96 h. The 96-h monocyte CBC/IL-8 combination showed an apparent within-cohort AUC of 0.78. Creatinine-defined renal impairment was associated with lower admission pH and base excess and a higher-IL-8/lower-CD4/CD8 combination (apparent AUC 0.88), alongside later myeloid and lymphocyte-related alterations. Berlin-defined ARDS showed predominantly low-odds associations, including higher early pH and phagocytic capacity; its 96-h combination of lower phagocyte CD64 expression and lower lymphocyte percentage yielded an apparent AUC of 0.80. Hepatic enzyme elevation showed low-odds associations involving higher 96-h monocyte HLA-DR expression and lower CD64+ phagocyte counts (apparent AUC 0.78). Hemodynamic endpoints showed distinct, endpoint-specific high-odds configurations. Bootstrap selection reproducibility was limited for the retained multivariable combinations.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The evaluated clinical endpoints were associated with distinct directional immune-metabolic configurations rather than a uniform inflammatory response. Their hypothesis-generating contribution lies in the endpoint-specific organization of established biological components across serial sampling points. These exploratory candidate signatures require independent validation before their potential clinical relevance can be established.

articles.title: Standardized 4-step surgical approach to address atrial fibrillation during coronary artery bypass grafting in a patient with severely reduced left ventricular function: a case report.

abstract.text: Atrial fibrillation (AF) may result in haemodynamic deterioration and is particularly detrimental in patients with severely impaired left ventricular function. In this high-risk population, the maintenance or restoration of sinus rhythm (SR) in cardiac surgery are of paramount importance, warranting the use of all available surgical strategies to comprehensively address atrial fibrillation. We report the case of a 60-year-old man who underwent successful out-of-hospital cardiopulmonary resuscitation following an acute myocardial infarction. Coronary angiography revealed severe three-vessel coronary artery disease, accompanied by highly reduced left ventricular function. The patient had a history of symptomatic paroxysmal AF and had recently undergone electrical cardioversion to restore SR after the index myocardial infarction. In addition to surgical coronary revascularization via median sternotomy, a standardized four-step concomitant AF procedure was performed. This approach included bipolar radiofrequency ablation, exclusion of the left atrial appendage, transection of the ligament of Marshall, and left-sided posterior pericardiotomy. The patient was successfully weaned from cardiopulmonary bypass in SR and maintained stable SR throughout an 8-month follow-up period without AF recurrence. This case highlights the importance of systematically addressing AF during cardiac surgery, especially in high-risk patients with severely reduced ventricular function, where maintenance of sinus rhythm may have haemodynamic benefits.

articles.title: Young ERC Masterclass journal club article: intubation trends and survival in paediatric in-hospital cardiac arrest - a critical appraisal.
Intra-arrest blood pressure monitoring during paediatric in-hospital cardiac arrest: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To evaluate the use of intra-arrest blood pressure monitoring and association between blood pressure thresholds and outcomes in infants and children.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A systematic review was performed, registered with PROSPERO (CRD42024590080). We executed the search strategy on MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials all years until April 1, 2026. We used GRADE and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale to assess the evidence found. Critically important outcomes included return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), survival to hospital discharge, and survival with favourable neurological outcome, as defined in the Paediatric Core Outcome Set for Cardiac Arrest.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Six studies were included in the final analysis. Two studies (577 events) were pooled. A diastolic blood pressure (DBP) of ≥25 mmHg for infants <1 year and ≥30 mmHg for children 1-≤18 years, averaged over the first ten minutes of CPR, was associated with improved rates of ROSC, survival to hospital discharge, and survival with favourable neurological outcome, with very low certainty of evidence. The analysis did not find a statistically significant association for intra-arrest systolic blood pressure (SBP) thresholds and the described outcomes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In infants and children with invasive arterial monitoring in place during IHCA, a DBP of ≥25 mmHg (infants) or ≥30 mmHg (children) during the first 10 min of CPR was associated with improved survival and neurological outcome. The evidence is observational and of very low certainty, and does not establish that titrating resuscitation to these thresholds improves outcomes.The protocol for this systematic review was registered as PROSPERO ID CRD42024590080.

articles.title: Golden Hours in Disaster Response and Early Clinical Outcomes: An Analysis of the First 24 Hours of the Kahramanmaraş Earthquake.

abstract.text: Background: This study examined the association between admission time within 24 h of the Kahramanmaraş earthquakes and trauma severity, rhabdomyolysis, and in-hospital mortality, and its potential as a temporal reference for field triage in mass-casualty incidents. Methods: This retrospective study included earthquake-related injury patients who presented to our tertiary emergency department within 24 h of the earthquake onset (04:17, 6 February 2023). Non-survivors who died before diagnostic work-up, and therefore had no laboratory results or trauma scores, were excluded from the analysis. Patients were compared by admission within the golden hour (≤6 h) or later (>6 h); laboratory samples were obtained within the first hour of presentation. Mortality predictors were examined using univariate and multivariable logistic regression, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis evaluated admission time for predicting rhabdomyolysis. Results: Three of 63 patients (4.8%) died; lower Glasgow Coma Scale scores and higher trauma severity indices were associated with mortality, whereas admission time and entrapment were not (very few deaths). Patients admitted after 6 h had higher Abbreviated Injury Scale (AIS) grades and significantly higher creatine kinase (CK), creatine kinase-MB isoenzyme (CK-MB), lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), C-reactive protein (CRP), and international normalized ratio (INR) values and longer hospitalizations. Admission time predicted rhabdomyolysis well (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.840; cutoff: 9 h) and correlated positively with log-transformed CK (r = 0.733). Conclusions: The initial temporal window may be associated with muscle and organ injury severity among patients reaching hospital, but does not support redefining the golden hour as a survival determinant across the care continuum. The time threshold is hypothesis-generating and requires external validation before field triage use.

articles.title: Emergency Department-Centered Digital Health Transformation: Narrative Review and Three-Pillar Implementation Framework.
articles.journal_full: The western journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Emergency departments (EDs) face escalating pressures from rising patient volumes, workforce shortages, and documentation burdens. Digital health technologies have shown promise individually, but most are implemented in isolation, limiting their collective impact. This narrative review synthesizes evidence for six digital health technologies applicable to the ED and proposes a three-pillar framework for their coordinated implementation, positioning the ED as a convergence point for health system digital transformation.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We searched PubMed and Google Scholar for peer-reviewed literature published from 2018 through July 2026 on ambient artificial intelligence (AI) documentation, telehospitalist programs, virtual nursing, remote patient monitoring, virtual specialty consultation, and postdischarge transitional care, prioritizing systematic reviews and meta-analyses. Fifty-one sources met inclusion criteria and were synthesized. We organized the technologies into three functional pillars: streamlining clinical workflows; expanding workforce capacity; and extending continuity of care. Outcomes included clinical, operational, and implementation measures. Experience from Houston Methodist, a nine-hospital health system, is presented as an illustrative example separate from the literature synthesis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of the 51 sources, 23 (45.1%) addressed streamlining clinical workflows, 16 (31.4%) expanding workforce capacity, and 12 (23.5%) extending continuity of care. Overall, 22 (43.1%) were ED-specific: 10, five, and seven within the respective pillars. Ambient AI documentation included 13 sources (seven ED-specific); telestroke included one ED-specific source. Evidence maturity varied by technology and setting. In non-ED settings, meta-analyses reported shorter documentation time with ambient AI documentation (standardized mean difference, -0.72; 95% CI, -0.99 to -0.45), lower hospital mortality with tele-intensive care (risk ratio, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.58-0.96), and lower odds of 30-day readmission with low-complexity post-discharge interventions (odds ratio [OR], 0.78; 95% CI, 0.66-0.92). Emergency department-specific evidence remained largely observational; one meta-analysis showed no mortality difference with telestroke (OR, 1.16; 95% CI, 0.94-1.43), while one systematic review found no demonstrable benefits from telephone follow-up post-ED discharge.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Current evidence supports individual digital health technologies in and around the ED. Based on implementation science principles and institutional experience, we propose that coordinated implementation across the three pillars may offer advantages over isolated deployments, a hypothesis warranting prospective comparative evaluation.

articles.title: Multimodal Imaging in Anomalous Aortic Origin of the Coronary Arteries: Contemporary Approaches to Risk Stratification.

abstract.text: Multimodal cardiac imaging has fundamentally reshaped the evaluation of anomalous aortic origin of the coronary artery, yet risk stratification remains challenging because anatomy, symptoms, and physiological demands vary widely across patients. This review summarizes contemporary anomalous aortic origin of the coronary artery classification and emphasizes anatomic features associated with higher risk, including interarterial and intramural courses, adverse ostial morphology, and compression related to the intercoronary pillar or myocardial bridges, which contribute to both fixed and dynamic ischemia. The complementary roles of echocardiography, coronary CT angiography with CT-derived fractional flow reserve, nuclear myocardial perfusion imaging, cardiac magnetic resonance, and hybrid anatomic-functional imaging are discussed, with attention to the specific clinical contexts in which each modality is most informative. Finally, we discuss the Vanderbilt management approach that integrates age, symptoms, detailed anatomic assessment, and functional testing to guide observation, exercise recommendations, invasive evaluation, and surgical intervention, with particular focus on individualized counseling and safe return-to-play decisions in young and athletic patients.

articles.title: Longer collapse-to-first-medical-contact interval is independently associated with ROSC in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: a paradoxical finding that may reflect case-mix differences.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Shortening prehospital time intervals is a cornerstone of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) management, with earlier medical contact generally assumed to improve survival. However, this assumption has rarely been scrutinized at the level of individual time metrics, particularly the interval from witnessed collapse to first medical contact (collapse-to-FMC), whose relationship with resuscitation outcomes independent of case-mix remains unclear. This study aimed to examine the association between core prehospital time intervals and the achievement of prehospital return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC).

abstract.label: PATIENTS AND METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective cohort study included 152 consecutive OHCA patients managed by the Cixi Emergency Center between April 2023 and March 2026. Time intervals were derived from synchronized dispatch center logs and onboard system timestamps, including dispatch-to-scene arrival, collapse-to-first medical contact, and collapse-to-CPR initiation intervals. Candidate variables for multivariable modeling were selected based on a prespecified causal rationale and clinical relevance, rather than solely on univariate statistical significance. Univariate logistic regression was performed for descriptive purposes to examine crude associations with prehospital ROSC. The main model included the two core time intervals (collapse-to-FMC and collapse-to-CPR initiation). Model 1 further adjusted for age, a clinically important confounder that did not reach statistical significance in univariate analysis. Model 2 additionally adjusted for etiology of arrest and presence of a shockable rhythm, which were selected a priori as pre-exposure confounders based on established prognostic importance in OHCA research. This approach ensured that clinically important confounders were retained regardless of their univariate P values. A main model included only time variables, and an adjusted model further incorporated clinical covariates. Multicollinearity was assessed using variance inflation factors, and model calibration was evaluated with the Hosmer-Lemeshow test. Discriminative ability was assessed by receiver operating characteristic curve analysis. Subgroup analyses were performed by age (<65 vs. ≥65 years) and etiology (cardiac vs. non-cardiac).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 152 patients, 52 (34.2%) achieved prehospital ROSC. Conventional dispatch-related intervals did not differ between groups. The collapse-to-first medical contact interval was significantly longer in the ROSC group (20.0 vs. 13.1 min, P < 0.001) and remained independently associated with ROSC after adjustment for prespecified pre-exposure confounders, including age, etiology of arrest, and presence of a shockable rhythm (OR 1.188, 95% CI: 1.079-1.307, P < 0.001). Bootstrap internal validation yielded an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.882 (95% CI: 0.827-0.936), with a calibration intercept of -0.063, a calibration slope of 0.972, and a Brier score of 0.132, indicating adequate calibration. In subgroup analyses, this association was predominantly observed in patients younger than 65 years (adjusted P = 0.037), and the interval from collapse to CPR initiation became significant in the cardiac etiology subgroup after adjustment (OR 1.567, 95% CI: 1.054-2.329, P = 0.026).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In this cohort of OHCA patients, a longer collapse-to-first medical contact interval was paradoxically associated with increased odds of prehospital ROSC, independent of prespecified pre-exposure confounders. This counterintuitive finding suggests that the interval may reflect patient salvageability and unmeasured case-mix characteristics rather than treatment delay alone. These results challenge the conventional premise that shorter time to medical contact uniformly translates to better outcomes, and underscore the need for a more nuanced understanding of how patient characteristics shape the relationship between prehospital timing and resuscitation success.

articles.title: Emergency department nurse-led systematic nursing model for septic shock: impact on 1-hour bundle adherence and mortality.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate the impact of a systematic septic shock nursing model led by emergency department (ED) nurses on adherence with resuscitation protocols and clinical outcomes in patients with septic shock.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Our team employed the Delphi method to develop a systematic nursing model, and it was implemented in August 2023. To verify its application effect, a retrospective controlled study was conducted in the emergency resuscitation room of the First Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University. Patients who met the Sepsis-3 criteria for septic shock were consecutively enrolled from January 2022 to February 2025. According to the nursing model received during different periods, they were divided into two groups: the control group (enrolled from January 2022 to July 2023, n = 331) received conventional nursing, and the observation group (enrolled from August 2023 to February 2025, n = 343) received the systematic nursing model led by emergency nurses. Propensity score matching (1:1, caliper value 0.2) was used to balance differences. Primary outcomes included the 1-hour bundle adherence rate, 28-day and 90-day mortality, and 24-hour resuscitation success rate. Secondary outcomes included SOFA score, duration of vasoactive agent use, mechanical ventilation duration, ICU length of stay, and incidence of adverse events.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: After propensity score matching, 524 patients were successfully matched, with 262 patients in each group. The 1-hour bundle adherence rate was significantly higher in the observation group than in the control group (23.66% vs. 14.12%, p = 0.005), although the absolute adherence rate remained low in both groups. Compared with the control group, the observation group showed a significant decreases in 28-day and 90-day mortality, and a significant increase in the 24-hour resuscitation success rate (p < 0.05). Moreover, SOFA scores were significantly reduced, and both the duration of vasoactive agent use and ICU length of stay were shortened (p < 0.05). The incidence of adverse events was also significantly lower in the observation group (p < 0.05).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The systematic nursing model led by ED nurses significantly improves adherence in patients with septic shock, reduces short and medium-term mortality, enhances organ function recovery, and shortens ICU length of stay, demonstrating good potential for clinical implementation.

articles.title: Association of the ISAR Score with Clinical and Operational Outcomes in Older Emergency Department Patients.

abstract.text: Background/Objectives: The Identification of Seniors at Risk (ISAR) score is widely used to identify older emergency department (ED) patients at increased risk of adverse outcomes. However, its association with immediate disposition and operational outcomes remains incompletely characterized. This study evaluated the association of ISAR scores with hospital admission and emergency department length of stay (EDLOS). Methods: This retrospective observational cohort study included ED presentations of patients aged ≥65 years at a tertiary university emergency department in 2024. Of 12,105 eligible presentations, 10,090 (83.4%) had a documented ISAR score and constituted the descriptive cohort; 9401 presentations with classifiable admission status were included in the primary admission analysis. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, presenting complaint, triage category, treating specialty, and referral source. The incremental contribution of ISAR beyond routinely available clinical variables was assessed by nested model comparison and receiver operating characteristic analysis. Prolonged EDLOS was defined as ≥6 h. Results: Higher ISAR scores were independently associated with hospital admission and prolonged EDLOS. In the continuous-score admission model, each one-point increase in ISAR was associated with higher odds of admission (OR 1.155, 95% CI 1.121-1.191; p < 0.001), although categorical sensitivity analysis demonstrated a nonlinear association with a plateau at higher scores. ISAR alone showed modest discrimination for admission (AUC 0.589, 95% CI 0.577-0.600). Addition of ISAR to the clinical model increased the AUC from 0.696 to 0.705 (ΔAUC = 0.009, 95% CI 0.005-0.012; p < 0.001). Median EDLOS increased from 326 min (IQR 215-494) at ISAR 0 to 596 min (IQR 324-1312) at ISAR 6. After adjustment including hospital admission status, each one-point increase in ISAR was associated with higher odds of prolonged EDLOS (OR 1.178, 95% CI 1.143-1.214; p < 0.001). Conclusions: Higher ISAR scores were associated with both hospital admission and prolonged EDLOS. ISAR provided statistically significant but modest incremental prognostic information beyond routinely available clinical variables and should be regarded as a geriatric risk-screening tool rather than a stand-alone disposition instrument. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether ISAR-guided clinical pathways improve patient or operational outcomes.

articles.title: Associations of Secondary Traumatic Stress and Emotional Labor with Suicidal Ideation Among Emergency Dispatch Personnel in South Korea: A Cross-Sectional Moderated Mediation Analysis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Emergency dispatch personnel are repeatedly exposed to callers' distress and emotionally demanding interactions, yet suicidal ideation in this workforce remains understudied. This study examined associations of secondary traumatic stress (STS) and emotional labor with suicidal ideation, including indirect associations through depression and conditional associations involving social support.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A cross-sectional correlational study was conducted among 211 fire-service personnel assigned to emergency dispatch centers in Busan and Gyeongnam, South Korea. Data were analyzed using Hayes' PROCESS macro Model 59 with HC3 standard errors and 5000 bootstrap resamples.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Social support moderated the associations of STS with depression and suicidal ideation and the association of depression with suicidal ideation. The conditional indirect association of STS with suicidal ideation through depression decreased across low, mean, and high social support (0.191, 0.076, and 0.013). For emotional labor, the emotional labor × social support interaction was significant in the depression model, and its association with depression and indirect association with suicidal ideation through depression were supported at low and mean, but not high, social support.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: STS and depression were associated with suicidal ideation, and the indirect association of STS through depression was weaker at higher social support. However, moderation findings involving suicidal ideation should be interpreted cautiously because the corresponding interaction terms were not statistically significant in the Tobit sensitivity analysis.

articles.title: Shoulder Dislocation Reduction Using Inhaled Nitrous Oxide in the Emergency Department: Retrospective Case Series.
articles.journal_full: The western journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Inhaled nitrous oxide (iNO) offers rapid onset analgesia with a favorable safety profile yet remains underused for shoulder dislocation reductions in the emergency department (ED). The objective of this study was to evaluate the use and outcomes of iNO for shoulder reduction in the ED, including whether intravenous (IV) access was required, whether successful reduction could be accomplished without additional analgesic or sedative medications under procedural sedation, and the rate of adverse effects from iNO.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective chart review of shoulder dislocation reductions using iNO at two high-volume EDs over three years (2019-2022). Data collected included age, sex, indication, procedural success, IV placement, medications administered, and adverse events and was stored in a password-protected database. The primary endpoint was successful reduction with iNO as the primary procedural analgesic; secondary endpoint was occurrence of any adverse events.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 138 patients, 125 (90.6%; 95% CI, 0.84-0.95) achieved successful reduction with iNO alone without escalation to procedural sedation; 102 patients (74%) did not require IV access. Adverse events were rare (2/138 or 1.4% [95% CI, 0.02-0.05]): one patient experienced transient agitation (a known side effect of N-methyl-D-aspartate antagonism), and one had vomiting. Both were self-limited without hemodynamic changes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This retrospective case series, the largest of its kind to date examining iNO for shoulder dislocation reduction, demonstrated a 90.6% success rate with minimal adverse events and reduced resource utilization compared to procedural sedation. These findings support further prospective investigation of iNO for shoulder dislocation as well as other orthopedic reductions and painful ED procedures.

articles.title: Effects of Racial Concordance and Perceived Racism on Emergency Department Patient Satisfaction.
articles.journal_full: The western journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Racial disparities in healthcare persist, with evidence suggesting that bias contributes to inequities in care and outcomes for Black patients. Racial concordance between patients and clinicians has been proposed as one strategy to improve patient satisfaction and health outcomes, but its impact in acute care settings such as the emergency department (ED) remains underexplored. The objective of this study was to assess how racial concordance between patient and clinician, together with patient perceptions of how race affected their care, influence patient satisfaction with care in the ED.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This secondary analysis used data from a previously published text message-based survey of patients discharged from two EDs between August and September 2021. Patients were categorized as not completely discordant if at least one clinician (physician, advanced practice clinician, or nurse) shared their self-identified race. The primary outcome was patient ratings of experience with ED care (scored 0 = poor to 5 = excellent). Multivariable ordinal logistic regression was used to assess associations between racial concordance, perceived impact of race on care, and experience ratings.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 516 respondents, 195 (37.8%) were classified as not completely discordant with at least one emergency clinician. Not completely discordant patients reported significantly lower experience ratings (scored 0 to 5) compared to racially discordant patients (median, 4 [3-5] vs 5 [3-5]; P = .01). In multivariable ordinal logistic regression, racial concordance was not independently significant in patient experience.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Contrary to expectations, in our population, racial concordance was not significantly associated with satisfaction in ED care. In the adjusted analysis, perceived negative impact on care due to race was the strongest independent predictor of lower overall satisfaction. These findings suggest that how patients perceived the role of race in their care may be more influential than simply patient-clinician concordance in the acute care setting. Further research is needed to investigate these factors in more diverse patient-clinician population and other ED settings to help inform policies focused on advancing health equity.

articles.title: English versus Non-English Language Preference and Computed Tomography Use in Pediatric Minor Head Trauma.
articles.journal_full: The western journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Whether the use of computed tomography (CT) in pediatric minor head trauma varies by documented language preference (English vs non-English), independent of race, is not well understood. Our objective was to identify factors associated with head CT use among children with minor head trauma in an institutional Pediatric Emergency Care Applied Research Network (PECARN)-based pathway.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients 2 to 14 years of age presenting with minor head trauma, January 2019 to June 2022, who were classified as low, intermediate, or high risk using PECARN criteria. Our primary outcome measure was a three-level clinical pathway: no CT and no traumatic brain injury (TBI); clinical TBI without CT; or CT performed. Secondary outcomes were CT positivity and short-term clinical outcomes. Multinomial logistic regression assessed associations between pathway and language preference, age, headache, weighted observed symptom score (OSS), and race (White vs non-White).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 1,167 patients, 319 (27.3%) underwent CT, 132 (11.3%) had clinical TBI diagnosis without CT, and 716 (61.4%) had neither; 430 (36.8%) were classified intermediate risk-the subgroup in which the imaging decision is most discretionary. Non-English language preference was associated with lower adjusted odds of CT in the intermediate-risk subgroup (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.48; 95% CI, 0.24-0.92; P = .03) but not in the full cohort (aOR, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.50-1.22; P = .27). Within the intermediate-risk subgroup, OSS was strongly associated with CT use (aOR, 3.65; 95% CI, 2.67-5.00; P < .001) and headache with clinical TBI without CT (aOR, 4.94; 95% CI, 1.64-14.90; P = .005), whereas race was not independently associated with CT use (aOR, 1.36; 95% CI, 0.82-2.25; P = .48). Language preference was not associated with CT positivity among scanned patients (aOR, 1.10; 95% CI, 0.44-2.72; P = .84), and short-term outcomes did not differ by language (all P > .35).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Documented non-English language preference was independently associated with lower use of head CT in PECARN intermediate-risk children; race was not after adjustment for clinical severity. Yield and short-term outcomes did not differ by language preference among imaged patients; however, imaging selection precludes conclusions about mechanism.

articles.title: The international Red Cross and nurses in the context of the Brazilian press (1864-1907).
articles.journal_full: Revista da Escola de Enfermagem da U S P

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To investigate the visibility of the Red Cross and the work of nurses at the national and international levels during the period 1864-1907.

abstract.label: METHOD
abstract.text: A historical study employing documentary analysis of newspaper articles, with the Brazilian Digital Newspaper Archive serving as the primary source.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 37 news articles were identified, 21 in the Jornal do Commercio and 16 in the Gazeta de Notícias. Internationally, most articles addressed armed conflicts, highlighting the Red Cross's role in blood banks, emphasizing the importance of nursing in wartime and the need for professional training. Nationally, the Federalist Revolution (1893-1895) stands out, with the organization of relief commissions and the dispatch of volunteers-such as nurses, doctors, and religious figures-to carry out humanitarian work during internal conflicts and to build an identity linked to the international principles of the Red Cross.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The Brazilian press from 1864 to 1907 contributed to the promotion of the Red Cross and the recognition of the importance of wartime nursing.

articles.title: Role of Cardiogenic Shock Centres and Regionalised Networks for Acute MI-related Cardiogenic Shock: State-of-the-art Review on Behalf of the British Cardiovascular Interventional Society Focus Group.

abstract.text: Cardiogenic shock (CS) complicating acute MI (AMI-CS) remains associated with high mortality and morbidity, despite advances in coronary revascularisation and mechanical circulatory support (MCS). Outcomes are determined not only by individual therapies, but also by the organisation of care, with current guidelines emphasising multidisciplinary, system-level approaches to enable rapid diagnosis, triage and treatment. This review examines how CS centres function within regional networks of care. We review definitions of AMI-CS, including haemodynamic, clinical and biochemical markers and their application to early identification and triage. We summarise key components of centre-based management, including revascularisation, invasive haemodynamic assessment, selective MCS use and post-percutaneous coronary intervention critical care. Contemporary data from dedicated CS centres and regionalised network models are compared, highlighting variations in transfer criteria and hub-spoke organisation alongside limitations in current evidence. The distinct phenotypic nuances of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest-associated CS are discussed and gaps in evidence with future perspectives are highlighted.

articles.title: Chemsex as a challenge for emergency medical teams: a narrative review.

abstract.text: Chemsex, defined as the intentional use of psychoactive substances before or during sexual activity, has emerged as an important public health concern and an increasingly relevant challenge for emergency medical services (EMS). Although most frequently described among men who have sex with men, sexualized substance use is increasingly reported among heterosexual men and women, indicating a broader at-risk population. Commonly used substances include methamphetamine, mephedrone, gamma-hydroxybutyrate/gamma-butyrolactone (GHB/GBL), alkyl nitrites, and other psychoactive agents, frequently used in combination during prolonged sexual sessions. Such practices are associated with a wide spectrum of acute complications, including agitation, psychosis, hyperthermia, cardiovascular instability, respiratory depression, altered consciousness, and mixed toxidromic presentations. This narrative review examines current evidence regarding chemsex-associated emergencies from a prehospital and emergency medicine perspective. Particular attention is given to syndromic clinical presentations, including hyperstimulatory syndromes, behavioral disturbances, acute GHB/GBL toxicity, and polysubstance-related emergencies. Operational challenges relevant to EMS teams, including scene safety, communication barriers, stigma, occupational risks associated with slamsex, and management of agitated patients, are also discussed. Chemsex-related emergencies share many clinical features with other substance-related emergencies. However, recognition of the sexualized substance use context may provide additional information relevant to prehospital assessment, including intentional drug combinations, repeated dosing, potential drug interactions, communication barriers, and occupational safety considerations. A syndromic approach focused on recognition of dominant clinical patterns rather than identification of individual substances may therefore provide the most practical framework for prehospital assessment and management. Although chemsex-associated emergencies are documented, evidence regarding their frequency and trends remains limited, particularly in prehospital settings. Further research is needed to support the development of evidence-based prehospital protocols, educational initiatives, and integrated care pathways.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence in emergency trauma perioperative management: applications, performance benchmarks, and translation barriers.

abstract.text: This review examines the current status of artificial intelligence (AI) applications in the perioperative management of emergency trauma. Published studies suggest performance advantages of AI over traditional methods in prehospital triage, radiographic injury detection, massive transfusion prediction, and early warning of postoperative complications, although findings vary across study designs and validation settings. However, actual adoption in trauma care remains limited due to data heterogeneity, performance degradation in external validation, workflow integration challenges, lack of interpretability, and a scarcity of prospective interventional evidence. This review further argues that methodologically inflated benchmark performance constitutes an underrecognized barrier to adoption in its own right, and that bridging the implementation gap will likely require a shift from area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC)-centered reporting toward reporting sensitivity at prespecified clinical thresholds and evaluating patient outcomes in prospective interventional trials.

articles.title: Biomarkers for differential diagnosis of myocarditis, acute coronary syndrome, and sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy.

abstract.label: BACKGROUNDS
abstract.text: Diagnosing acute myocardial injury remains a significant challenge in contemporary cardiovascular and critical care medicine. Myocarditis, acute coronary syndrome (ACS), and sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy (SICM) frequently present with overlapping features, chest pain, elevated cardiac biomarkers, and electrocardiographic abnormalities, yet require divergent management, making rapid and accurate etiological diagnosis essential for optimal patient outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the pathophysiology and biomarker signatures of myocarditis, ACS, and SICM, and examines how these signatures can be integrated into a practical diagnostic approach for the emergency department and intensive care unit.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) remains the central biomarker of acute myocardial injury, but its kinetics differ across the three conditions. A steep rise and fall in ACS, a sustained moderate elevation in myocarditis, and a gradual, severity-parallel course in sepsis. Among complementary biomarkers, C-reactive protein lacks specificity, whereas procalcitonin supports the recognition of bacterial sepsis in SICM, and natriuretic peptides reflect myocardial wall stress, disproportionately elevated relative to troponin in SICM. Emerging molecular biomarkers, circulating microRNAs (like miR-4763-3p and miR-155) and extracellular matrix remodeling markers, show promise for distinguishing inflammatory from ischemic myocardial injury, but remain investigational owing to the lack of standardized assays and practical constraints on acute bedside use. Therefore diagnosis rests on an integrated, multimodal assessment.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The differential diagnosis of acute myocardial injury requires a systematic, biomarker-centered multimodal approach. Future research should prioritize the prospective validation of multi-biomarker panels and the development of rapid non-invasive tools to reduce reliance on emergency coronary angiography.

articles.title: Emergency medical services personnel's work capability sets: associations with job demands, job resources, and flourishing at work.

abstract.text: Emergency Medical Services (EMS) personnel perform complex and demanding work under challenging conditions while providing essential healthcare services. Understanding the factors that support their flourishing at work is important for their sustainable employability and the functioning of healthcare systems. This study investigated EMS personnel's work capability sets (enabled and achieved valued work outcomes) and their associations with job demands (emotional demands and work pressure), job resources (autonomy at work and co-worker support), flourishing at work (emotional, psychological, and social well-being), and negative affect. A cross-sectional survey design was used with 197 EMS personnel in South Africa. Participants completed the Job Demands-Resources Questionnaire, the Capability Set for Work Questionnaire, and the Flourishing at Work-Short Form. Correlation analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, latent class analysis, and Bolck-Croon-Hagenaars analyses were conducted. Using knowledge and skills, developing knowledge and skills, and building and maintaining meaningful relationships at work emerged as the strongest work capabilities, whereas earning a good income, involvement in important decisions, and contributing to something valuable were the weakest. Latent class analysis identified three distinct capability sets: a weak capability set (48%), a constrained capability set (30%), and a robust capability set (22%). Emotional demands were negatively associated with work capabilities and flourishing and positively associated with negative affect, whereas work pressure was positively associated with negative affect but not significantly associated with overall work capabilities or flourishing. Job demands did not significantly differentiate the capability sets, whereas autonomy and co-worker support did. EMS personnel in the robust capability set reported greater flourishing and lower negative affect than those in the weak capability set. The findings are consistent with the Sustainable Employability model grounded in the Capability Approach showing that broader capability sets are associated with greater flourishing at work. Strengthening enabling work conditions, particularly autonomy and co-worker support, while attending to demands that may constrain work capabilities, may help create conditions conducive to the realization of valued work outcomes, flourishing, and sustainable employability among EMS personnel.

articles.title: A tale of two nails: A retrospective cohort comparison of TFNA and PFNA in proximal femoral fracture fixation.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: The aging population has transformed proximal femoral fractures into a public health crisis, resulting in an increased burden of postoperative complications and revision surgeries. While the Proximal Femoral Nail Antirotation (PFNA) has been a standard in certain countries, the Trochanteric Fixation Nail Advanced (TFNA) was introduced with engineering refinements intended to enhance fixation. This study aims to compare the two implants, specifically focusing on fixation failure rates and distinct biomechanical failure mechanisms.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective cohort study at an Academic Level I trauma center involving 1006 patients treated between January 2020 and March 2025. Patients with a minimum six-month follow-up were included (681 PFNA, 325 TFNA). Radiographic assessments, including reduction quality, Tip-Apex Distance (TAD), and blade positioning, were independently performed by two senior fellowship-trained surgeons. The primary outcome was fixation failure requiring reoperation.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The fixation failure rate was 1.6% (n = 11) in the PFNA group and 3.4% (n = 11) in the TFNA group; however, this difference was not statistically significant. While radiographic parameters such as TAD and reduction quality did not differ significantly between the failure groups, a distinct shift in biomechanical failure modes was identified. PFNA failures were overwhelmingly characterized by the classic "cut-out" mechanism (91%), whereas TFNA failures frequently involved medial migration or "cut-through" (55%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Although the TFNA was associated with a higher absolute rate of fixation failure, no statistically significant difference in fixation failure rates was observed between the two implants. However, the failure profile shifted toward medial "cut-through" migration with the TFNA. These findings suggest that the TFNA may possess a unique failure profile, potentially reflecting a learning curve or specific biomechanical properties. Suboptimal reduction and blade positioning were frequent among the failures and may have contributed to them; however, a considerable proportion of failures occurred after a reduction graded as good. These findings emphasize that technical precision remains the primary determinant of stability, regardless of the cephalomedullary device used.

articles.title: Co-Evolutionary Sensor Deployment Optimization for Layered Low-Altitude Airspace Monitoring Under Worst-Case Traffic Composition.

abstract.text: Layered sensor networks that monitor low-altitude airspace must detect heterogeneous aerial traffic, yet sensor deployment is usually optimized against a single fixed traffic case and can leave an entire target kind undetected when the composition changes. This paper formulates deployment against worst-case traffic composition through a high-low transition (HL) trajectory model, a library of 35 target templates in four kinds, and a per-kind fairness objective f4, the worst per-kind miss rate. An adaptive co-evolution (ACE) framework trains deployments against a co-evolved, kind-diverse population of traffic cases with a hall of fame and a robust final selection, and ACE-A6 instantiates it with a sensor-count dispatcher. Over four scenarios with five, four, three, and two sensors; 30 seeds; and two independent sets of 60 held-out cases, ACE-A6 lowers the worst per-kind miss rate of four state-of-the-art evolutionary optimizers on the four-, three- and two-sensor scenarios with large effect sizes (Cliff's δ≥ 0.44, Holm-corrected p<0.05). Equal-budget experiments locate the gain in the training framework: each of five optimizers trained inside ACE breaks the f4,max=1 ceiling, and ACE-A6 performs on par with them. The advantage persists under probabilistic detection, masking, position error and moderate library shift.

articles.title: Workplace Violence Exposure and Burnout Among Fire-Service-Based Paramedics in South Korea: The Indirect Association Through Post-Traumatic Stress Symptoms and the Moderating Roles of Social Support and Resilience.

abstract.text: Background/Objectives: This study examined the indirect association between workplace violence exposure and burnout through post-traumatic stress symptoms (PTSS) and the moderating roles of social support and resilience among South Korean fire-service-based paramedics. Methods: This analytical cross-sectional study included 210 paramedics in Busan, South Korea. Conditional process analyses were conducted using PROCESS Model 8, with social support and resilience examined in separate models. Results: Workplace violence exposure was positively associated with PTSS, which was positively associated with burnout. Conditional indirect associations were significant at the mean of each moderator. In the final sample (N = 210), social support moderated the associations of workplace violence exposure with PTSS (p = 0.002) and burnout (p = 0.015), and its index of moderated mediation was significant (-0.024, 95% bootstrap CI [-0.041, -0.009]). However, the social support interaction predicting PTSS and its index of moderated mediation were statistically significant only after excluding one influential observation (N = 210 vs. N = 211). The social support interaction predicting burnout remained significant in both samples. Resilience did not significantly moderate the PTSS association; its nominally significant interaction predicting burnout did not remain significant after Holm correction, and its index of moderated mediation was not significant. Conclusions: Social support may play a moderating role in the associations linking workplace violence exposure, PTSS, and burnout, although some findings were sensitive to the exclusion of one influential observation. These cross-sectional findings require cautious interpretation and further replication.

articles.title: Implementation of a low-cost trauma intake form with real-time clinical decision support: Mixed-methods findings from a stepped-wedge clinical trial in Ghana.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Most injured patients in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) receive care from non-specialist providers at smaller hospitals lacking trauma experience and standardized protocols. A trauma intake form (TIF) with real-time clinical decision support prompts was developed to address this gap. This study examined key implementation outcomes, including adoption, usability, acceptability, appropriateness, feasibility, and sustainability.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This study was conducted at six district and two regional hospitals in Ghana as part of a hybrid effectiveness-implementation stepped-wedge clinical trial. Direct observation of 4077 injured patients over 17.5 months was combined with a structured questionnaire administered to all 241 participating clinicians, alongside thematic analysis of open-ended responses.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Overall observed TIF uptake was 85.6%, with five of eight hospitals classified as adopters. Implementation outcomes were consistently positive across qualitative and quantitative measures, with high levels of acceptability, appropriateness, feasibility, and usability reported across both adopting and non-adopting facilities. Barriers included time constraints, a lack of pre-existing documentation culture, and a perception among some clinicians that patients were too sick to prioritize use of the form.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The TIF achieved high adoption among non-specialist providers in a resource-limited setting, demonstrating that low-cost, contextually developed tools can bridge the gap between clinical effectiveness and implementation success. Sustained scale-up will require structural solutions to address time and documentation barriers, targeted training to correct the misperception that the tool is unsuitable for the most severely injured patients, and embedded feedback mechanisms to maintain clinician engagement.

articles.title: Safety and Analgesic Consumption Impact of Continuous Peripheral Regional Analgesia in Earthquake-Related Crush Injury: A Retrospective Cohort Study.

abstract.text: Background: The 6 February 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquake caused an unprecedented burden of crush-related extremity trauma. Continuous peripheral regional analgesia is frequently used in these patients, but its safety regarding renal outcomes and its effect on systemic opioid consumption have not been quantified in comparative cohort data. Methods: We conducted a retrospective, exploratory cohort study of 181 hospitalizations (141 patients) following the earthquake, comparing patients who received a continuous peripheral nerve catheter with those managed without one. No prospective sample-size calculation was performed. The primary outcome was acute kidney injury (AKI), defined per adapted KDIGO criteria; the secondary outcome was systemic opioid exposure, assessed both as opioid-days and, in a dose-based sensitivity analysis, as morphine milligram equivalents (MME). Because patients contributed multiple admissions, regression models used cluster-robust standard errors. A propensity-score-matched sensitivity analysis (age, sex) addressed confounding by indication, and intensive care unit (ICU) days were added as a further covariate in sensitivity models. Results: Catheter and non-catheter groups had similar age (p = 0.369) but differed in length of stay (median 42 vs. 16 days) and surgical procedures (10 vs. 2), reflecting catheter-selection criteria; detailed injury-severity and comorbidity data were not available for either group. Catheter use was not significantly associated with AKI (adjusted OR 0.49, 95% CI 0.16-1.47, p = 0.203) or with systemic opioid-day rate (adjusted RR 1.15, 95% CI 0.88-1.51, p = 0.294). Results were materially unchanged after adding ICU days as a covariate (AKI OR 0.42, p = 0.148, n = 123; opioid-days RR 1.23, p = 0.223, n = 160) and when opioid exposure was expressed as MME per day (adjusted ratio 1.32, 95% CI 0.73-2.38, p = 0.361, n = 165). A propensity-matched analysis (26 pairs) was concordant for all outcomes. Conclusions: In this exploratory, hypothesis-generating cohort, we did not detect a significant association between continuous regional analgesia and either AKI risk or opioid consumption across six complementary analyses. These non-significant findings do not establish equivalence or safety, particularly given wide confidence intervals, a modest number of events, incomplete clinical characterization, and residual confounding that could not be fully resolved with the available data; they should be regarded as hypothesis-generating pending confirmation in better-characterized, adequately powered, multicenter cohorts.

articles.title: Redundancy-Based Validity Screening of Strain-Gauge Records from In-Service Hydraulic Turbine Servomotors.

abstract.text: Strain gauges on the push-pull rod are a practical means of measuring the load on in-service hydraulic actuators, but the channels degrade silently, and a degraded channel still yields a credible-looking load characteristic. A redundancy-based validity screen for such records is presented and applied to every record from four guide-vane servomotors of Francis units under wind-photovoltaic-hydro complementary dispatch. Four elementary screens are combined: channel coherence with an applicability floor, configuration sensitivity of the interval loading gradient against a tolerance band built from fifteen reference channel configurations, step magnitude, and abscissa integrity. The screen refuses none of the reference configurations, in sample or under leave-one-out.
