UGRA promotes healing, reduces opioid use, and improves pain management. Although there are risks, safety and accessibility are enhanced by careful technique, monitoring, and advances such as portable ultrasonography and AI. Standardized training is necessary for optimal use.

articles.title: Penetrating thoracoabdominal injuries: belly first or chest first?
articles.journal_full: Kardiochirurgia i torakochirurgia polska = Polish journal of cardio-thoracic surgery

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Penetrating thoracoabdominal injuries raise a critical surgical question: which cavity should be explored first, the chest or the abdomen? In unstable patients, an incorrect initial approach may delay control of the dominant life-threatening injury.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: The aims of this study were to describe the clinical characteristics of patients with penetrating thoracoabdominal injuries, analyze the sequence of operative interventions, and evaluate the appropriateness of initial cavity selection.

abstract.label: MATERIAL AND METHODS
abstract.text: We performed a retrospective cohort study of adult patients with penetrating thoracoabdominal injuries who underwent emergency surgical treatment at Kyiv City Clinical Hospital No. 17 between January 2000 and December 2023. For the purpose of this analysis, patients were stratified according to the initial operative approach into chest-first and abdomen-first groups. The primary outcome was the appropriateness of initial cavity selection, defined as control of the dominant life-threatening injury through the initially selected surgical access without an urgent need to proceed to the opposite cavity.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The study population consisted of 111 patients with penetrating thoracoabdominal injuries requiring emergency surgical intervention. The mechanisms of injury were stab wounds in 99 (89.2%) patients, gunshot wounds in 7 (6.3%) patients, and penetrating injuries involving impacted foreign bodies in 5 (4.5%) patients. According to the initial operative approach, 69 patients were assigned to the chest-first group and 42 patients to the abdomen-first group. A single-cavity operation was sufficient in 74 patients, whereas 37 patients required sequential or repeated access to another cavity. Thoracotomy alone was performed in 40 patients, laparotomy alone in 34 patients, and combined or repeated procedures in 37 patients. The mean estimated blood loss was 836 ml. Emergency department thoracotomy was performed in 18 (16.2%) patients. Incorrect initial cavity selection occurred in 6 patients (5.4% of the total cohort; 16.2% of patients requiring combined or repeated access). The mortality rate was 0.9%, with 1 death among 111 patients.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Penetrating thoracoabdominal injuries should not be managed according to a universal "chest-first" or "abdomen-first" rule. The initial operative approach should be guided by hemodynamic status, suspected source of bleeding, imaging findings, chest tube output, and mechanism of injury. Although most patients in this cohort were successfully managed through the initially selected cavity, surgeons should remain prepared for rapid conversion to the opposite cavity when the initial assessment proves incorrect.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence-driven advancements in radiation biodosimetry.
articles.journal: Mutat Res Genet Toxicol Environ Mutagen
articles.journal_full: Mutation research. Genetic toxicology and environmental mutagenesis

abstract.text: Radiation dose estimation is fundamental to the effective management of radiological emergencies, where prompt and accurate assessment is critical for medical intervention. Conventional biodosimetry methods, including the dicentric chromosome assay (DCA), premature chromosome condensation (PCC), γ-H2AX foci detection, cytokinesis-block micronucleus (CBMN) assay, and fluorescence in situ hybridisation (FISH) translocation analysis, remain important approaches for biological dose estimation. However, their conventional implementation can involve labour-intensive sample preparation and manual or semi-automated analysis, require specialised expertise, and have limited scalability for mass-casualty events. Recent advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), offer considerable potential to enhance biodosimetry through automated image analysis, multimodal data integration, and accelerated dose assessment. DL approaches, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), enable high-throughput image analysis and automated identification of radiation-induced cytogenetic damage. Furthermore, integrating explainable AI (XAI) approaches may improve model transparency, interpretability, and confidence in clinical applications. This review examines current advances, challenges, and prospects of AI in radiation biodosimetry, highlighting its potential to support rapid, accurate, reproducible, and scalable dose assessment in radiological emergencies.

articles.title: Optimising planned patient transportation: A qualitative descriptive study of current practices in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.
articles.journal_full: South African family practice : official journal of the South African Academy of Family Practice/Primary Care

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Planned patient transportation is a key component of healthcare provision in KwaZulu-Natal. However, persistent inefficiencies in the transportation system have been associated with suboptimal health outcomes among patients. Understanding current planned patient transportation practices is therefore imperative to guide improvements in the Emergency Medical Care referral system. This study aimed to describe current planned patient transportation practices in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A descriptive qualitative design was employed. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 11 purposively selected Emergency Medical Services managers, and five focus group discussions were conducted with 35 pre-hospital emergency care providers recruited using maximum variation purposive sampling. Data were transcribed verbatim and analysed thematically using NVivo. Ethical approval was obtained from the relevant ethics committees.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Findings revealed four superordinate themes related to enablers of effective planned patient transportation: (1) digital transformation and operational innovations; (2) stakeholder collaboration and community engagement; (3) decentralised healthcare delivery; and (4) policy coherence.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Planned patient transportation is essential for healthcare access and continuity of care but remains constrained by coordination, resource, organisational and policy challenges. Strengthening referral systems, stakeholder communication, policy standardisation, digital health systems and resource allocation may improve transportation effectiveness and support patient-centred, equitable primary healthcare delivery in KwaZulu-Natal and similar settings.Contribution: The findings provide insights to guide planned patient transportation service improvement through system strengthening and process enhancement.

articles.title: Explaining Variation in the Percentage of Admissions for Patients Aged 80 and Over in Municipal InPatient Acute Care Services: A Cross-Sectional Analysis From Norway.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Municipal Inpatient Acute Care (MIPAC) units in Norway provide short-term inpatient services, but structural and contextual disparities, spanning resources, competence, and accessibility, may affect utilization patterns.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To examine to what extent variation in the percentage of admissions involving patients aged ≥80 years across MIPAC units is associated with structural and contextual conditions.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Cross-sectional study using aggregated register and survey data.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The analytical sample included 147 MIPAC units, corresponding to 68% of the 215 units in the administrative dataset. Descriptive statistics describe sample characteristics and admissions by age group. Pearson correlations assessed interrelationships and multicollinearity before regression analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The model explained 38% of the variance. Unit location, registered nurse coverage, and driving distance to the nearest emergency department were associated with the percentage of admissions involving patients aged ≥80 years. Units located in GP out-of-hours clinics had a lower percentage compared to nursing home-based units (B = -17.12, 95% CI [-23.51 to -10.73], β =-0.41, p < 0.001). Greater registered nurse coverage (B = -0.12, 95% CI [-0.22 to -0.02], β = -0.18, p = 0.021) and longer driving distance to the nearest emergency department (B = -0.07, 95% CI [-0.11 to -0.04], β = -0.31, p < 0.001) were also associated with lower percentages. The estimate for the proportion of adults ≥80 years in the MIPAC catchment area was positive, but uncertain, as the confidence interval included zero (B = 1.76, 95% CI [-0.06 to 3.57], β = 0.20, p = 0.057).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: MIPAC admission patterns for the oldest patients were associated with both service configuration and local context. These findings highlight variation in the use of MIPAC services across different units. Future research should examine how structural and contextual factors are related to patterns of MIPAC utilization and explore the mechanisms underlying these associations.

articles.title: Auricular Battlefield Acupressure: A Promising Non-Pharmacologic Therapy for Pain in the Emergency Department.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Assess the utility of Battlefield Acupuncture (BFA) protocol with beads (BFA-B) to treat pain in the emergency department (ED).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective chart review was performed for patients who received BFA-B in an inner city ED from 2019-2020.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Thirty-one charts were reviewed.

abstract.label: UNLABELLED
abstract.text: Eleven Pediatrics: The median age 13 years (range 8-19), 55% female, 91% of Hispanic.

abstract.label: UNLABELLED
abstract.text: Twenty Adults: The median age 39 years (range 21-73); 70% female, 40% Hispanic, 15% Not Hispanic or Latino, 45% unknown race/ethnicity.Pain locations as follows.For pediatric patients: Headache (7), abdomen (2), musculoskeletal (2).For adult patients: headache (8), abdomen (3), musculoskeletal (7), chest (3), flank (1), facial or eye (1), and not specified (1) Some patients had multiple pain locations.The Verbal Pain Scores 0-10 Scale was used. Combined pediatric and adult groups -Mean pre-acupressure pain score: 7.55 ± 2.01 SD.Mean post-acupressure pain score: 3.37 ± 2.53 SD.Mean change of pain score: 4.18 ± 2.38 SD (p < 0.001). Median time to lowest pain score: 32 min (range 3-146 min). No adverse events were noted.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Battlefield acupressure with beads may provide pain relief for adult and pediatric patients who present to the ED with various pain syndromes. Further investigation is warranted.

articles.title: Prevalence, determinants, and consequences of workplace violence in emergency departments - a systematic review.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Workplace violence, including physical assault, verbal abuse, and bullying, is a growing public health concern worldwide. EDs are consistently identified as high-risk environments due to overcrowding, high emotional stress, time pressure, and frequent interactions with distressed patients and relatives. In Pakistan, evidence on the prevalence and determinants of WPV in ED settings remains fragmented. This systematic review aimed to synthesize available evidence on the prevalence, forms, perpetrators, and contributing factors of workplace violence against healthcare professionals in emergency departments, with particular attention to findings from Pakistan within the broader international literature.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Four electronic databases (PubMed, ScienceDirect, Web of Science, and CINAHL) were searched for English-language peer-reviewed studies published between January 2015 and December 2025. Quantitative, qualitative, mixed-methods, and relevant evidence-synthesis studies examining workplace violence among healthcare professionals in emergency care settings were eligible for inclusion. Methodological quality and risk of bias were assessed and considered during interpretation of the findings.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Twenty-nine studies met the inclusion criteria. Across studies, the prevalence of workplace violence ranged from approximately 33% among healthcare workers in Pakistan to over 90% among emergency nurses in Taiwan. Verbal abuse was the most frequently reported form of violence, affecting 52-91% of healthcare professionals, while physical violence ranged from 7.8% to 74.9%. Patients and their relatives were consistently identified as the primary perpetrators. Major determinants included communication failures, prolonged waiting times, overcrowding, staff shortages, night-shift duties, and limited professional experience. Workplace violence was frequently underreported because of normalization of violence, lack of organizational support, and ineffective reporting systems. Reported consequences included psychological distress, anxiety, reduced job satisfaction, increased turnover intentions, and impaired perceptions of workplace safety.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Workplace violence against healthcare professionals in emergency departments is a common and multifactorial problem driven by interpersonal, organizational, and contextual factors. Addressing workplace violence requires comprehensive strategies that strengthen communication practices, improve reporting mechanisms, enhance workplace security, support healthcare workers, and address organizational contributors such as overcrowding and staffing shortages. Future research should prioritize multicenter studies, standardized measurement approaches, and evaluations of interventions designed to prevent workplace violence in emergency care settings.

abstract.label: CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER
abstract.text: Not applicable.

articles.title: Opening the Door to Sunrise: A Pediatric Integrative Chinese Medicine Approach to War-Related Trauma and Resilience.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Armed conflict exposes children to trauma and continuous threat, leading to high rates of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), anxiety, depression, and somatic complaints. Following the October 7, 2023, attacks and subsequent multi-front conflict in Israel, demand for mental health services increased substantially, highlighting the need for scalable supportive interventions. Pediatric complementary and integrative medicine (CIM), including Chinese medicine (CM) and mind-body approaches, may provide adjunctive tools for addressing trauma-related symptoms and promoting resilience in war-exposed children.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To respond to the rising need for CIM treatment for pediatric emotional distress, addressing both emotional and somatic manifestations of trauma and supporting resilience and post-traumatic recovery.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: A protocol, integrating principles of CM Five-Element theory with various pediatric CIM modalities, was developed during the acute phase of the conflict.

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: The protocol was initially implemented in the emergency department of Barzilai Medical Center, a hospital located near the Israeli-Gaza border, for children presenting with acute stress reactions and later disseminated to practitioners across Israel.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The Five-Element theory-based framework enables practitioners to address trauma-related emotional and somatic manifestations through targeted therapeutic strategies aimed at restoring regulation, stability, and adaptive functioning.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The Five-Element model may provide a structured approach for addressing trauma-related symptoms in war-exposed children and may support resilience and recovery when conventional mental health services are limited. Additional studies are required to explore the generalizability of this model in varied international settings where children are challenged by war-related concerns.

articles.title: Trends and demographic predictors of cefdinir use for common bacterial infections in children enrolled in Medicaid, 2016-2023.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To determine trends and predictors of cefdinir use for common pediatric infections in the United States.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Retrospective cohort study, 2016-2023.

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: U.S. outpatient encounters (ambulatory, emergency department, urgent care) included in the Medicaid MarketScan database.

abstract.label: PATIENTS
abstract.text: Children aged 0-18 years diagnosed with bacterial rhinosinusitis, pharyngitis, urinary tract infection (UTI), acute otitis media (AOM), or community-acquired pneumonia (CAP).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We assessed cefdinir prescription rates by diagnosis and year, comparing to other commonly administered antibiotics. We used logistic regression to identify demographic predictors of cefdinir use.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 7,346,547 encounters, most common diagnoses were AOM (36.9%) and bacterial pharyngitis (36.2%). Patients were predominantly non-Hispanic White (53.0%), 1-5 years-old (41.1%), and seen in ambulatory settings (75.3%). Cefdinir was prescribed in 10.4% of encounters, ranking among the top prescribed antibiotics. After an initial increase, use declined post-2020 to 7.6%. In children 1-18 years-old, younger age was uniformly associated with higher odds of cefdinir prescription across all diagnoses. This pattern was inconsistent among infants <1 years-old across diagnoses but persisted for UTI, with ORs of 9.38 (95% CI, 8.91-9.88) for <1 years-old and 5.91 (95% CI, 5.76-6.06) for 1-5 years-old versus 15-18 years-old patients. NH Black patients and those seen in urgent care or the emergency department were less likely to receive cefdinir.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Despite a small decline in use since 2020, cefdinir use remains substantial, especially among young children with UTI. Continued efforts to reduce inappropriate use and promote antibiotic stewardship are warranted.

articles.title: Point-of-care ultrasound use in the Canadian Armed Forces: Current practices, barriers, and opportunities for integration.
articles.journal_full: Journal of military, veteran and family health

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) enables real-time diagnostic imaging to support clinical decision-making and procedural safety. Its use is particularly relevant in military environments, where access to conventional imaging is often limited or unavailable. This study assessed current POCUS use, training and perceived barriers among Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) clinicians to guide future integration across clinical and operational contexts.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A cross-sectional survey was distributed to CAF clinicians between Sep. 6 and Nov. 24, 2024. The survey collected data on clinician demographics, POCUS training, device access, clinical applications, frequency of use, perceived barriers, and preferred modalities of future instruction. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize survey responses. The study received ethics approval from the Montfort Hospital Research Ethics Board and endorsement from the Surgeon General Health Research Program.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 112 clinicians completed the survey. Respondents included medical officers (61%), medical specialist officers (17%), physician assistants (16%), and nurse practitioners (6%). Prior POCUS training was reported by 73% of respondents, primarily through civilian courses and peer-led instruction. Only 59% reported current access to a POCUS device. Trauma (95%), cardiac (76%), and lung (72%) assessments were the most common applications. Barriers included limited device access (58%), insufficient training (41%), skill decay, and absence of institutional standards. POCUS use varied by clinical role and was less frequent in operational deployments.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: This study identified variability in POCUS training, access, and use across the CAF. A coordinated strategy involving clinical and non-clinical stakeholders may support more consistent implementation across CAF health care settings.

articles.title: [Microbiomics‑Based Prediction of Postmortem Interval in Rats with Ethanol Exposure Combined with CO Poisoning].

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To investigate the temporal changes of intestinal bacterial communities in rats that died from combined ethanol and carbon monoxide (CO) poisoning using microbiome analysis techniques, and to explore potential correlations between these changes and the postmortem interval (PMI).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Four experimental groups were established：fatal CO poisoning, fatal CO poisoning following ethanol exposure, ethanol exposure, and blank controls. Rectal specimens were collected at 0, 1, 3, 7, and 14 days postmortem. High-throughput sequencing of the 16S rRNA gene was employed to analyze bacterial communities. Bacterial diversity, relative abundance, and community differences were analyzed. A predictive model for PMI estimation using bacterial community succession patterns was constructed using a random forest algorithm.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The intestinal bacterial community structure of rats changed at both the phylum and genus levels within 14 days postmortem in the experimental groups. The PMI estimation model based on bacterial characteristics demonstrated good predictive performance across different experimental groups, with model fitting accuracies of 0.60, 0.59, 0.61 and 0.60 for each of the four groups. The average prediction error across all groups was approximately 1 day.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Ethanol exposure, CO poisoning, and the combined effects of ethanol exposure and CO poisoning all affect postmortem bacterial succession in rat cadavers. In forensic practice, it is recommended to adopt a predictive model specifically developed for the corresponding poisoning condition to improve the accuracy of PMI estimation.

articles.title: Self-perceived MHPSS competency and war-related exposure among nurses in Gaza: a cross-sectional study.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To assess self-perceived mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) competencies among nurses working in Gaza and examine differences according to demographic, professional, and war-exposure characteristics.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Nurses in conflict settings frequently provide psychosocial support while working under insecurity, mass casualties, disrupted services, and personal exposure to traumatic events. However, evidence regarding nurses' MHPSS competencies in Gaza remains limited.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A cross-sectional descriptive study was conducted among 102 nurses working in governmental hospitals, private hospitals, and health service points in Gaza. Data were collected between January-April 2026 using a structured self-administered questionnaire comprising demographic and professional characteristics, a 42-item MHPSS competency scale, and a 5-item war-related exposure scale. The response rate was 68%. Descriptive statistics, independent-samples t tests, one-way analysis of variance, and Pearson correlation analysis were performed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The overall mean MHPSS competency score was 2.83. Relatively higher scores were observed for strengthening support systems, problem-solving, professional boundaries, and knowledge of psychosocial resources, whereas lower scores were found for classification of mental disorders, anxiety-related disorders, support for unaccompanied children, and suicide-risk assessment. Self-perceived competency scores did not differ significantly according to demographic or professional characteristics. War-related exposure showed a weak positive correlation with overall MHPSS competency (r = 0.247, 95% CI = 0.055-0.421, p = 0.012), explaining approximately 6.1% of the variance in self-perceived competency(r² = 0.061). Older nurses and those with more than 10 years of experience reported significantly higher war-exposure scores.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Nurses in Gaza reported an overall self-perceived MHPSS competency score below the theoretical competent level, with relatively higher self-perceived competency in supportive-care domains and lower self-perceived competency in specialized psychosocial assessment and risk management. Although war exposure was positively associated with self- competency, the association was weak, suggesting that factors beyond war exposure contribute to self-perceived competency development. Unlike previous studies conducted in conflict-affected settings such as Yemen, Syria, and Ukraine, this study simultaneously examined nurses' self-perceived MHPSS competency and war-related exposure in Gaza, providing context-specific evidence from one of the world's most protracted humanitarian crises. Given the cross-sectional design and convenience sampling, causal inferences and generalizability should be interpreted with caution. These findings support the need for context-specific MHPSS education, ongoing clinical supervision, strengthened referral pathways, and staff-support strategies.

articles.title: The impact of simulation with debriefing on developing clinical competence and performance in paramedicine students.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Paramedics handle diverse medical and trauma cases, where any lapse in competency can compromise patient safety. Student paramedics must meet high standards set by oversight bodies to protect both the profession and the public. Growing evidence indicates that simulation facilitates attainment and reinforcement of clinical competencies. However, limited evidence explores the impact of simulation and debriefing on developing clinical competence in undergraduate paramedicine students. This study aimed to evaluate the association between weekly practice session performance and summative practical exam outcomes, assessing how simulation-based practice supports the development of clinical competence among paramedicine students.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective analysis of performance-based assessment data (2019-2024) in a university paramedicine program evaluated the role of high-frequency simulation. Second-year students participated in weekly three hour simulated practice sessions and a summative practical exam, with performance assessed using the Clinical Competence Assessment Tool (CCAT). Practice session data were grouped into tertiles to assess trends. Pearson's correlation measured the association between practice frequency and exam outcomes, paired samples t-tests evaluated performance progression, and hierarchical regression identified significant predictors of exam outcomes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Data from 305 students and 1,243 practice scenarios revealed a significant positive correlation between practice frequency and exam performance (r = 0.257, p < 0.001). Clinical competence scores improved progressively across the trimester, with the strongest correlation observed in the final tertile (r = 0.229, p < 0.001). Earlier tertiles showed weaker but statistically significant correlations (p < 0.05). A performance dip in 2020 due to reduced simulation exposure during COVID-19 further highlighted the critical role of consistent, high-frequency practice in fostering competence and exam success.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This study demonstrates the value of structured, high-frequency simulation and debriefing in enhancing clinical competence and exam performance. The findings underscore the importance of consistent practice, particularly in the final trimester weeks, supporting its integration into paramedicine curricula to ensure readiness for real-world practice and sustained competence.

articles.title: Profiles of active transportation injury survivors: findings from a British Columbia inception cohort.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Active transportation (AT) uptake is increasing as a result of its beneficial effects on health and the environment. Active transport injury (ATI) events that do not involve a motor vehicle are common but go unreported in traffic injury databases. This manuscript reports sociodemographic, pre-injury health, and injury-related factors of ATI survivors, as well as circumstances of ATI events.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This was a prospective inception cohort study of ATI survivors recruited between January 2022 and December 2023 from four emergency departments (EDs) in British Columbia, Canada. Participants were aged ≥ 16 years and arrived in a participating ED within 48 h of sustaining an ATI. Data were collected from structured interviews and review of medical records.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The cohort of 1,932 ATI survivors included 978 pedestrians, 524 cyclists, 168 e-cyclists, 161 e-scooter users, and 100 other micromobility device users. Mean (SD) age was 47.0 (19.3) years; 982 (51%) were female. Over two-thirds of pedestrians were female (70%), compared to a greater proportion of males in other transport modes. Pedestrians and e-cyclists were of older age. Overall pre-injury health was good, with minimal levels of psychological distress, and somatic symptom severity. Pre-existing alcohol, cannabis, and other recreational drug use was highest among other micromobility device users and lowest among pedestrians. The overall cohort had mild injury severity, with e-cyclists sustaining relatively more severe injury, whereas pedestrians and e-scooter users had the lowest injury severity scores. Motor vehicle involvement was reported in one quarter (27%) of incidents. Pedestrians and other micromobility device users were more likely to have been injured via a fall/collision with a stationary object; whereas, cyclists were more likely to have been injured via motor vehicle collision.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In a large cohort of ATI survivors, most participants reported good pre-injury health. Injury severity, patterns, and circumstances differed by transport mode; however, across all transport modes, motor vehicle involvement was present in only one quarter of incidents; emphasizing the importance of considering non-motor vehicle incident mechanisms when monitoring ATIs or informing priority areas for ATI prevention.

articles.title: Development and internal validation of a nomogram for in-hospital mortality in older adults with severe trauma: a secondary analysis of a single-center cohort.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Mortality after severe trauma remains high in older adults. Models developed in broader trauma populations may not perform similarly in this group. We developed and internally validated a penalized nomogram and assessed calibration, potential net benefit, missing-data uncertainty, model stability, and nonlinearity.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a secondary analysis of the publicly available single-center Peterer et al. cohort. Patients were eligible if they were aged > = 65 years, had Injury Severity Score > = 16, and had a recorded in-hospital mortality outcome. Missing predictors were handled with 20 chained-equation imputations; mortality was used as an auxiliary predictor but was not imputed. The primary ridge model included age, New Injury Severity Score, Glasgow Coma Scale, and lactate. A seven-predictor model was examined as a sensitivity analysis. We used 1000 bootstrap resamples for internal validation and also assessed calibration, nonlinearity, and decision curves.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 311 source records, 263 met the eligibility criteria and 153 patients died (58.2%). Model A had an apparent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.871 and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.863 (bootstrap test-AUC interval 0.855-0.873). Its calibration intercept was - 0.006, slope 1.053, observed-to-expected ratio 1.00, and Brier score 0.145; the mean bootstrap calibration slope was 1.006. The restricted cubic spline sensitivity model performed similarly (AUC 0.872; Brier 0.145). Model B had an apparent AUC of 0.888. In complete-score cases, recalibrated Trauma and Injury Severity Score, its age-extended form, and Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II had AUCs of 0.802, 0.822, and 0.722, respectively.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this selected single-center cohort, the ridge nomogram showed good discrimination and acceptable overall calibration after internal validation. Its transportability and clinical utility require external validation and prospective impact assessment. Because the source dataset lacked frailty, comorbidity burden, medication use, baseline functional status, and cognitive status, the model should be regarded as a prediction model for older adults with severe trauma rather than a geriatric-specific model.

articles.title: Association of mental health encounters in medical school with physician specialty in Ontario, Canada.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Mental health concerns among medical students are common and may influence specialty selection and early-career practice patterns. However, their potential impact on physician workforce distribution across specialties is not well understood.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a population-based cohort study of physicians newly registered with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario (CPSO) between 2008 and 2018. We linked CPSO demographic data with ICES (formerly known as the Institute for Clinical and Evaluative Sciences) health administrative databases using unique encoded identifiers. Mental health encounters were defined as ≥ 1 healthcare encounter for mental health or substance use in the two years prior to medical school graduation. The outcome was the first specialty listed at initial CPSO registration, reflecting physicians' earliest registered specialty upon entry into practice. We used multivariable logistic regression to examine the association between mental health encounters and specialty (with Family Medicine as the referent group) adjusting for age, sex, language proficiency, medical school, rurality and neighbourhood income quintile at age 16.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 7105 physicians (median age 26 years, 56% female), 46% entered Family Medicine (n = 3261). Compared with Family Medicine, physicians with a prior mental health encounter had lower odds of entering acute care specialties including Emergency Medicine/Critical Care (OR 0.48; 95% CI 0.35, 0.67), Surgery (OR 0.63; 95% CI 0.52, 0.77), Anaesthesia (OR 0.67; 95% CI 0.50, 0.91) and Internal Medicine/Neurology (OR 0.68; 95% CI 0.58, 0.80), and higher odds of entering Psychiatry (OR 1.55; 95% CI 1.22, 1.97).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Mental health encounters near medical school graduation are associated with early-career specialty registration. These findings may reflect differences in perceived or actual residency support, lifestyle considerations, or training demands across specialties.

abstract.label: CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER
abstract.text: Not applicable.

articles.title: Surge capacity challenges in emergency departments during sport-related mass gatherings.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Emergency departments (EDs) are critical components of healthcare systems and serve as the primary entry point for medical care during disasters and mass gatherings (MGs). Sporting MGs, particularly football matches, occur frequently in urban settings and can significantly influence patterns of healthcare demand. However, the broader impact of these events on ED utilization, beyond the immediate vicinity of stadiums, remains underexplored.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This multicenter, retrospective descriptive study analyzed ED admissions from three hospitals in Trabzon, Türkiye, during 47 official Trabzonspor football matches held between August 2021 and June 2022, and on 47 corresponding non-match days.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 214,535 ED admissions were analyzed, of which 104,597 occurred on match days and 109,938 on corresponding non-match days. No significant differences were observed in patient age (34.83 ± 22.32 vs. 34.85 ± 22.33; p = 0.848), sex distribution (female: 60.0% vs. 59.9%; p = 0.616), or mode of arrival by ambulance (2.6% vs. 2.5%; p = 0.559). However, total ED visits were significantly lower on match days compared with non-match days (p < 0.001). The proportion of medico-legal cases was significantly higher on match days (2.0% vs. 1.8%; p < 0.001), with traffic accidents (13.8%) and workplace injuries (10.5%) being the most frequent types. During the 2-hour match period, total ED visits decreased significantly compared with the equivalent period on non-match days (10368 vs. 12782; p < 0.001). Although ambulance arrivals were numerically higher during match hours (2.5% vs. 2.1%; p = 0.032), this difference did not remain statistically significant after Bonferroni correction. Medico-legal case presentations were also higher during match hours (2.2% vs. 1.6%; p = 0.002). These findings indicate that while overall patient volume declines during football matches, the relative burden of ambulance-transported and medico-legal cases increases, reflecting a qualitative shift in emergency care demand.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: These findings suggest that football matches, as recurring mass gatherings, can alter patterns of healthcare demand in urban EDs. From a surge capacity perspective, the simultaneous reduction in general patient volume and increase in ambulance and medico-legal case admissions indicate a shift in patient profile rather than an absolute reduction in healthcare needs. Therefore, preparedness strategies should not solely focus on the stadium environment but also anticipate city-wide implications, including increased risks of medico-legal incidents and ambulance utilization.

abstract.label: CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER
abstract.text: Not applicable.

articles.title: Frequent Callers to Emergency Medical Services: an observational cohort study from Region Zealand, Denmark (2018-2025).

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Frequent callers to Emergency Medical Services represent a small group of citizens who account for a substantial number of calls. Despite their impact, little is known about their characteristics and patterns of EMS use. This study aimed to examine frequency, dispatch outcomes, and characteristics of frequent callers in a prehospital setting.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted an observational cohort study of calls to the Emergency Medical Dispatch Center in Region Zealand, Denmark, between 2018 and 2025. Calls without a civil register number and individuals younger than 18 years were excluded. Frequent callers were defined as individuals contacting 1-1-2 five or more times within 12 consecutive months. Calls from frequent callers were categorized as pre-frequent calls (before reaching the threshold) and post-threshold calls (from the fifth call onward). Descriptive statistics were used to compare frequent callers with non-frequent callers, as well as subgroups of frequent callers based on call frequency.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Overall, 214 091 individuals made 443 977 calls. Of these, 3.0% (n = 6 415) were frequent callers, accounting for 19.9% (n = 88 260) of all calls. "Unclear problem" was the most common contact cause across all groups, whereas "Alcohol/intoxication/overdose" and "Psychiatry - Suicidal" were only among the five most common contact causes in the post-threshold groups with the highest call volumes. High-priority dispatch was assigned to 89.6% of non-frequent calls, 84.3% of pre-frequent calls, and 73.1% of post-threshold calls. Telephone resolution without ambulance dispatch increased across groups (7.3%, 12.5%, and 23.8%, respectively), as did non-conveyance after dispatch (19.2%, 20.8%, and 27.4%). Differences became more pronounced with increasing post-threshold call volume.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Frequent callers accounted for a substantial proportion of contacts to the Emergency Medical Dispatch Center. While pre-frequent calls resembled calls from non-frequent callers, post-threshold calls were more often resolved over the phone and less often resulted in hospital transport.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: Approval for performance of the study was given by the Emergency Medical Services in Region Zealand (p202519525).

articles.title: The perspectives of critical care nurses regarding the influence of staffing levels and workload on patients' care quality and safety: a qualitative study from Saudi Arabia.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: High-pressure environments, such as ICUs and EDs, require optimal staffing levels to ensure patient safety, maintain care quality, and support staff wellbeing. Inadequate staffing and excessive nursing workloads have been consistently linked to poorer patient outcomes. This study explores the perspectives of frontline critical care nurses regarding how staffing levels and workload influence the quality and safety of patient care.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A descriptive qualitative study was conducted at a public, government-funded tertiary hospital in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. Purposive-convenience sampling was used to recruit 12 full-time critical care nurses (7 from the intensive care unit and 5 from the emergency department) for semi-structured interviews. The majority (75%) were female and 66.7% were Saudi. The data were analysed using Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The analysis identified five major themes, summarized as follows: (i) workload reality: nurses consistently face unsafe nurse-to-patient ratios and physically demanding daily tasks; (ii) patient safety: high workloads force a rushed approach, causing delayed care and increasing the risk of incidents such as falls, self-extubation, and medication errors; (iii) nurse wellbeing: sustained workplace pressure leads to severe physical strain, psychological burnout, and high staff turnover; (iv) coping mechanisms: to manage demands, nurses rely heavily on informal team-based strategies; and (v) organizational improvements: proposed system-level interventions include hiring more registered nurses, utilizing patient care technicians (PCTs) for non-clinical tasks, and implementing automated charting.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Staff shortages and high workloads compromise patient safety, the consistency of care, and workforce wellbeing in ICU and ED settings. While teamwork serves as the primary coping mechanism, systemic organizational improvements are critically required, including improved staffing, clearer role delineation, a reduction in non-nursing tasks, and greater support for nurses' well-being to sustainably manage these high-pressure clinical environments.

articles.title: A brucellosis-associated vasculopathy presenting with focal neurological deficit: a case report in a pediatric patient with unique imaging.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Brucellosis is the most prevalent bacterial zoonosis worldwide. While neurobrucellosis occurs in 5-7% of the affected adults, it is a rare pediatric complication, with an estimated incidence of 0.8%. Limited knowledge of its presentations, diagnosis, and management leads to a significant delay in accurate diagnosis. Although rare, cerebrovascular accident is a leading cause of childhood mortality, 30-50% of which occurs in the context of cerebral vasculopathy. Infection is the most common etiology of secondary cerebral vasculopathies.

abstract.label: CASE PRESENTATION
abstract.text: A 10-year-old girl presented to the emergency department with a throbbing left-sided parietal headache, nausea, vomiting, photophobia, phonophobia, nuchal rigidity, and bilateral papilledema. Her initial symptoms began five months ago, including polyarthritis, limping, and conjunctivitis, accompanied by a progressively worsening headache and fever, which led to two prior hospitalizations at our institution. Past medical and familial history were unremarkable, except for a diagnosis of familial hypercholesterolemia. The clinical course was further complicated by a sudden onset of right-sided hemiparesis one day after admission. Brain MRI upon the focal neurologic deficit demonstrated an enhancing parasellar-suprasellar lesion that encased and significantly narrowed the left internal carotid artery along the cavernous to supraclinoid segments. The only remarkable laboratory findings were positive CSF inflammatory markers, elevated CSF 2-ME and serum anti-Brucella antibodies, and a positive CSF culture for Brucella species. The constellation of clinical, laboratory, and imaging findings led to a final diagnosis of left internal carotid perivascular granuloma in the context of neurobrucellosis. Treatment was initiated with anti-Brucella antibiotics and corticosteroids, resulting in complete resolution of the perivascular granuloma and clinical symptoms, with no residual sequelae.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This case demonstrates that cerebral vascular involvement can occur in pediatric neurobrucellosis. With prompt diagnosis and targeted therapy, this complication can yield a favorable outcome. Clinicians should include neurobrucellosis-associated cerebral vascular involvement in the differential diagnosis when evaluating pediatric patients who present with focal neurologic deficits in the setting of meningoencephalitis.

articles.title: An ecological time-series study of heat-related illness in Honolulu County, Hawai'i: implications for heat preparedness and public health response.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Heat-related illness (HRI) is a growing public health concern. HRI risk in Hawai'i has not previously been reviewed to determine the risks of heat on public health and well-being. This study summarizes HRI in Honolulu County and evaluates the relationship between local daily heat metrics and HRI by residency status.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Syndromic surveillance was used to collect clinical visits to hospital emergency departments, urgent care centers, and outpatient clinics for HRI in Honolulu County from January 2022 to December 2024. Associations between daily maximum heat metrics (dry bulb, wet bulb, and heat index) and HRI were estimated using Poisson regression with distributed lag non-linear models (DLNMs). Models incorporated a 3-day cumulative lag and were adjusted for temporal trends and day of the week, with relative risks estimated by comparing the 75th to the 25th percentile of each heat metric.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: During the study period, the syndromic surveillance system captured 969 HRI cases in Honolulu County; 698 (72.0%) occurred in residents and 271 (28.0%) in visitors. Daily maximum dry bulb, wet bulb, and heat index temperatures showed seasonal variation. In DLNMs, dry bulb temperature was not significantly associated with HRI. In contrast, higher wet bulb temperature was associated with increased HRI risk for both residents (RR = 1.60, 95% CI: 1.21-2.12) and visitors (RR = 2.54, 95% CI: 1.66-3.90), and higher heat index was also associated with increased risk for residents (RR = 2.13, 95% CI: 1.36-3.34) and visitors (RR = 2.68, 95% CI: 1.33-5.41).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: HRIs in Honolulu County were strongly associated with heat metrics that incorporate humidity. Consistent with previous studies, these results highlight the importance of accounting for both temperature and humidity when assessing the risk of heat stress, as humidity-inclusive metrics may better guide heat-related public health prevention and preparedness efforts in humid climates such as Hawai'i. Because meteorological exposures were derived from a single monitoring station representing county level conditions, these findings should be interpreted at the county level and may not fully capture localized microclimatic variability across O'ahu.

articles.title: Using capnography to differentiate airway from gastrointestinal placement of nasogastric tubes: a prospective multicentre diagnostic accuracy study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Patient safety incident reports and case reports have repeatedly highlighted factors contributing to inadvertent airway placement of nasogastric tubes, including misleading pH readings, insufficiently documented placement checks, and misinterpretation of radiographs. The study aimed to: (i) evaluate the diagnostic performance of capnography compared with radiography for detecting inadvertent airway placement of nasogastric tubes; and (ii) estimate the average cost incurred when radiography is used alone versus when capnography is used in conjunction with radiography.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A multicentre, prospective, observational diagnostic study was conducted. The diagnostic accuracy of capnography was examined using three end-tidal carbon dioxide thresholds (> 5 mmHg, > 10 mmHg, > 15 mmHg), with radiographic confirmation as the reference standard. For each threshold, true positives, false negatives, true negatives, and false positives were determined. Cost savings per patient were estimated using a bias-corrected and accelerated bootstrapping method with 20,000 replications.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 508 participants were recruited from 39 study sites across 21 hospitals, including medical or geriatric wards, intensive care units, and emergency departments. Most participants (n = 485; 95.5%) had end-tidal carbon dioxide readings ≤ 5 mmHg. Radiography confirmed correct gastric placement in 452 cases (89.0%), with one case (0.2%) of inadvertent airway placement. Estimated cost savings per patient, were HK$210.3, HK$214.5, and HK$217.5 for the three respective end-tidal carbon dioxide thresholds, based on a hypothetical strategy in which radiographic confirmation was performed only when the end-tidal carbon dioxide value exceeded a predefined threshold, compared with a radiography-only strategy in which all patients underwent radiographic confirmation of nasogastric tube placement.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Given the favourable outcomes and the simplicity of capnography measurement, capnography can be considered a first-line tool for excluding airway placement of nasogastric tubes, used alongside pH testing of aspirates.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: ClinicalTrials.gov, Number NCT05817864 (Registration date: 18 April 2023).

articles.title: Nationwide pediatric injury surveillance across two successive system disruptions in South Korea, 2016-2024.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Long-term trends in emergency department (ED)-based pediatric injury surveillance during and after the COVID-19 pandemic remain poorly characterized, particularly in settings that experienced additional system-level disruption. In February 2024, South Korea experienced a second healthcare-system disruption following the mass resignation of trainee physicians from teaching hospitals after a government decision to expand medical school admissions.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We analyzed National Emergency Department Information System data for children aged under 10 years with injury diagnoses (S00-T79) or external cause codes (V01-Y98), January 2016 to December 2024 (108 months). Monthly ED-recorded injury visit rates were calculated using resident-registration pediatric population denominators. Interrupted time-series analysis used two prespecified breakpoints (COVID-19 onset, March 2020; mass resignation of trainee physicians, February 2024). Recovery Indices compared 2023 with 2018-2019, stratified by resource intensity (KTAS 1-2, ICU, death, or transfer-in) and facility type.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 2,783,933 pediatric injury-related ED visits over 9 years, population-adjusted injury contact burden remained incompletely recovered by 2023 (Recovery Index 78.7% after adjusting for a 20.3% pediatric population decline; raw Recovery Index 62.7%), with the transfer-excluded resource-intensity group recovering more completely than the non-resource group (Recovery Index 76.2% vs. 62.3%), suggesting a post-COVID shift in the recorded ED case mix. Regional emergency centers recovered most by 2023 (71.5%) but showed the largest decline at the February 2024 breakpoint (β=-88.7 per 100,000), while non-teaching facilities showed no detectable change (β=+2.4). The level change at the February 2024 breakpoint was - 157.9 per 100,000 (95% CI - 223.7 to - 92.0), against - 183.3 (95% CI - 220.2 to - 146.5) at COVID-19 onset.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: ED-recorded pediatric injury contacts in South Korea remained below pre-pandemic levels, while the recorded case mix showed a relative shift toward more resource-intensive presentations. The 2024 trainee-physician workforce disruption was associated with a second, facility-selective decline that was largest in regional emergency centers and not detectable in other emergency facilities; with 11 months of follow-up these estimates are preliminary. These findings show that pediatric injury surveillance during healthcare-system disruption should not rely on visit counts alone; case mix and facility-tier distribution are needed to interpret ED-recorded injury trends.

articles.title: Fibrinogen Early In Severe Trauma studY II (FEISTY II): study protocol for a randomised clinical trial of fibrinogen concentrate vs cryoprecipitate in traumatic haemorrhage in Australia and New Zealand.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Haemorrhage is a leading cause of preventable death amongst severe trauma patients and is often complicated by hypofibrinogenaemia. Fibrinogen replacement can be achieved using fibrinogen concentrate (FC) or Cryoprecipitate (Cryo), but comparative evidence in traumatic haemorrhage is limited.

abstract.label: PRIMARY OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To determine, in trauma patients with major haemorrhage and hypofibrinogenaemia, whether fibrinogen replacement using FC compared to Cryo increases the number of days alive and out of hospital (at home) within the first 90 days after randomisation (DAOH90).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The Fibrinogen Early In Severe Trauma studY II (FEISTY II) is a phase III, multi-centre, randomised, two-arm parallel, open-label, superiority trial comparing FC and Cryo for fibrinogen replacement in severely injured trauma patients with major haemorrhage and hypofibrinogenaemia. Inclusion criteria are adults (≥ 18 years) affected by trauma and judged to have significant active haemorrhage with FIBTEM A5 ≤ 10 mm, TEG FF A10 ≤ 15 mm or FibC ≤ 2 g/L, for whom the local Major Haemorrhage Protocol (MHP) has been activated and/or emergency blood products have been transfused. Exclusion criteria are injuries judged incompatible with survival, inability to randomise within 6 h of trauma centre admission, pregnancy, objection to blood products, genetic or acquired coagulation disorder, dedicated fibrinogen replacement prior to randomisation, participation in competing study, and pre-existing co-morbidity that may interfere with the assessment of outcome. Patients will be block randomised 1:1 and stratified by site and clinical suspicion of Traumatic Brain Injury. The primary outcome is DAOH90. Secondary outcomes include all-cause mortality, transfusion requirements and measures of functional recovery and quality of life. Safety data will include symptomatic deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE), myocardial infarction (MI), ischaemic stroke and transfusion reactions. A total of 900 patients will be recruited by trauma centre clinical staff across 23 trauma centres in Australia and New Zealand.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: The optimal approach to fibrinogen replacement in traumatic haemorrhage remains uncertain. FEISTY II is a multi-centre randomised clinical trial in severely injured bleeding trauma patients, comparing FC to Cryo in terms of efficacy, safety, and cost-effectiveness.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: ClinicalTrials.gov. NCT05449834 . Registered on 08 July 2022. 1st Participant enrolled 21 November 2022.

articles.title: A rare case of endobronchial carcinoid causing recurrent pneumothorax: a case report.

abstract.text: Endobronchial carcinoid tumor rarely causes secondary spontaneous pneumothorax. We report a female in her 30s who reported progressive decline in her overall exercise tolerance with dyspnea on exertion and frequent upper respiratory infections (URIs) for 2 years presented for persistent spontaneous pneumothorax (SP). Initially, she presented to the emergency department (ED) for concerns of cough with mild hemoptysis and congestion for 2 weeks. She was found to have a small left-sided pneumothorax. She was admitted and treated for community-acquired pneumonia (CAP). Post-hospital follow-up showed a persistent pneumothorax unchanged in size. She was followed for weeks with serial chest X-rays, which later showed an increased size of the pneumothorax. She was admitted, and a chest tube was placed. Later, bronchoscopy was done, which showed near complete occlusion of the left mainstem bronchus by an endobronchial lesion. Pathology results showed a well-differentiated neuroendocrine grade 1 tumor consistent with carcinoid. She was successfully treated with tumor resection and photodynamic therapy (PDT). This case highlighted an unusual presentation of an endobronchial carcinoid tumor that requires further diagnostic workup with appropriate intervention.

articles.title: Case report of rare complication: unilateral chest wall hematoma after intracranial aneurysm embolization.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Unilateral chest wall hematoma is a rare but life-threatening cause of shock following endovascular procedures. We report a case of refractory hypotension and unilateral chest wall swelling in the post-anesthesia care unit, which was initially suspected to be a tension pneumothorax but was ultimately diagnosed as a contained chest wall hematoma.

abstract.label: CASE PRESENTATION
abstract.text: An 81-year-old male patient developed refractory hypotension and right chest wall swelling 15 min post-procedure. Initial bedside eFAST examination showed no pleural effusion, pneumothorax, or pericardial effusion. Cardiac ultrasound revealed normal wall motion, making myocardial infarction less likely. Physical examination revealed a rock-hard, high-tension mass in the chest wall. Emergency CT and ultrasound confirmed a massive intermuscular hematoma in the right chest wall.

abstract.label: OUTCOME
abstract.text: The patient received aggressive fluid resuscitation, blood transfusion, and compressive bandaging therapy. Angiography showed no active extravasation. The patient's hemodynamics stabilized within 24 h, and the hematoma gradually absorbed over the subsequent days.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Chest wall hematoma should be considered in the differential diagnosis of postprocedural shock, particularly when eFAST is negative. Physical examination and palpation are critical for identifying a localized tense mass, and prompt CT imaging is key to avoiding misdiagnosis as tension pneumothorax and ensuring correct treatment.

articles.title: Predictors of vaso-occlusive crisis-related emergency department encounters in children with sickle cell disease in Western French Guiana.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Vaso-occlusive crises (VOCs) are a major cause of emergency department (ED) utilization in children with sickle cell disease (SCD). In Western French Guiana, recurrent VOC-related ED encounters may reflect both disease severity and barriers to longitudinal preventive care.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective observational study using routine-care data from children with SCD who had at least one VOC-related ED encounter during a standardized 12-month observation period. The dataset contained 235 VOC-related ED encounters corresponding to 105 unique patient identifiers. To address repeated records, descriptive analyses are presented both at encounter level and at patient level. The primary multivariable analysis used unique patients as the unit of analysis; the outcome was the number of VOC-related ED encounters per unique patient identifier. Negative binomial regression was used for the count outcome. Recurrent ED use was defined as ≥ 4 VOC-related ED encounters per year.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The 235 ED encounters corresponded to 105 unique patient identifiers. At the patient level, median age was 8 years [IQR: 6.5-11], n = 56 (53.3%) were female, and n = 80 (76.2%) had SS genotype. The median number of VOC-related ED encounters per unique patient was 2 [IQR: 1-3], and n = 19 (18.1%) had ≥ 4 VOC-related ED encounters/year. In the patient-level multivariable model, ferritin was not independently associated with ED encounter burden (adjusted incidence rate ratio [IRR]: 0.96; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.84-1.08; p = 0.474). Rural residence, irregular hydroxyurea observance, regular follow-up, asthma, and dry season showed associations with encounter burden; however, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because the study included only children with at least one ED encounter and did not include children with zero VOC-related ED visits.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In this high-burden pediatric SCD cohort from Western French Guiana, no single biological or treatment variable reliably explained recurrent VOC-related ED utilization. The patient-level analysis no longer supports ferritin as an actionable independent predictor. Recurrent ED use likely reflects a combination of disease severity, rurality, healthcare access, and continuity-of-care factors. Prospective studies including the full followed SCD population, including children with zero ED visits, are needed.

abstract.label: CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER
abstract.text: Not applicable.

articles.title: From professional competence to coordinated field functioning: a qualitative study of disaster response readiness among members of disaster-deployable emergency medical teams in China.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Disaster response readiness is essential to the effective deployment of emergency medical teams (EMTs). In this study, EMTs refer to multidisciplinary, disaster-deployable medical units supporting health services during major emergencies, outbreaks, and disasters, rather than routine local or regional prehospital EMS, including paramedic- or ambulance-based teams providing day-to-day emergency response, transport, and initial stabilisation. As readiness is commonly framed in terms of competencies, training completion, or deployability, this study explored how EMT members understood disaster response readiness and the core dimensions they associated with it.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A qualitative descriptive study was conducted in Sichuan Province, China, with members of three national disaster-deployable emergency medical teams. Data were collected through two sequential phases of semi-structured, face-to-face, in-depth interviews. In Phase 1, 29 EMT members were interviewed. In Phase 2, 9 of these participants took part in supplementary interviews to clarify and deepen issues emerging from the preliminary analysis. Interview data were analysed using thematic analysis, with the two phases interpreted sequentially and then integrated.

abstract.label: FINDINGS
abstract.text: Participants understood disaster response readiness not as a fixed inventory of competencies, but as an enacted and context-dependent capacity to function effectively in disaster settings. Four interrelated themes were identified: (1) professional competence is an essential foundation, but not readiness itself; (2) readiness requires reorientation from hospital practice to disaster-task functioning; (3) readiness is shown by sustained functioning under pressure, uncertainty, and risk; and (4) readiness is enacted collectively through teams, leadership, and organisational support. Across participant roles, differences lay mainly in emphasis: clinical participants more often highlighted triage, adaptation of care, and functional endurance, whereas leadership, logistical, and administrative participants placed greater emphasis on coordination, operational order, and enabling support systems.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: From the perspective of members of disaster-deployable EMTs, disaster response readiness is better understood as coordinated field functioning rather than competence possession alone. Readiness is enacted through the interaction of individual capability, disaster-task adaptation, sustained functioning, and team and organisational support. These findings may inform EMT training, drills, readiness assessment, and capability development by encouraging greater attention to how readiness is operationalised in practice.

abstract.label: CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER
abstract.text: Not applicable.

articles.title: Understanding Australian health professionals' knowledge of concussion: a cross-sectional nationwide survey.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Concussion is a common condition following head injury affecting people across the lifespan. The purpose of this study was to understand the current state of concussion knowledge held by Australian health professionals, namely medical, nursing and allied health professionals. The primary aim was to establish health professionals' knowledge of concussion, specifically its: (i) mechanisms of injury; (ii) symptoms; (iii) management; (iv) differential diagnosis; (v) consequences; and vi) to determine the current frequency and type of care provided to concussion patients.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: An electronic survey was conducted. Participants included Australian health professionals who had worked in a professional capacity in the last 12-months. Convenience sampling was used for nationwide data collection over a 9-month period disseminated via email (e.g. through professional associations) and social media, allowing for snowballing. Quantitative methods of analysis were primarily adopted, supplemented by qualitative content analysis for free text responses.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: There were 126 participants (survey completion rate, 58%), who were most frequently female (n = 98/126, 78%), had more than 10 years of health professional experience (n = 88/126, 69%), and were aged between 30 and 39 years (n = 38/126, 30%). Participants were physiotherapists (n = 39/126, 31%), occupational therapists (n = 23/126, 18%), nurses (n = 17/126, 14%), medical professionals (including General Practitioners (GPs), physicians) (n = 13/126, 10%) and other health professionals (n = 20/126, 16%). Most participants correctly identified concussion injury mechanisms (n = 85/126, 68%); few participants correctly identified all concussion symptoms (n = 30/126, 24%); half the participants indicated they would frequently rely on published concussion management guidelines to inform practice (n = 65/126, 52%); differential diagnoses was considered by health professionals to varying degrees (e.g. intracranial injury (n = 57/64, 89%), and only some health professionals reported knowledge of persistent post-concussion symptoms (n = 78/126, 62%). The frequency and type of care provided to patients with concussion varied, but most frequently involved weekly (n = 25/66), or monthly (n = 10/66, 15%) reviews/treatment, with onward referral to Emergency Medicine Specialists being frequent for diagnosis of concussion (n = 11/17, 65%), and to a GP for treatment within 3 months (n = 7/18, 39%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: While most Australian health professionals understand the mechanisms of injury for concussion, a gap exists regarding concussion symptoms, differential diagnoses, consequences and management. These gaps form a framework for future targeted education opportunities for health professionals who provide care to patients with a suspected or actual concussion.

articles.title: Non-urgent emergency department utilization in adults: a systematic review of associated factors across diverse health systems.
articles.journal: Scand J Trauma Resusc Emerg Med
articles.journal_full: Scandinavian journal of trauma, resuscitation and emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Non-urgent emergency department (ED) visits represent a growing global challenge with significant economic and operational consequences. Despite previous reviews, important gaps remain. No review has included all commonly used terms for non-urgent ED visits, recent evidence has not been synthesised, and factors related to patients, health systems, and care contexts have rarely been examined together. This systematic review aimed to identify and categorize factors associated with non-urgent ED visits in adults.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science for articles published between January 2015 and May 2026. We included cross-sectional, cohort, and case-control studies that compared urgent and non-urgent ED visits and reported at least one associated factor. Quality assessment was performed using Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) checklists. Because of substantial heterogeneity in definitions, the findings were synthesised narratively.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Thirty-two studies from 21 countries were included. The proportion of non-urgent visits ranged from 1% to 82.4%, depending on the definition and measurement approach used. Five approaches were used to define non-urgent visits. The most common were triage-based (41%) and clinical judgment-based (28%). Associated factors were classified into three main categories: (1) demographic and socioeconomic (younger age, female sex, low income, lower education, non-native nationality); (2) access and health system (self-referral, arrival on foot, weekend visits, shorter distance to ED, lack of a family physician, public insurance); and (3) clinical and perceptual (non-specific diagnosis, musculoskeletal problems, mental health conditions, prior ED visit history, and patient perception of illness severity). The strongest associations were reported for frequent previous ED visits (aOR up to 82.13) and patients who perceived their illness as non-serious (aOR up to 21.03).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Non-urgent ED visits are influenced by multiple individual, health system, and perceptual factors. The substantial heterogeneity in definitional approaches underscores the need for conceptual standardization. No single intervention is likely to reduce non-urgent ED visits. Effective strategies should strengthen primary care, improve insurance policies, increase public health education, and empower patients.

articles.title: Joint high level of low-density lipoprotein and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein are associated with early neurological deterioration after thrombolysis in patients with mild stroke.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Low-density lipoprotein (LDL) and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) play important roles in cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases through pathways such as inflammation and oxidative stress. We aimed to explore whether LDL and hs-CRP were associated with early neurological outcome after thrombolysis in patients with mild stroke.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We studied patients with mild stroke who received intravenous alteplase at the emergency department from April 1, 2017 to April 1, 2024. LDL and hs-CRP levels were measured after thrombolysis through the first blood draw after emergency admission to the neurology department. Patients were divided into 4 groups according to different combinations of LDL (LDL ≤ 3.16 mmol/L, LDL > 3.16 mmol/L) and hs-CRP (hs-CRP ≤ 5 mg/L, hs-CRP > 5 mg/L) levels. Early neurological deterioration (END) was defined as an increase of 2 or more points in NIHSS score at 24 h of thrombolysis. Logistic regression was used to investigate the association of LDL and hs-CRP with early neurological deterioration after thrombolysis in patients with mild stroke. We conducted subgroup analyses based on the following variables: gender, age, NIHSS score at admission, TOAST type, and DWI-defined cerebral infarction area after adjusting for confounding factors. In addition, We conducted three sensitivity analyses by changing the cutoff values of LDL and hs-CRP to enhance the robustness of the findings. This observational study was reported in accordance with the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) statement.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 625 patients (410 men; mean age, 68 (58, 76) years) included in this study, 80 (13%) had early neurological deterioration. Compared with patients with LDL ≤ 3.16 mmol/L, hs-CRP ≤ 5 mg/L, Mild stroke patients with LDL > 3.16 mmol/L and hs-CRP > 5 mg/L had an increased risk of early neurological deterioration (OR, 3.62 [95% CI, 1.49-8.19]) after thrombolysis, and this association persisted after adjustment for confounders (OR, 2.98 [95% CI, 1.11-7.63]).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Joint high levels of LDL and hs-CRP were associated with early neurological deterioration after thrombolysis in patients with mild stroke. It can help neurologists better assess the treatment outcomes of patients with mild strokes after thrombolysis. Preparations can be made for remedial measures in the early stages.

articles.title: Association of sodium bicarbonate use during CPR with sustained return of spontaneous circulation in adult in-hospital cardiac arrest.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Sodium bicarbonate (SB) is frequently administered during cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) despite contemporary guidelines advising against routine use. Observational evaluation is challenging because SB is often given later in resuscitations, creating confounding by indication and resuscitation-time bias. We assessed the association between SB administration during CPR and sustained return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We performed a retrospective cohort study of adult (≥ 18 years) in-hospital cardiac arrests from January 1, 2020, to January 2, 2025, at a single academic hospital (~ 1,000 beds). Arrests were documented in real time on standardized Code Blue forms with stopwatch timestamps and supplemented with electronic medical record data. The primary outcome was sustained ROSC (≥ 20 min). Crude associations were estimated using risk difference (RD), risk ratio (RR), and odds ratio (OR). To account for time-varying confounding, we implemented a marginal structural model (MSM) with stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting using discrete 2-minute intervals from CPR initiation to sustained ROSC or termination. SB was modeled as a time-varying initiation exposure.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 1,301 events, 1,298 were included after excluding 3 with missing exposure/outcome. SB was administered in 565/1,298 (43.5%) cases; sustained ROSC occurred in 803/1,298 (61.9%) overall. In crude analysis, sustained ROSC occurred in 304/565 (53.8%) SB-exposed versus 499/733 (68.1%) unexposed cases (RD - 14.3%, 95% CI - 19.6 to - 9.0; OR 0.55, 95% CI 0.44-0.69; p < 0.0001). In the weighted MSM, SB initiation was not associated with higher sustained ROSC (aRR 0.98, 95% CI 0.91-1.06; marginal risk difference - 1.2%, 95% CI - 4.7 to + 2.3). Exploratory timing and 15-minute landmark analyses did not identify a clear administration window associated with higher sustained ROSC.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this cohort, SB use during CPR was associated with lower sustained ROSC in crude analyses, but the association attenuated toward the null after adjustment for measured time-varying confounding. Exploratory analyses did not identify a clear timing-dependent association between SB initiation and sustained ROSC. Because downstream outcomes and specific guideline-supported indications were incompletely captured, these findings should be interpreted as limited to sustained ROSC in an unselected in-hospital cardiac arrest cohort.

articles.title: Hyperbaric exposure in rodents with non-invasive imaging assessment of decompression bubbles: a scoping review.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Decompression sickness (DCS) is the primary hazard for undersea commercial and military operations, and a factor for astronauts during decompression for extra-vehicular activity in space, but a reliable biomarker for predicting DCS remains to be identified. This scoping review investigated imaging modalities previously used for estimating decompression stress and detecting bubbles in rodents after hyperbaric exposure.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Search methods were established under the Joanna Brigg's Institute Scoping Review Framework and Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta Analyses. Two independent reviewers considered each study for inclusion, with a third available for settling disputes. Eligible publications met the following requirements (1): used a rodent test subject for (2) hyperbaric exposure to simulate a dive profile and (3) implemented an imaging modality for post-dive evaluation of decompression bubble presence. An exposure factor was calculated for each publication, that included sufficient procedure methodology, using an established Mixed-Gas Model or pressure-time based index and the relationship was compared with the post-dive bubble presence.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Ultrasound was the most common modality utilized post-dive, except for 6 publications using either magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), positron emission tomography (PET), or computed tomography (CT).
