Venous gas emboli (VGE) detected using echocardiography was regularly used to assess the severity of the exposure. Massive bubble presence post-dive typically corresponded with fatal DCS. Several factors have been identified for relationship to VGE including body weight, temperature, and exercise. Recent publications using MRI and PET have presented novel approaches for detecting bubble formation and monitoring inert gas kinetics, respectively. A mixed-gas model previously proposed for calculating the risk of DCS for a given dive profile was found to underestimate the true experimental result, yet performed better than a pressure-time approach.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This scoping review summarizes the imaging modalities that have been used in past rodent studies with DCS and discusses the relationship between VGE and post-dive mortality in small animals. Future reports should include sufficient information for repeatability including imaging settings, example views of the imaged area, and a complete list of VGE grades (if collected). Additional work is needed to confirm safe thresholds for ultrasound imaging of decompression bubbles, and for the development of other modalities in the decompression context including MRI, PET, and bioelectrical impedance.

articles.title: Development and internal validation of an interpretable machine-learning model for predicting sepsis within 48 hours after admission in emergency-admitted patients with pulmonary infection.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To develop and internally validate a machine-learning model using routinely available early clinical variables to predict clinically documented sepsis within 48 h after admission among patients with pulmonary infection in a single-center development-only setting.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Adult patients with pulmonary infection admitted through the Department of Emergency Internal Medicine of Ningde Municipal Hospital between December 2021 and December 2025 were retrospectively included. The primary outcome was clinically documented sepsis within 48 h after admission, adjudicated retrospectively using a clinical-record-based Sepsis-3 conceptual framework. Patients were randomly divided into training and validation sets at a 7:3 ratio. Predictors were selected using LASSO regression and bidirectional stepwise logistic regression based on the Akaike information criterion. Six models were developed using the same predictor set: logistic regression, random forest, support vector machine, neural network, gradient boosting machine, and XGBoost. Model performance was assessed using discrimination, calibration, decision curve analysis, bootstrap confidence intervals, DeLong testing, bootstrap 0.632+ optimism correction, threshold sensitivity analyses, class-imbalance sensitivity analyses, and supplementary comparisons with NEWS/NEWS2, MEWS, and SIRS. Model-agnostic SHAP was used to interpret the selected SVM model.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 425 patients were included, of whom 106 (24.94%) developed clinically documented sepsis within 48 h. The final model included Glasgow Coma Scale score, respiratory rate, systolic blood pressure, procalcitonin, C-reactive protein, and lactate. In the validation set, SVM achieved an AUC of 0.869 (95% CI, 0.805-0.933), with sensitivity of 0.812, specificity of 0.760, PPV of 0.531, NPV of 0.924, and F1 score of 0.642. LR showed similar sensitivity and discrimination, with an AUC of 0.872 (95% CI, 0.808-0.937), sensitivity of 0.812, specificity of 0.771, PPV of 0.542, NPV of 0.925, and F1 score of 0.650. XGBoost achieved the numerically highest AUC of 0.879 (95% CI, 0.819-0.939), but had lower sensitivity of 0.625. Pairwise DeLong testing showed no significant AUC difference between SVM and LR or XGBoost. Model-agnostic SHAP analysis of the SVM model identified lactate, procalcitonin, Glasgow Coma Scale score, respiratory rate, C-reactive protein, and systolic blood pressure as contributors to model output.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this single-center development-only study, SVM based on six routinely available early variables showed a sensitivity-favorable profile for identifying patients with pulmonary infection at risk of clinically documented sepsis within 48 h after admission. LR provided a transparent nomogram-based statistical reference, whereas XGBoost showed higher specificity but lower sensitivity. These models may support early risk stratification and focused monitoring in conjunction with standardized early warning scores and clinical judgment, but they cannot be used as stand-alone rule-out tools or deployed clinically without external validation and prospective evaluation.

articles.title: From XR-derived performance metrics to an objective performance score in point-of-care ultrasound.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) quality depends on operator proficiency. As POCUS training expands, scalable approaches to performance evaluation are needed. Current performance evaluation relies largely on examiner-intensive Objective Structured Clinical Examinations (OSCE). Extended Reality (XR) technologies offer opportunities to capture objective performance metrics and provide the digitization needed to support automated and standardised performance evaluations. The objective of this study was to explore the use of XR-derived performance metrics and examine how an automated performance score using these metrics relates to OSCE performance.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Medical students (novices), physicians with limited ultrasound experience (intermediates), and experienced physicians and sonographers (experts) performed a cardiac ultrasound task on a phantom, while using a phone as a probe and wearing a HoloLens that immerses them in an XR environment. They were tasked to obtain four cardiac POCUS views. OSCE was scored by two independent experts. Probe trajectories were derived from the phone and were used to extract kinematic metrics, such as time, path length, straightness index, and dimensionless squared jerk. These were complemented with image quality surrogates (position and angle deviation), and gaze behaviour (gaze shifts to the display). A metric-based performance score was constructed using multivariable regression and compared with OSCE scores.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Ninety participants were included (34 novices, 31 intermediates, 25 experts). The OSCE scoring demonstrated excellent inter-rater reliability (ICC 0.97) and clear discrimination across experience levels. Kinematic and gaze metrics aligned with experience level and OSCE performance, whereas image quality surrogates showed weaker associations. Factor analysis of the XR-derived performance metrics identified two underlying domains of technical performance; probe handling and image quality, with gaze behaviour emerging as a distinct construct. The automated performance score showed a moderate to good correlation with OSCE performance (ρ = 0.69). Replacing XR-derived image quality surrogates with expert-rated image quality substantially improved associations (ρ = 0.91).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: XR-derived, automated performance scoring represents a promising, scalable approach for formative feedback and early-stage screening, particularly in novice learners, while reducing examiner burden. These findings lay the foundation for further development toward fully automated ultrasound performance tracking. Further validation is required before use in high-stakes or fully automated assessment.

articles.title: Implementation and early operational evaluation of a National Pediatric Triage System in a Referral Hospital in Beira, Mozambique: a one-year implementation study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Pediatric mortality in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) remains largely attributable to time-sensitive and treatable conditions. Structured triage systems are essential to prioritize care and reduce preventable deaths, yet implementation evidence in LMIC referral hospitals is limited.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: This study aimed to describe the implementation of a newly developed national triage tool in the Pediatric Emergency Department (PED) in a referral hospital in Beira, Mozambique, and evaluate its early operational integration using implementation outcomes over the first year of practice.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a multi-component implementation of the triage tool between October 2023 and January 2026. A retrospective observational analysis evaluated implementation outcomes between April 2024 and March 2025.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 28,469 pediatric visits, 76.3% underwent documented triage. Uptake varied over time, with lower adherence on weekends than weekdays (62.8% vs 80.1%), during night versus morning shifts (70.0% vs 90.3%), in September 2024 (56.6%) and March 2025 (59.1%) coinciding with understaffed shifts and workforce instability. Adherence to data recording improved over time, from an average of 36.7% missing data in April 2024 to 17% in March 2025. Among triaged patients, 83% were classified as non-urgent and 17% as urgent. Overall, 86.9% were discharged, 12.3% hospitalized, 0.7% required intensive care admission, and 0.1% died in the PED.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Pediatric triage system implementation was feasible in a resource-constrained referral hospital, although sustainability was mainly influenced by workforce instability. Dedicated training, workflow redesign, institutional ownership, and continuous monitoring emerged as key implementation strategies that may inform future scale-up across similar LMIC settings.

articles.title: Prehospital endotracheal intubation and return of spontaneous circulation in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest patients: a retrospective cohort study based on prehospital emergency registry data.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The optimal airway strategy during out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) remains uncertain. This study investigated the association between prehospital endotracheal intubation (ETI) and return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) using a regional emergency medical services registry.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective cohort study analyzed 6,162 adult non-traumatic OHCA patients treated by emergency medical services between October 2023 and November 2024. Patients were categorized into an ETI group (n = 1,448) and a basic airway (BA) group (n = 4,714). The primary outcome was prehospital ROSC. Long-term survival and neurological outcomes were not available in the registry. Multivariable logistic regression and propensity score-matched sensitivity analysis were used to evaluate the association between ETI and ROSC while accounting for measured confounders. Airway strategy was selected by on-scene physicians during routine EMS care, and rhythm-stratified unadjusted analyses were performed to describe whether the ETI-ROSC association differed by initial rhythm category.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: ROSC occurred more frequently in the ETI group than in the BA group (21.1% vs. 3.8%, P < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, ETI was strongly associated with ROSC (OR = 7.61, 95% CI: 6.07-9.53, P < 0.001). Shockable initial rhythm (OR = 5.42, 95% CI: 3.80-7.74, P < 0.001) and defibrillation (OR = 1.82, 95% CI: 1.37-2.42, P < 0.001) were also positively associated with ROSC, whereas longer response time and epinephrine administration were negatively associated with ROSC. In 1:1 propensity score-matched analysis, the association between ETI and ROSC remained significant (OR = 6.33, 95% CI: 4.72-8.47, P < 0.001). Rhythm-stratified analyses showed that the unadjusted association was strongest in non-shockable and other/unknown rhythm strata and was not statistically significant in the shockable rhythm stratum.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this retrospective prehospital registry cohort, ETI during OHCA resuscitation was strongly associated with higher ROSC rates. Because airway timing relative to collapse and ROSC, survival to discharge, and neurological outcomes were not captured, these findings should be interpreted as an association with immediate resuscitation success rather than evidence of a causal survival benefit. The observed association may also reflect physician selection of airway strategy and other unmeasured resuscitation factors, and should therefore be considered hypothesis-generating.

abstract.label: CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER
abstract.text: Not applicable.

articles.title: Laparoscopic approach for emergency colon resection: a retrospective propensity score-matched study.
articles.journal_full: World journal of emergency surgery : WJES

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Despite its routine use in elective procedures, the role of laparoscopy in emergency colorectal surgery remains debated due to limited evidence. This study compared laparoscopic and open surgery regarding complications, mortality, and hospital stay following emergency colon operations.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective study included adult patients treated at Päijät-Häme Central Hospital between 2010 and 2020 who underwent emergency colon resection. Propensity score matching was used to adjust for comorbidities, prior ICU admission, surgical indication, and contamination between laparoscopic and open surgery groups.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: All together 484 patients had an emergency colorectal resection of which 85 (17.6%) were carried out laparoscopically, 31 (6.4%) were converted and 377 (76.0%) were open. In the whole cohort, Comprehensive complication index was lower among laparoscopy patients than open surgery patients if intraoperative conversion to open surgery was avoided (25.8 vs. 34.9, p = 0.012). The subgroup analysis also showed lower CCI after laparoscopic resection for patients presented with obstruction (21.3 vs. 29.7, p = 0.046) or colorectal cancer (21.1 vs. 29.4, p = 0.020) A multivariable regression analysis also showed that starting the procedure laparoscopically predicted lower complication rates. Patients who had a laparoscopic resection also had shorter hospital stay (9.0 vs. 12.9 days, p < 0.001). Patients with open surgery had significantly more wound complications (10.3% vs. 1.2%, p = 0.010). Open surgery was also an independent risk factor for higher CCI (p = 0.008) and the need for intensive care (p = 0.027). Mortality was similar regardless of the approach in short term (30 days, p = 0.810; 90 days, p = 0.354) and in long-term survival (p = 0.466).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The laparoscopic technique in colorectal emergencies may offer similar benefits as in elective surgery, with a lower burden of total complications, less wound complications and shorter hospital stay. Laparoscopy was not associated with any unexpected harmful events.

articles.title: Parental satisfaction with pediatric healthcare services is low in Eastern Ethiopia.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Parental satisfaction is crucial for evaluating pediatric healthcare services, but there is a lack of data on satisfaction levels with inpatient services in the study setting. Therefore, this study aims to determine the level of parental satisfaction with pediatric inpatient healthcare services at Hiwot Fana Comprehensive Specialized Hospital in eastern Ethiopia.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A cross-sectional study was conducted at Hiwot Fana Comprehensive Specialized Hospital (HFCSH) involving 413 parents who had brought their children for pediatric inpatient services between February 1 and March 30, 2024. The participants were chosen through systematic random sampling with a K- interval of two. The parental level of satisfaction was measured using the EMPATHIC parent satisfaction tool. The analysis was conducted using SPSS version 27. Bivariate logistic regression was performed to assess the association of the outcome variable with the independent variable. The strength of association was determined by an AOR and a 95% confidence interval. Statistical significance was declared at a p-value < 0.05.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: This study included 413 parents, with a 100% response rate. The satisfaction level of parents was 61.5% (95% CI 56.6%, 66.0%). Factors significantly associated with parental satisfaction were having children aged 2 to 6 years (AOR = 1.671, 95% CI 1.01, 2.75), visiting pediatric emergency wards (AOR = 0.31, 95% CI: 0.18, 0.56), poor health status (AOR = 0.479, 95% CI: 0.29, 0.79), moderate social support (AOR = 2.06, 95% CI: 1.30, 3.75), and caring behavior of health professionals (AOR = 6.62, 95% CI: 4.01, 10.91).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This study revealed that the level of parental satisfaction with pediatric healthcare services was low. The study also identified modifiable factors that predicted parental satisfaction, including moderate social support, good health professional caring behavior, children in poor health, and inadequate services in the pediatric emergency unit.

articles.title: Investigation of the ability of JAM-A molecule to predict clinical outcome, mortality, and symptom onset in patients with acute stroke: a prospective observational single-center cohort study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: This study aimed to evaluate the relationship between serum JAM-A levels and both hospital survival and six-month mortality in patients with acute ischemic stroke. It also aimed to investigate the correlation with the time elapsed from symptom onset to event.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This prospective, single-center study included 70 patients presenting to the emergency department with a diagnosis of acute ischemic stroke. Serum JAM-A levels were measured in venous blood samples taken at admission. Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, vascular occlusion localization, ASPECT score, and treatment methods applied were evaluated.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of the patients included in the study, 53 (75%) survived after treatment, while a total of 21 patients died at six-month of follow-up, resulting in a mortality rate of 30%. The mean age was 68.14 ± 11.95 years, and the mean age, BUN level, and AST level were significantly higher in the deceased patient group compared to the surviving patients (P = 0.012, P = 0.022, and P = 0.041, respectively). Distal vessel occlusions were more frequent in surviving patients, and a significant association was found between the localization of the vessel occlusion and clinical outcome (P = 0.011). In multivariate analysis, age (OR = 0.94; 95% CI: 0.90-0.98; P = 0.006) and the presence of distal occlusion (OR = 5.02; 95% CI: 1.55-16.23; P = 0.008) were found to be independent predictors. No association was found between JAM-A level and six-month mortality (P = 0.883), and its discriminatory power was weak in ROC analysis (AUC = 0.49). No significant correlation was found between the time elapsed from symptom onset to event and the JAM-A score (Pearson r = - 0.18, P = 0.129; Spearman rho = - 0.02, P = 0.870).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Serum JAM-A levels were found not to be significant in predicting hospital survival and six-month mortality in patients with acute ischemic stroke. Advanced age and localization of vascular occlusion emerged as important determinants of prognosis.

articles.title: Constructing health meanings in blue spaces: a blue mind perspective on water-based leisure in Türkiye.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Although research on blue spaces has expanded considerably, existing studies have largely emphasized their restorative and therapeutic functions, offering limited insight into how individuals construct health-related meanings through water-based leisure experiences. Drawing on Blue Mind theory, which proposes that contact with water promotes psychological and emotional well-being, this study aimed to examine how individuals in Türkiye who regularly participate in water-based leisure activities interpret and construct their experiences in relation to psychological, cognitive, bodily, ecological, and social health dimensions.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This qualitative study was conducted with 10 participants from different regions of Türkiye who regularly engaged in a variety of water-based leisure activities, including sailing, surfing, scuba diving, fishing, camping, and stand-up paddleboarding. Participants were recruited using purposive criterion sampling. Data were collected through semi-structured online interviews conducted via Zoom between July and August 2025. Interview data were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using inductive content analysis following established qualitative analysis procedures. Coding and theme development were conducted independently by two researchers and refined through consensus discussions to enhance analytical credibility.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The analysis revealed five overarching themes: psychological regulation space, cognitive effects of the aquatic environment, reconstruction of perceived bodily competence, development of ecological sensitivity through proximity to water, and strengthening of social bonds. Participants described blue spaces as multifunctional experiential domains that facilitated emotional regulation, stress reduction, resilience, cognitive clarity, creativity, problem-solving, bodily awareness, perceptions of vitality and youthfulness, ecological responsibility, and social connectedness. Findings further demonstrated that water-based leisure experiences supported not only individual well-being but also identity reconstruction, environmental stewardship, and selective social withdrawal for psychological replenishment. Rather than functioning solely as passive restorative settings, blue spaces emerged as active relational contexts through which individuals negotiated meanings associated with health, selfhood, and social belonging.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The findings extend Blue Mind theory beyond restoration-oriented interpretations by conceptualizing water-based leisure as a multidimensional and culturally embedded process of meaning-making. Blue spaces appear to function as public health resources that support psychological, cognitive, physical, ecological, and social well-being. The study highlights the importance of developing accessible and sustainable water-based leisure opportunities that may contribute to holistic health promotion and environmental awareness in rapidly urbanizing societies.

articles.title: Near-fatal foreign body aspiration - bronchoscopic rescue by the "push-down manoeuvre" and retrieval under ECMO: a case report.

abstract.text: In this case report, we describe a child with a near-fatal foreign body aspiration rescued by a unique lifesaving endoscopic manoeuvre and transfer for foreign body retrieval to an extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) centre. A 2-year-5-month-old girl suffered a near-fatal foreign body aspiration at home and was successfully resuscitated by the paramedics. On arrival, she was severely dyspnoeic, hypercapnic and cyanotic, showed marked paradoxical breathing movements with hardly any breath sounds consistent with near-complete central airway obstruction. After induction of anaesthesia for emergency bronchoscopy, bag mask ventilation was nearly impossible resulting in a "cannot ventilate, cannot oxygenate" scenario and bradycardia. Only after successfully pushing down the foreign body into the right main bronchus (push-down manoeuvre) was mask ventilation successful. Any further manipulation led to severe desaturations and attempts to retrieve the foreign body were impossible. Therefore, transfer to the nearest centre with paediatric ECMO facilities via air ambulance was carried out. Foreign body retrieval was successful under veno-venous ECMO and the girl showed a complete recovery without any neurological sequelae. In this case of total airway obstruction, the bronchoscopic push-down manoeuvre was lifesaving and allowed temporary stabilisation to enable transport to a centre where secondary difficult foreign body retrieval was performed under ECMO.

articles.title: Coal phaseout undermines co-benefits of fly ash as a clinker substitute.

abstract.text: Replacing clinker with fly ash is a critical CO2 mitigation pathway for cement clinker plants (CCPs), yet this potential may be adversely affected by the phaseout of coal-fired power plants (CFPPs). Here, we draw upon a high-resolution infrastructure-level database encompassing approximately 4,460 CFPP units and 1,540 CCP production lines in China. Through industrial symbiosis simulations and cost-benefit analyses, we evaluate the mitigation performance and adaptation costs of CCPs under various future CFPP retirement and flexible dispatch pathways. Our findings indicate that CCPs could reduce CO2 emissions by 141 Mt and generate 8.2 billion Chinese Yuan (CNY) in economic benefits through clinker substitution with fly ash. However, under the 1.5°C warming target by 2050, the coal power phaseout would undermine these benefits by more than 80%. While deploying adaptation measures could offset 57 Mt of CO2 losses, these measures incur an additional 5 billion CNY in costs for CCPs, potentially turning net economic benefits into an estimated loss of 17 billion CNY. Developing systematic and collaborative decarbonization strategies for highly connected sectors is essential for mitigating transition risks and improving decision-making effectiveness.

articles.title: Approaching Machine Learning for Length of Stay Prediction in Sepsis Patients Presenting to the Emergency Department From 2014 to 2024.

abstract.text: Sepsis is a life-threatening presentation in the emergency department and is associated with poor clinical outcomes and emergency crowding due to prolonged length of stay (LOS). The current study outlines the LOS prediction in sepsis patients using machine learning methods with a decade-long analysis from 2014 to 2024. The study deployed four different classification algorithms for the prediction of LOS: Random Forest, Logistic Regression, Gradient Boosting, and XGBoost. All the models were evaluated through sensitivity, specificity, precision, F1 score, and area under the curve. The dataset was randomly split into a training set (70%) and a validation set (30%). A total of 13,858 adult patients (>18 years) were included in the study. A total of 14 key attributes were analyzed. No difference in the LOS was observed in the patients with age >60 or <60 years. Interestingly, there was an equal number of patients with sepsis in younger and older age groups. The Random Forest classifier best predicted both short and long LOS (sensitivity: 75.54%, specificity: 78.35%, and area under the curve: 94.5%). The external validation of the model yielded an overall accuracy of 80% and sensitivity and specificity of 68% and 91%, respectively. The model can be implemented for improving emergency department workflows and operational efficiency. Future studies with larger and more diverse datasets can further improve the model performance.

articles.title: Revamping Patient Transfers: A Comparative Assessment of Lean Readiness in Intensive Care and Postoperative Unit Admissions.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Efficient patient transfers between the operating room (OR), postoperative care units (POCUs), and general intensive care units (GICUs) are vital for ensuring patient safety and quality of care. Traditional methods of patient transfer are often inefficient, creating delays and potential risks. Lean methodologies, which focus on reducing waste and improving process efficiency, may offer solutions, but little is known about how ready current patient transfer and admission processes are for Lean implementation.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To assess the Lean readiness of patient admission processes in the GICU and POCU, focusing on the value-added (VA) aspects of nursing practices, including time, cost, and effort during patient transfers.

abstract.label: METHOD
abstract.text: A descriptive comparative design was applied to observe 100 nurses during 100 patient admissions in the GICU and POCU at a single general university hospital in Egypt. Using a Lean-based observational checklist developed and psychometrically tested for this study, activities were timed, classified as VA or non-value-added (NVA), and compared between the two units. Lean was used as an assessment framework only; no Lean intervention was implemented.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 100 observed admissions (47 in GICU and 53 in POCU), the overall VA score was significantly higher in the GICU than that in the POCU (97.0 ± 2.4 vs. 95.9 ± 2.1; p = 0.037; effect size r = 0.21, small), with the largest difference for the use of a recognized assessment framework (VA score 89.6 ± 7.8 vs. 83.8 ± 2.4; p < 0.001; r = 0.41). Overall time, effort, and cost scores were also higher in the GICU, but the mean differences were small (2.1-4.6 points on a 0-100 scale). Effort for preparing to receive the patient differed significantly between units (p = 0.016; r = 0.24) although the means were similar (40.3 ± 6.0 in GICU vs. 39.6 ± 4.4 in POCU). Preparation for receiving patients ranked lowest on time, effort, and cost scores in both units. The average time spent per admission activity was 24.3 ± 21.2 min, with no significant difference between units (p = 0.528). These findings describe current admission practice and indicate where Lean-based improvement could be targeted; they do not show any effect of Lean.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Nursing practices during patient admissions differed modestly between the GICU and POCU: the GICU showed a higher VA contribution of structured assessment and higher overall time, effort, and cost scores, whereas the time in minutes was similar. Because no Lean intervention was implemented, the findings indicate partial Lean readiness and identify targets for future Lean-based improvement, the effect of which still needs to be tested.

abstract.label: IMPLICATIONS TO NURSING MANAGEMENT
abstract.text: A Lean-based assessment of admission workflows can help nurse managers identify NVA activities and set unit-specific priorities for improvement; the effect of subsequent Lean implementation on safety and efficiency needs to be evaluated.

articles.title: [Severe shrapnel cervical thoracic injury: emergency specialized surgical care (lessons on optimizing surgical care at the advanced stages of medical evacuation)].

abstract.text: The authors describe successful treatment of severe cervical thoracic wound with damage to the main vessels in advanced military field hospital (Role 3). Analytical review is based on this clinical case and rich experience of authors in surgical care for wounded in modern armed conflict. The subject of review was specifics of early specialized surgical care to the wounded within the concept of «Optimizing surgical care».

articles.title: Inflammatory cytokines as risk factor of septic shock in patients with sepsis.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Aim: To prove pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory cytokines as risk factors of septic shock in patients with sepsis.

abstract.label: PATIENTS AND METHODS
abstract.text: Materials and Methods: This study used a prospective observational study. The target population were sepsis patients who were admitted to the emergency room of Dr Kariadi Hospital. TNF-α, IL-6, IL-10, and IL-4 levels were examined using the ELISA method. Bivariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses as well as receiver operating characteristic curve analysis were used to predict septic shock.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Results: Patients with septic shock had higher levels of IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-10 compared to those with sepsis. Multivariate analysis results showed that IL-6 and IL-10 were independent risk factors for septic shock. IL-6 level ≥11.4 pg/ml had an OR of 7.02, CI 95% 1.78-27.70 (p = 0.005), and IL-10 level had an OR of 3.89, CI 95% 1.13-13.45 (p = 0.031), as risk factors for septic shock.shock.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Conclusions: IL-6 and IL-10 are risk factors of septic shock in sepsis. Meanwhile, TNF-α and IL-4 levels are not associated with shock in sepsis.

articles.title: Factors affecting the duration of hospitalization due to odontogenic abscesses in children.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The spread of an odontogenic abscess can have serious consequences and may result in severe morbidity or death. There is no consensus regarding the factors that may predict the length of hospital stay (LOHS) in children hospitalized for odontogenic abscesses.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: The aim of the study was to examine the factors affecting LOHS among children and adolescents who were hospitalized for surgical treatment of odontogenic abscesses.

abstract.label: MATERIAL AND METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective cohort study included children and adolescents aged 1-17 years who were admitted to the pediatric emergency department of the Scheneider Children's Medical Center of Israel between 2018 and 2022 for a dentoalveolar or odontogenic abscess.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In total, 127 patients (55.9% male) with a median age of 6 years were included. Dental caries was the most common odontogenic cause of abscess formation (72%). The median LOHS was 3 days (range: 2-8 days). The logistic regression analysis identified age, body temperature at admission, white blood cell (WBC) count at admission, and the year of admission as predictors of LOHS, explaining 44.9% of the model's variance. Sex, C-reactive protein (CRP) levels and neutrophil, monocyte and eosinophil counts were not significant predictors of LOHS in this patient population.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Age, body temperature at admission, WBC count at admission, and the year of admission were associated with LOHS in children and adolescents hospitalized for odontogenic abscesses.

articles.title: Infectious Flexor Tenosynovitis of the Lower Extremity: A Case Report.
articles.journal_full: Journal of education & teaching in emergency medicine

abstract.label: UNLABELLED
abstract.text: Infectious flexor tenosynovitis (IFT) of the lower extremity is rare but serious, requiring early recognition and aggressive management to prevent severe morbidity. Often associated with penetrating trauma or hematogenous spread, IFT can lead to devastating complications if not promptly identified and treated. A 57-year-old female with cirrhosis, diabetes mellitus, and hypertension presented to the emergency department with progressive right ankle pain, swelling, and systemic symptoms. Despite prior emergency visits, her condition worsened. Imaging revealed infectious tenosynovitis involving the flexor hallucis longus and flexor digitorum longus tendons, with concerning signs of soft tissue necrosis. She received broad-spectrum antibiotics and underwent emergent surgery, ultimately requiring a below-the-knee amputation due to extensive necrosis. Blood cultures confirmed group B Streptococcus as the pathogen. Her postoperative course was complicated by hepatic encephalopathy and hematochezia, necessitating multidisciplinary care. This case highlights the importance of early recognition of IFT, particularly in immunocompromised patients, and the role of imaging in diagnosing deep soft tissue infections. Delayed diagnosis can lead to severe outcomes, emphasizing the need for heightened clinical suspicion and timely intervention. Increased awareness and prompt management of IFT are crucial for improving patient outcomes and limb preservation.

abstract.label: TOPICS
abstract.text: Infectious flexor tenosynovitis, flexor hallucis longus, flexor digitorum longus, Emergency Department.

articles.title: Nutritional content and amino acid profile of edible insects (Lethocerus indicus, Dytiscus marginalis, and Odontotermes feae) consumed by ethnic communities of Assam, India.
articles.journal_full: Journal of food science and technology

abstract.label: UNLABELLED
abstract.text: Entomophagy is a common practice among ethnic communities of Assam, India. This study examines the nutritional composition of Lethocerus indicus (giant water bug, GW), Dytiscus marginalis (great diving beetle, GD), Odontotermes feae (termite). While previous analyses focused largely on proximate and mineral contents, amino acid profiling and molecular protein distribution of these insects are proposed first time. They are protein-rich sources, ranging from 28.875 to 16.712%, other nutrients (carbohydrates and lipids) and energy contents (874.638 ± 5.313 to 1634.001 ± 10.701 kJ/100 g). GD displayed the highest amino acid content, followed by Termite and GW. Abundant non-essential (NEAA) and essential amino acid (EAA) in all three insects were Proline and Lysine, respectively. However, only Termite fulfilled the FAO/WHO recommended standards of EAA as 40% and essential to NEAA ratio of 0.6. Leucine and Valine, respectively, are the limiting amino acids in all insects for all age groups. SDS-PAGE showed five protein fractions: actin-arginine kinase, cuticle proteins, heat shock proteins, hemocyanin, and myosin. Smeared bands < 20 kDa were absent, confirming negligible proteolysis. Further research is crucial to emphasize insects as future sustainable human and animal feed, thereby enhancing food security and boosting the insect industry.

abstract.label: SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION
abstract.text: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13197-025-06358-0.
